CheckPluginOptions.title: CheckPluginOptions (interface, sygnal/vite)
CheckPluginOptions.summary: sygnal-check in dev. A setting left out comes from the project's sygnal-check config file (`sygnal-check.config.json`, or the `"sygnal-check"` key in package.json; its `paths` stand in for `include`), so the overlay, the CLI and the editor agree; without one, from the defaults below. A sygnal-check older than 0.4.0 reads no config file.

options: strict?: boolean - Also run sygnal-check's strict (SYG5xx) rules.

CheckPluginOptions.a11y.title: CheckPluginOptions.a11y?: "error" | "warn"
CheckPluginOptions.a11y.summary: Severity of the a11y lane (SYG701-708). 'warn' keeps it a warning, also under `strict`; 'error' makes it an error, which opens the overlay.

CheckPluginOptions.include.title: CheckPluginOptions.include?: string[]
CheckPluginOptions.include.summary: Files, directories or globs to check, relative to the Vite root. By default the existing ones of src/, pages/ and renderer/ (Vike apps), else the project root (node_modules, dist and other build output are skipped); a one-time notice is logged when the default finds no directory or when none of the given paths exists.

CheckPluginOptions.overlay.title: CheckPluginOptions.overlay?: false | "error" | "warn"
CheckPluginOptions.overlay.summary: Error-severity findings also open Vite's error overlay ('error'); false: never. Every finding is printed in the terminal and logged in the browser console (sygnal-check's codes are currently all warnings or info, so in practice that is where they go). Warnings never use the overlay, because Vite's client reloads the page on the next HMR update while an overlay is open: 'warn' is still accepted, and treated as 'error' with a one-time notice. The overlay is sent only to the page that loads (not to every client), closed before each HMR update and sent again after the re-check.

DefineComponentOptions.head.summary: Document head values for `makeHeadDriver()`, derived from state: `App.head = (state) => ({ title: state.task?.title })`. Recomputed when the result changes; removed on dispose. A later-mounted component's `title` wins; `meta` keys and `link`s merge. Also collected by `renderToString(App, { head: list })` for SSR (`renderHead(list)`). Like every declaration static, it is sent with or without a model; a root needs `initialState` (SYG132).

DefineComponentOptions.name.title: DefineComponentOptions.name?: string

DefineComponentOptions.resources.title: DefineComponentOptions.resources?: { [name: string]: (state: STATE & CALCULATED, bag: DeclarationBag<STATE & CALCULATED, PROPS, CONTEXT>) => false | 0 | ResourceRequest | PagedRequest<any, any>; }
DefineComponentOptions.resources.summary: declarative reads (`makeFetchDriver()`). Each entry derives a request from state and (7.2, as every declaration static) the bag, the view's `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`: `(state, { id, context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + (id ?? route.params.id)`; re-run when the state, the context or a prop changes; falsy means idle: `Quote.resources = { quote: (state) => state.id && '/api/quotes/' + state.id }`. `state.quote` is a `Resource`: `{ status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error', data, error, refreshing }`, written by the built-in RESOURCE action (idle until the first request).

DefineComponentOptions.route.title: DefineComponentOptions.route?: string | ((state: STATE & CALCULATED, bag: DeclarationBag<STATE & CALCULATED, PROPS, CONTEXT>) => string | false)
DefineComponentOptions.route.summary: The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.

FetchRequest.abort.title: FetchRequest.abort: string | true
FetchRequest.abort.summary: Cancel. Reply actions: `{ abort: 'LOADED' }` aborts this instance's requests in flight whose key (`key`, else `ok`, else `error`) is 'LOADED'; `{ abort: true, key: 'search' }` does the same by key. Without reply actions: `{ category: 'search', abort: true }` aborts this component's requests in that category (all of them, reply-action ones included, without a category or key). Nothing is delivered for a cancelled request.

FetchRequest.batch.title: FetchRequest.batch?: readonly { url?: string; method?: string; headers?: Record<string, string>; query?: Record<string, unknown>; json?: unknown; body?: BodyInit; parse?: 'auto' | 'json' | 'text' | ((response: Response) => any); }[]

One failure fails the request (once). The test fake (renderComponent) answers the request as one, by its own `url` / `json`. `decide()` makes these

FetchRequest.cache.title: FetchRequest.cache?: boolean
FetchRequest.cache.summary: : cache this request's reply in the driver's `queryCache()` (any method; a POST is SYG630; without a queryCache nothing is cached, SYG635). `false`: never cached (a resource under `makeFetchDriver({ cache: queryCache() })` too). A request with reply actions is otherwise one-send-one-request

FetchRequest.category.title: FetchRequest.category?: string

Disposing the app still aborts it

FetchRequest.done.title: FetchRequest.done?: string | ((piece: any) => boolean)

FetchRequest.error.title: FetchRequest.error?: string
FetchRequest.error.summary: Reply action that receives a failure, `{ error, status?, body?, headers?, request }` (FetchFailure)

FetchRequest.headers.title: FetchRequest.headers?: Record<string, string> | Headers
FetchRequest.headers.summary: Merged over the driver's `headers`, case-insensitively (names are sent lowercased)

FetchRequest.init.title: FetchRequest.init?: FetchInit
FetchRequest.init.summary: Other fetch() options (merged over the driver's `init`)

FetchRequest.invalidate.title: FetchRequest.invalidate: FetchInvalidate
FetchRequest.invalidate.summary: , from any component: matching cache entries go stale and matching mounted resources refetch, keeping data. With or without the cache

FetchRequest.invalidateOn.title: FetchRequest.invalidateOn?: FetchInvalidateOn
FetchRequest.invalidateOn.summary: When `invalidates` runs (React Query's `onSuccess` / `onSettled`): `'success'` (the default), after a 2xx only; `'settled'`, after the final outcome, failures included (a non-2xx, a network error, a timeout, a `validate` failure), so an optimistic update that failed is refetched. Never after an abort, and once after the last retry. On a failure it runs after the resource's error and the `error` action. Overrides the driver's `invalidateOn`

FetchRequest.invalidates.title: FetchRequest.invalidates?: FetchInvalidate
FetchRequest.invalidates.summary: After a 2xx reply: invalidate these tags / URL prefixes / the predicate's matches (like `{ invalidate }`). A read of them already in flight is aborted, so an older reply never lands. With `invalidateOn: 'settled'`, after a failure too

FetchRequest.json.title: FetchRequest.json?: any
FetchRequest.json.summary: Sent as JSON.stringify(json), with `Content-Type: application/json` unless set

FetchRequest.keepHeaders.title: FetchRequest.keepHeaders?: string[]
FetchRequest.keepHeaders.summary: response headers to keep (case-insensitive): a resource's state gets `headers: { 'x-computed-at': '…' }` (lowercased names, `null` when absent) next to `data` on 'success', kept with `data` on refetches and `keepPrevious`; the query cache stores them with the entry (cache hits, `dehydrate()`, SSR). Part of the cache key and of the request's identity. The `ok` action still gets the body

FetchRequest.key.title: FetchRequest.key?: string
FetchRequest.key.summary: Reply actions: the `latest` / `abort` group (default: the `ok` action, else `error`, else `chunk`). Requests with the same key from the same instance supersede each other under `latest: true`

FetchRequest.latest.title: FetchRequest.latest?: boolean
FetchRequest.latest.summary: Latest only: sending this request aborts this component's requests still in flight in the same category; their responses and errors are never delivered. Default: the driver's `latest` option.

FetchRequest.meta.title: FetchRequest.meta?: boolean
FetchRequest.meta.summary: with `stream: 'sse'`, each piece is `{ data, id, event }` (SseEvent, as a socket SSE connection's `meta: true`): the data JSON-parsed when it parses, the last event id ('' when none was sent) and the event type ('message' or its name). SSE only: NDJSON lines and text have no id or type, so it is ignored there

FetchRequest.method.title: FetchRequest.method?: string
FetchRequest.method.summary: Default: 'POST' when `json` or `body` is set, else 'GET'

FetchRequest.more.title: FetchRequest.more: string
FetchRequest.more.summary: load one more page of this instance's paged resource (a `PagedRequest`): after the last page, or before the first with `previous: true`. Ignored while the resource is loading, has no page yet, or `next` / `previous` gave no cursor (`hasMore` / `hasPrevious` false)

FetchRequest.multipart.title: FetchRequest.multipart?: Record<string, MultipartValue | readonly MultipartValue[]>
FetchRequest.multipart.summary: a multipart/form-data body, written as data: `{ file: state.file, title: state.title }`. A File or Blob is a file part, an array repeats the name (`files: [a, b]`), null/undefined are skipped, an object is sent as JSON text, anything else as a string. The browser sets the content-type (with its boundary); a `content-type` header is dropped. POST by default

FetchRequest.ok.title: FetchRequest.ok?: string
FetchRequest.ok.summary: Reply action that receives the parsed body of a 2xx response (the Response with `parse: 'response'`; with `stream`: the end, `FetchStreamEnd`)

FetchRequest.parse.title: FetchRequest.parse?: "text" | "json" | "auto" | "response" | ((response: Response) => any)
FetchRequest.parse.summary: How the 2xx body becomes `value`: 'auto' (default; JSON when the content-type says json, else text; 204 → null), 'json', 'text', 'response' (the Response), or a function.
FetchRequest.parse.example: renderComponent(C, { now: Date.parse('2026-01-01'), random: 1, uuid: true })

FetchRequest.prefetch.title: FetchRequest.prefetch: string | { [field: string]: any; url: string; }
FetchRequest.prefetch.summary: (H-7): fetch this request into the driver's `queryCache()` without a reply (a fresh entry or the same fetch in flight: nothing new), so a resource that reads it later renders 'success' at once. Without a queryCache it does nothing (SYG635)

FetchRequest.progress.title: FetchRequest.progress?: string | true
FetchRequest.progress.summary: report upload and download progress. An action name: each step arrives as that action of the sending instance (`UPLOADING: (state, { phase, fraction }) => ...`); `true`: on `HTTP.progress(category?)`. Data: FetchProgress. The request then goes over XMLHttpRequest (the only way to see upload progress in every browser); fetch-only `init` options (`keepalive`, `priority`, `cache`, `redirect`, `integrity`, `mode`, `referrerPolicy`) don't apply (SYG636). Not for resources or `batch`. Without XMLHttpRequest (Node): no steps

FetchRequest.query.title: FetchRequest.query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | (string | number | boolean)[]>
FetchRequest.query.summary: Appended as a query string (`{ q: 'dune' }` → `?q=dune`), before any `#fragment`; null/undefined values are skipped; an array repeats the key (`{ tag: ['a', 'b'] }` → `?tag=a&tag=b`)

FetchRequest.refresh.title: FetchRequest.refresh: string | string[]
FetchRequest.refresh.summary: A: refetch this instance's resource(s) by name, keeping data (nothing while idle)

FetchRequest.reset.title: FetchRequest.reset: true | FetchInvalidate
FetchRequest.reset.summary: 7.2 (React Query's resetQueries), from any component: matching cache entries are dropped; matching mounted resources go back to 'loading' with no data and no error, then refetch; paused ones (a hidden Switchable page) lose their kept result ('idle'). `true` matches everything (logout: `{ reset: true }`); otherwise matched like `invalidate`. With or without the cache

FetchRequest.retry.title: FetchRequest.retry?: number | FetchRetry
FetchRequest.retry.summary: Retries (default 0): a count, or a count with the backoff of makeSocketDriver's reconnect (`{ count: 3, delayMs: 500, maxDelayMs: 10000, jitter: 0.2 }`; count defaults to 3). Network errors, 408, 429 (a Retry-After in seconds wins) and 5xx are retried, never other 4xx; the failure arrives once, after the last attempt, with `attempts`

FetchRequest.split.title: FetchRequest.split?: (request: any, error: Error & { status?: number; body?: any;}) => any[] | null | undefined
FetchRequest.split.summary: a request (or a `batch` part) that fails with an HTTP error is sent again as the requests this returns (≥ 2, in parallel, merged by `combine`), at most 3 times deep; null keeps the error. `decide()` halves its questions on a 400 / 413 that names a size limit

FetchRequest.staleTime.title: FetchRequest.staleTime?: number
FetchRequest.staleTime.summary: How long a cached reply stays fresh, in ms (served without a fetch). Implies `cache`

FetchRequest.stream.title: FetchRequest.stream?: "text" | "sse" | "ndjson"
FetchRequest.stream.summary: read a 2xx body as a stream of pieces as they arrive (a POST that streams: a copilot endpoint answering `data: {...}` lines). 'sse': each event's `data`, JSON-parsed when it parses; 'ndjson': each non-blank line, JSON-parsed; 'text': the text as it arrives. Each piece is the `chunk` action (else a reply on `select(category)`); the end of the body (or the `done` piece) is the `ok` action, with `{ status, headers }` (FetchStreamEnd). `latest`, `abort`, `key` and `timeoutMs` (here: the time to the first byte) apply; `retry`, `cache`, `parse`, `validate` and `progress` don't. Not for resources. Test: `t.push('HTTP', piece)` per piece, then `t.respond('HTTP', null)` to end

FetchRequest.tags.title: FetchRequest.tags?: string[]
FetchRequest.tags.summary: Invalidation tags of this request (and its cache entry): `{ invalidate: 'quotes' }` matches `tags: ['quotes']`

FetchRequest.timeoutMs.title: FetchRequest.timeoutMs?: number
FetchRequest.timeoutMs.summary: Fail with a TimeoutError (on `errors()`) after this many ms. Default: the driver's `timeoutMs`

FetchRequest.updates.title: FetchRequest.updates?: string | string[] | Record<string, true | ((data: any, reply: any) => any)>
FetchRequest.updates.summary: A (G-184; React Query's setQueryData): after a 2xx reply, write it into this component's resources with these names (and their `queryCache()` entries) before the `ok` action and before `invalidates`: `updates: 'item'` (the reply becomes `state.item.data`), or `{ items: (list, reply) => newList }` to derive it. A read of them in flight is aborted; other mounted resources on the same cache entry show it too. Resources without a request (idle) are skipped. The `ok` action still gets the reply

FetchRequest.validate.title: FetchRequest.validate?: StandardSchemaLike<any, any>
FetchRequest.validate.summary: A Standard Schema (zod, valibot, arktype, ...) the parsed 2xx body must pass; the reply is the schema's (possibly transformed) value. A failure is an error with `issues`

LazyComponent.agent.title: LazyComponent.agent?: AgentDeclaration<any, {}>
LazyComponent.agent.summary: what agents (the in-app assistant, WebMCP, coding agents) may do with this component and see of it: `{ name, description?, read?, label?, actions: { ACTION: { description, input?, consequential?, when?, idempotent? } } }`. Only the listed actions become tools; their keys are checked against the model's actions, and `input`'s output against the action's data. See `agentTools` in 'sygnal/ai'.
LazyComponent.agent.example: uses = { chat: chat({ agent: false, form: '.ask', prompt: '.prompt', stop: '.stop' }) }

LazyComponent.browser.title: LazyComponent.browser?: (state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => BrowserSources<string>
LazyComponent.browser.summary: browser sources derived from state, run by `makeBrowserDriver()` (registered: `run(App, { BROWSER: makeBrowserDriver() })`; renderComponent provides a fake, `t.browser`) and delivered as this instance's own actions: `Card.browser = (state) => ({ seen: !state.seen && { intersection: '.cover', action: 'SEEN' } })`. Diffed by name as `timers`: a new name starts, a falsy or removed one stops, a changed spec restarts. A hidden Switchable page's sources stop unless `background: true`; dispose stops them; nothing runs during SSR.

LazyComponent.connections.title: LazyComponent.connections?: (state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => Connections
LazyComponent.connections.summary: WebSocket / server-sent events connections derived from state (`makeSocketDriver()`): `Chat.connections = (state) => ({ room: state.room && { socket: '/ws/rooms/' + state.room, message: 'RECEIVED' } })`. Recomputed from the current state (after the action's reducer) and sent to the socket driver's sink whenever the result changes structurally (once at startup too): a new name opens, a removed or falsy one closes, a changed URL reconnects. Events arrive as the named actions on this instance; send with `{ to: 'room', json }` from a model entry (a connection the same action opens or changes is declared first). Dispose closes them.

LazyComponent.context.title: LazyComponent.context?: { [field: string]: ContextEntry<any, any, PROPS, {}>; }
LazyComponent.context.summary: Context this component provides to itself and its descendants. Typed by PROVIDED_CONTEXT, which defaults to CONTEXT (the context the view and reducers see).

LazyComponent.head.title: LazyComponent.head?: (state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => false | HeadValue
LazyComponent.head.summary: Document head values for `makeHeadDriver()`, derived from state: `App.head = (state) => ({ title: state.task?.title })`. Recomputed when the result changes; removed on dispose. A later-mounted component's `title` wins; `meta` keys and `link`s merge. Also collected by `renderToString(App, { head: list })` for SSR (`renderHead(list)`). Like every declaration static, it is sent with or without a model; a root needs `initialState` (SYG132).

LazyComponent.load.title: LazyComponent.load: () => Promise<void>
LazyComponent.load.summary: start the import now (a deferred `when` one too: preload on hover), or again after it failed; any number of times. Resolves once it has loaded or failed

LazyComponent.persist.title: LazyComponent.persist?: Persist<any>
LazyComponent.persist.summary: save this root component's state and restore it at startup: `TodoApp.persist = persist({ key: 'todo-app', pick: ['todos', 'filter'] })`. `pick` / `omit` are typed against STATE's keys. Root component only (SYG224 elsewhere).

LazyComponent.resources.title: LazyComponent.resources?: { [name: string]: (state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => false | 0 | ResourceRequest | PagedRequest<any, any>; }
LazyComponent.resources.summary: declarative reads (`makeFetchDriver()`). Each entry derives a request from state and (7.2, as every declaration static) the bag, the view's `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`: `(state, { id, context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + (id ?? route.params.id)`; re-run when the state, the context or a prop changes; falsy means idle: `Quote.resources = { quote: (state) => state.id && '/api/quotes/' + state.id }`. `state.quote` is a `Resource`: `{ status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error', data, error, refreshing }`, written by the built-in RESOURCE action (idle until the first request).

LazyComponent.route.title: LazyComponent.route?: string | ((state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => string | false)
LazyComponent.route.summary: The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.

LazyComponent.timers.title: LazyComponent.timers?: (state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => Timers<string>
LazyComponent.timers.summary: timers derived from state, run by `makeTimerDriver()` (registered: `run(App, { TIMER: makeTimerDriver() })`; renderComponent provides it) and delivered as this instance's own actions: `Stopwatch.timers = (state) => ({ tick: state.running && { every: 100, action: 'TICK' } })`. Diffed by name whenever the result changes structurally: a new name starts, a falsy or removed one stops, a changed spec restarts. `every` is drift-free (data `{ n, t }`), `after` fires once (`{ t }`), `frame` runs every animation frame (`{ t, dt }`). A hidden Switchable page's timers stop unless `background: true`; dispose stops them; nothing runs during SSR.

LazyComponent.viewTransitions.title: LazyComponent.viewTransitions?: string[]
LazyComponent.viewTransitions.summary: actions whose state change animates as a View Transition: `Board.viewTransitions = ['MOVE']`, `App.viewTransitions = ['ROUTE']` (the router's reply action) for route changes. The DOM patch that the action's STATE reducer causes runs inside `document.startViewTransition()`, which needs the app's DOM driver from `makeViewTransitionDOMDriver()` (SYG645 in dev otherwise). Patched at once, without a transition, under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and where the browser has no API.

RenderResult.actions.title: RenderResult.actions: TestAction[]
RenderResult.actions.summary: every action the rendered tree ran (children and Collection items included), in order, as `{ type, data, component, instance, sinks, cause, at }`. Live array.

RenderResult.agentContext.title: RenderResult.agentContext: () => Record<string, unknown>
RenderResult.agentContext.summary: what a model sees of the app: the `read` projections keyed by declaration `name` (an item declaration's: an array, one projection per live item, each with its `id`). `agent = { name: 'todos', read: s => ({ todos: s.todos }) }` gives `{ todos: { todos: [...] } }`

RenderResult.back.title: RenderResult.back: () => Promise<void>
RenderResult.back.summary: Router fake: the browser's back button (popstate a task later; a block undoes it). With no entry to go back to it throws at the call, as t.respond does (`expect(() => t.back()).toThrow()`), or, behind queued input, rejects

RenderResult.browser.title: RenderResult.browser: BrowserFake
RenderResult.browser.summary: the browser fake's controls (no browser driver passed): `await t.browser.intersect('.cover', true)`, `await t.browser.media('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', true)`, `t.browser.active()`. Each input resolves once its actions are reduced and the tree rendered. Throws when a driver was passed for the browser sink.

RenderResult.cache.title: RenderResult.cache: (sinkName: string) => FakeCacheEntry[]
RenderResult.cache.summary: the cache entries of an HTTP fake (`renderComponent(C, { http: { cache: queryCache() } })`)

RenderResult.callTool.title: RenderResult.callTool: (name: string, args?: unknown, options?: { confirm?: AgentConfirm;}) => Promise<AgentResult>
RenderResult.callTool.summary: run a tool as an agent does (cause 'agent'); resolves with the result after the flush. A consequential tool throws unless `confirm` says the user's answer: `t.callTool('todo_remove', { id: 1 }, { confirm: true })`.

RenderResult.commands.title: RenderResult.commands: { (sinkName?: 'ELEMENT'): ElementCommand[]; (sinkName: string): any[]; }
RenderResult.commands.summary: the element commands the tree's instances sent on `ELEMENT`, one entry per command (arrays flattened), as sent: `expect(t.commands('ELEMENT')).toEqual([{ focus: Email }])`; a `sygnal/ui` dialog's or popover's command with its selector: `{ showModal: '.profile' }`. The mock DOM records them (and reports SYG640/SYG641); `dom: 'real'` also runs them (jsdom gets `<dialog>` show/showModal/close, the popover methods and a no-op scrollIntoView). Another sink name gives its sinkValues.

RenderResult.connections.title: RenderResult.connections: (sinkName: string) => FakeConnection[]
RenderResult.connections.summary: A driverless sink that gets `{ connections }` / `{ to }` values (e.g. `WS` with no `drivers: { WS }`) is a fake makeSocketDriver: diffed per component and connection name, `open`/`message`/`close`/`error` as reply actions of the sender (no `close` for closes the app makes), other events on `WS.select(name)`, shared by URL, reconnect per the spec on the test's timers (fake timers included). The connections declared now, in order. t.open / t.push / t.drop throw at the call when no connection matches (unless input is still queued before them, as for respond) and resolve once the result has been reduced and rendered.

RenderResult.container.title: RenderResult.container: Element
RenderResult.container.summary: `{ dom: 'real' }`: the element the tree is mounted in (removed by dispose()); otherwise null

RenderResult.diagnostics.title: RenderResult.diagnostics: Diagnostic[]
RenderResult.diagnostics.summary: Live array of diagnostics reported while rendered (reading it counts as checking them under `strict`)

RenderResult.dispose.title: RenderResult.dispose: () => void
RenderResult.dispose.summary: Tear down the component, clean up listeners and restore the diagnostics mode. A second call does nothing. Throws a failure the test hasn't seen yet (an event whose element never rendered) and, under `strict: true`, the warn/error diagnostics the test never read.

RenderResult.drop.title: RenderResult.drop: (sinkName: string, close?: { code?: number; reason?: string;} | FakeConnectionTarget, target?: FakeConnectionTarget) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.drop.summary: Connection(s) close without the app closing them: `close` fires with `{ code, reason, willReconnect }` (default `{ code: 1006, reason: '' }`; a connecting one fails to open: `error` first), then the fake reconnects per the spec's `reconnect`.

RenderResult.emitted.title: RenderResult.emitted: { type: string; data: any; }[]
RenderResult.emitted.summary: Live array of EVENTS sink emissions ({type, data})

RenderResult.events$.title: RenderResult.events$: any
RenderResult.events$.summary: Event bus source — call .select(type) to filter

RenderResult.expectNoDiagnostics.title: RenderResult.expectNoDiagnostics: () => void
RenderResult.expectNoDiagnostics.summary: Throws (with the formatted texts) if any warn/error diagnostics were collected

RenderResult.explain.title: RenderResult.explain: (predicate: (state: STATE) => boolean) => ExplainedAction<STATE> | undefined
RenderResult.explain.summary: the first action whose resulting root state matches the predicate, with that state and its STATE reducer; undefined when none did.

RenderResult.fail.title: RenderResult.fail: (sinkName: string, error: any, target?: string | FakeReplyOptions | Record<string, any> | ((request: any) => boolean)) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.fail.summary: Fail a pending request (chosen as in respond): one with reply actions (`error: 'FAILED'`) gets `{ error, request, status?, body? }` as its `FAILED` action, on its sender; a plain one `{ error, category, request, status, body }` on `HTTP.errors(category)`. `error`: an HTTP status (an error response: 404 → the driver's Error 'HTTP 404: url', status 404), or an Error / message (a network failure: no status). On the LLM fake: the stream fails with `error` (a number: Error 'HTTP 429' with `status`), and the request's `error` action gets `{ key, error, request }`; a request with no `error` action throws (the driver would only log it, SYG678).

RenderResult.focus.title: RenderResult.focus: () => void
RenderResult.focus.summary: the window regains focus (queued like simulate*): stale mounted resources refetch (cache on)
RenderResult.focus.example: defineWidget({ children: true, mount, sync(instance, childrenVnode, el), focus(instance, child) })

RenderResult.forward.title: RenderResult.forward: () => Promise<void>
RenderResult.forward.summary: Router fake: the browser's forward button. With no entry to go forward to: as t.back()

RenderResult.frames.title: RenderResult.frames: (n?: number) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.frames.summary: Wait for `n` frames (default 1) of the running `frame` timers: their actions reduced, the tree rendered. Under fake timers it moves the clock frame by frame (deterministic: the same input, the same frames); with real timers it waits for them. Rejects when no frame timer runs. `settle()` doesn't wait on a frame loop: what a frame timer causes isn't activity.

RenderResult.head.title: RenderResult.head: () => { title: string | undefined; meta: Record<string, string>; link: Array<Record<string, any>>;}
RenderResult.head.summary: HEAD fake (no HEAD driver passed): the head the components declare now (`head` statics and HEAD sink values), merged as makeHeadDriver merges them: `{ title, meta: { name: content }, link: [{ rel, href }] }`, `titleTemplate` applied

RenderResult.html.title: RenderResult.html: () => string
RenderResult.html.summary: Latest rendered VNode serialized to HTML like innerHTML (text escapes only & < >, so `Couldn't`, not `'`). Throws if called before the first render: wait with `await t.ready()` (or `t.next(...)`) first. '' for a component that renders nothing.

RenderResult.inspect.title: RenderResult.inspect: (options?: Pick<InspectOptions, 'actions'>) => InspectGraph
RenderResult.inspect.summary: The app graph of the rendered tree (components, actions, selectors with the mock DOM's match / isolation results, EVENTS, diagnostics). Throws unless 'sygnal/diagnostics' is loaded. `{ actions: true }` (or a number: the last n) adds `recentActions` (GS-10).

RenderResult.location.title: RenderResult.location: { path: string; search: string; query: Record<string, string>; hash: string; href: string; }
RenderResult.location.summary: Router fake: the in-memory location: `path` (pathname), `search` ('?tab=x' or ''), `query` (the search parsed as `state.route.query` has it: `{ tab: 'x' }`), `hash` ('#c' or ''), `href`

RenderResult.navigate.title: RenderResult.navigate: (target: string | { to: string; params?: Record<string, string | number>; query?: Record<string, any>; hash?: string; replace?: boolean;}) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.navigate.summary: Router fake (`renderComponent(App, { router })`): navigate as a click on a link with this href (`'/tasks/2'`), or as the command `{ to: 'task', params: { id: 2 }, query?, hash?, replace? }`. Goes through `{ block }` like the real thing. Throws at the call for an unknown route name, a missing param or another origin; resolves once the route has been reduced and the tree rendered.

RenderResult.next.title: RenderResult.next: (predicate?: (state: STATE) => boolean, timeoutMs?: number) => Promise<STATE>
RenderResult.next.summary: Wait for the next state emitted AFTER this call (right after `await t.ready()`: after the component became ready) that satisfies the predicate (default: any state). Resolves with it once the whole tree (children included) has rendered it; rejects after timeoutMs (default: the timeoutMs option, 2000). The error names a model next() still scheduled, and a recorded state that already matched. A next() right after another wait (no input in between) starts after the state that wait resolved with, so `await t.next(a); await t.next(b)` sees a `b` that arrived while `a` rendered.

RenderResult.online.title: RenderResult.online: () => void
RenderResult.online.summary: the browser comes back online (queued like simulate*): stale mounted resources refetch (cache on)

RenderResult.open.title: RenderResult.open: (sinkName: string, target?: FakeConnectionTarget) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.open.summary: Complete the open of connecting connection(s) (`autoConnect: false`, or a pending retry): `open` fires with `{ reconnected }`

RenderResult.pageLoads.title: RenderResult.pageLoads: { url: string; replace: boolean; }[]
RenderResult.pageLoads.summary: Router fake: the full page loads the app made, in order, as absolute URLs: a navigation to an `external` URL or with `reload: true` (`replace: true` for a replace), or a link click the router left to the browser. Recorded, not made: the location and the rendered page stay as they were

RenderResult.progress.title: RenderResult.progress: (sinkName: string, step: { loaded: number; total?: number; phase?: 'upload' | 'download';}, target?: string | FakeReplyOptions | Record<string, any> | ((request: any) => boolean)) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.progress.summary: one progress step of a pending request sent with `progress` (chosen as in respond; `'UPLOADING'` matches its progress action too): `t.progress('HTTP', { loaded: 50, total: 100 }, 'UPLOADING')`. The component gets FetchProgress (`fraction: 0.5`) as that action, or on `HTTP.progress()` for `progress: true`. `phase` defaults to 'upload' for a request with a body, else 'download'. The request stays pending until respond()/fail(). Resolves once reduced and rendered.

RenderResult.push.title: RenderResult.push: (sinkName: string, data: any, target?: FakeConnectionTarget | { event?: string; id?: string | number; connection?: FakeConnectionTarget;}) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.push.summary: The server sends `data` (objects as JSON text) on open connection(s): `message` fires with the data, JSON-parsed when it parses. `{ event, connection? }` sends an SSE named event; `{ id }` gives an SSE event its id (what `meta: true` reports and `resume` resumes from). on an HTTP fake, `data` is one piece of the pending request sent with `stream` that `target` picks (as in respond), written in its format (SSE `data:` lines, an NDJSON line, text; objects as JSON) and parsed by the real driver; `t.respond(name, null)` ends it. A sink other than the socket sink that declares no connections pushes to its stream requests.

RenderResult.query.title: RenderResult.query: { <E extends Element = Element>(selector: string): E; <CONTROL extends AnyControl>(control: CONTROL): ControlElementOf<CONTROL>; }
RenderResult.query.summary: The first element matching a selector in the rendered tree (Portal content included), or null: `expect(t.query('input[name="plan"]:checked').value).toBe('team')`. With `dom: 'real'` a real element (any CSS selector); with the mock DOM a read-only snapshot of what the view rendered (simulateEvent's selectors plus `:checked`/`:disabled`/`:enabled`; textContent, value, checked, disabled, getAttribute, classList, dataset, querySelector, closest, next/previousElementSibling...; no focus()). Throws before the first render (`await t.ready()` first). Right after `await t.next(pred)` / `waitForState` / `settle()` / `ready()` / `simulateEvent()` it shows the state the wait resolved with.

RenderResult.queryAll.title: RenderResult.queryAll: { <E extends Element = Element>(selector: string): E[]; <CONTROL extends AnyControl>(control: CONTROL): ControlElementOf<CONTROL>[]; }
RenderResult.queryAll.summary: Every element matching a selector (or a control) in the rendered tree (Portals included), as query(), in document order, also for a ',' list: `t.queryAll('.empty, .filters')` lists whichever comes first first (an order check)

RenderResult.ready.title: RenderResult.ready: () => Promise<void>
RenderResult.ready.summary: Resolves once the component is subscribed (earlier simulate* calls are buffered and replayed). Also a cursor: the first next() after `await t.ready()` also matches the states the replayed calls produced, unless another t.* call came in between.

RenderResult.requests.title: RenderResult.requests: (sinkName: string) => any[]
RenderResult.requests.summary: Live array of the requests a sink was sent, as objects: a string request is `{ url }`, a resource fetch `{ url, ...request, resource: name }`. Never the `{ abort }` commands, `{ resources }` declarations or `{ refresh }` / `{ more }` commands (sinkValues has every value, as sent)

RenderResult.respond.title: RenderResult.respond: (sinkName: string, value: any, target?: string | FakeReplyOptions | Record<string, any> | ((request: any) => boolean)) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.respond.summary: Answer a pending request on a driverless sink/source (e.g. `HTTP` with no `drivers: { HTTP }`, which runs makeFetchDriver over an in-memory fetch) with a response whose body is `value` (JSON; text for a string): a request with reply actions (`ok: 'LOADED'`) gets the parsed body as its `LOADED` action, on exactly the component that sent it; a plain one gets `{ category, value, status: 200, request }` on `HTTP.select(category)`. Which request (the newest pending one that matches): `target` is an `ok`/`error` action name, key, category, resource name or URL (`'LOADED'`); a partial request compared by value with its t.requests form (`{ url: '/a' }`, the constant the model returns);

RenderResult.sent.title: RenderResult.sent: (sinkName: string, to?: string) => any[]
RenderResult.sent.summary: Live array of the `{ to, json | text | binary }` values sent (`to`: only those to that connection). For the router fake's sink (`t.sent('ROUTER')`): the commands the components sent (`{ to, params }`, `{ back: true }`, `{ block }`...), not the `route` declarations. For PARENT and EVENTS (no driver): the values sent on them, as `sinkValues` (a step's `{ wizard: 'NEXT' }`)

RenderResult.settle.title: RenderResult.settle: (timeoutMs?: number) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.settle.summary: Resolves once nothing is pending: the component is ready, no simulated input is waiting, and nothing in the tree has rendered, reduced or changed state for settleMs (default 20, longer than a model next()'s default delay). Rejects after timeoutMs if it never calms down.

RenderResult.simulateAction.title: RenderResult.simulateAction: (actionName: string, data?: any, options?: SimulateActionOptions) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.simulateAction.summary: Push an action into the intent→model pipeline under its real name (all sinks of the entry run), like the component's intent emitting it. It reaches one instance: the rendered component, or with `{ component: Child }` the first rendered instance of `Child` (`within`: inside the first element matching a selector or control, e.g. one Collection item). A name that instance has no model entry for (nor a behavior action or a built-in) fails the test, naming the components that handle it: `t.simulateAction('INFER_FILE', file, { component: Start })`. Awaitable: resolves once the action is delivered and the tree has rendered it

RenderResult.simulateEvent.title: RenderResult.simulateEvent: (selector: string | AnyControl, eventType: string, eventInit?: SimulatedEventInit) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.simulateEvent.summary: Dispatch a synthetic DOM event through the mock DOM source so the component's real intent streams fire (DOM.click('.x'), DOM.select('.x').events('click'), .value(), .data()). Targets the first rendered element matching `selector` and bubbles within its isolation scope. Selectors match the rendered tree like the real DOM: tag, .class, #id, [attr], [attr="v"] (^= $= *= ~=), :first-child, :last-child, :only-child, :nth-child(an+b|odd|even), :nth-last-child(), :first/last/only/nth-of-type, :not(), descendant ' ', child '>', next-sibling '+' and later-sibling '~' combinators, ',' lists. Other syntax (:has(), pseudo-elements...) throws.

RenderResult.sinkValues.title: RenderResult.sinkValues: (sinkName: string) => any[]
RenderResult.sinkValues.summary: Live array of values emitted on a sink (EVENTS as {type, data}, PARENT unwrapped, custom sinks of any component in the tree)

RenderResult.sinks.title: RenderResult.sinks: Record<string, any>
RenderResult.sinks.summary: All sink streams by driver name

RenderResult.sources.title: RenderResult.sources: Record<string, any>
RenderResult.sources.summary: All source objects by driver name
RenderResult.sources.example: Counter.intent = ({ DOM }) => ({                          // sources: DOM STATE EVENTS CHILD props$ commands$ dispose$ + drivers

RenderResult.state.title: RenderResult.state: STATE
RenderResult.state.summary: The latest recorded state (`t.states.at(-1)`; undefined before the first one), calculated fields current. Read-only

RenderResult.states.title: RenderResult.states: STATE[]
RenderResult.states.summary: Collected state values — grows as new states are emitted

RenderResult.storage.title: RenderResult.storage: <ENTRY = PersistedEntry<STATE>>(key: string) => ENTRY
RenderResult.storage.summary: the fake storage's entry for `key` (`{ version, state }`), undefined when none (a raw string when what is stored isn't JSON). Pending persist() writes are flushed by t.settle(). A `format: 'plain'` entry is the stored keys: `t.storage<{ title: string }>('note-draft')`

RenderResult.stream.title: RenderResult.stream: (sinkName: string, chunks: FakeChatChunk[], target?: string | (FakeReplyOptions & { end?: boolean;}) | Record<string, any> | ((request: any) => boolean), options?: { end?: boolean;}) => Promise<void>
RenderResult.stream.summary: stream into a pending request of the LLM fake (the sink named by `llmSink`, default 'LLM': the real makeChatDriver over an in-memory transport). Chunks: strings (text), `{ reasoning }`, `{ toolCall: { id?, name, input } }`, `{ toolResult: { id, output } }`, `{ data, name?, id? }`, `{ finish: reason | { reason, usage } }`, or ChatEvents. Each call is one frame: at most one `delta` action, with no timers involved (fake timers work unchanged). The stream then ends (the `ok` action) unless `{ end: false }` is passed, as the last argument or in the target options; a `{ finish }` chunk ends it too. The request is chosen as in respond. Resolves once the replies are reduced and the tree rendered.

RenderResult.timers.title: RenderResult.timers: () => ActiveTimer[]
RenderResult.timers.summary: the timer fake's active timers, in start order (`{ name, every | after | frame, action, background?, component }`): a fired `after`, a stopped one or an invalid spec is not listed. The fake is the real makeTimerDriver(), so fake timers drive it (`vi.useFakeTimers()`, then `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms)`). Throws when a driver was passed for the timer sink.

RenderResult.tools.title: RenderResult.tools: () => AgentTool[]
RenderResult.tools.summary: the agent tools of the shown instances' `agent` declarations (`{ name, description, inputSchema, annotations }`); a declared tool that can't be offered (SYG240) is listed with its `error`.

RenderResult.waitForState.title: RenderResult.waitForState: (predicate: (state: STATE) => boolean, timeoutMs?: number) => Promise<STATE>
RenderResult.waitForState.summary: Wait for a state that satisfies the predicate. Matches the recorded HISTORY too: a state from before the call resolves it (e.g. `count === 0` right after a reset resolves at once with the initial state). Resolves with the matching state once the whole tree (children included) has rendered it. Use `next()` to wait for a new state.

RenderResult.widget.title:
RenderResult.widget: {

(selector: string): WidgetHandle; (control: CONTROL): WidgetHandle; }
RenderResult.widget.summary: A widget's host, by selector (`'.due'`) or control. `props`: what the view passed the widget (mock DOM: the rendered host's; `dom: 'real'`: the mounted widget's). `instance` (`dom: 'real'`): what `mount` returned. `emit(name, detail)`: the CustomEvent the widget's dispatch() sends, sent like `simulateEvent`. Reading `props`/`instance` throws when no widget host matches.

Each entry derives a request from state and (7.2, as every declaration static) the bag, the view's `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`: `(state, { id, context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + (id ?? route.params.id)`; re-run when the state, the context or a prop changes; falsy means idle: `Quote.resources = { quote: (state) => state.id && '/api/quotes/' + state.id }`. `state.quote` is a `Resource`: `{ status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error', data, error, refreshing }`, written by the built-in RESOURCE action (idle until the first request).

RootComp.route.title: RootComp.route?: string | ((state: SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, bag: DeclarationBag<SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, {}, SpecOf<T, "context", {}>>) => string | false)
RootComp.route.summary: The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.

RootComp.timers.title: RootComp.timers?: (state: SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, bag: DeclarationBag<SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, {}, SpecOf<T, "context", {}>>) => Timers<ActionNameOf<SpecOf<T, "actions", {}>>>

Diffed by name whenever the result changes structurally: a new name starts, a falsy or removed one stops, a changed spec restarts. `every` is drift-free (data `{ n, t }`), `after` fires once (`{ t }`), `frame` runs every animation frame (`{ t, dt }`). A hidden Switchable page's timers stop unless `background: true`; dispose stops them; nothing runs during SSR.

SYG101.title: SYG101 (warn): Intent action has no model entry
SYG101.summary: The intent returns an action stream whose name has no matching key in `model`. Events on that stream are produced but nothing handles them, so the action silently does nothing. Built-in actions (`BOOTSTRAP`, `INITIALIZE`, `DISPOSE`, `READY`, and `RESOURCE`, which the core writes for a `resources` static) and internal `__*` actions are never reported. `HYDRATE` is not built in since 6.0: it is an ordinary action name.
SYG101.note:
Fix: Add a model entry with the same name, e.g. `model = { SAVE: (state) => ({ ...state, saved: true }) }`, or remove or rename the intent action so it matches an existing model key.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG101

SYG102.title: SYG102 (info): Model entry is unreachable
SYG102.summary: A model entry has no intent action of the same name and is not a built-in action (`BOOTSTRAP`, `INITIALIZE`, `DISPOSE`, `READY`, `RESOURCE`; `HYDRATE` is an ordinary action since 6.0), so nothing in the intent can trigger it. A request also triggers the reply actions it names (`{ url, ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }` sent to a driver sink, and an HTTP request's `progress: 'UPLOAD_PROGRESS'`), and so does a `connections` entry (`message`, `open`, `close`, `error`) or a request a `resources` entry derives (`ok`, `error`). A `RESOURCE` entry replaces the built-in reducer that writes `state[name]` for a `resources` static.
SYG102.note:
Fix: Add the action to the component's `intent`, name it in a request (`HTTP: (state) => ({ url, ok: 'ACTION' })`), dispatch it with `next('ACTION')` from another entry, or remove the dead model entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG102

SYG103.title: SYG103 (info): Intent selector matched no rendered element
SYG103.summary: A selector passed to `DOM.select()` in the intent has not matched any element the component rendered, so its events never fire (often a typo in the class or id). The dev entry skips selectors whose class/id/tag tokens all appear in the view source (assumed conditionally rendered); others are reported as info on the first check and escalated to warn after at least 3 renders and about 2 s of render-idle time with no match. Under `renderComponent`, `simulateEvent()` on a selector that matches no rendered element throws an error instead; with `{ allowMissing: true }` the event is dropped and SYG103 is reported.
SYG103.note:
Fix: Check the selector against the `className`/`id` in the view. If the element is rendered by a child component, handle the event inside that child instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG103

SYG104.title: SYG104 (warn): Intent selector crosses an isolation boundary
SYG104.summary: An intent selector matches nothing in the component's own scope, but does match elements rendered inside a child component or Collection item. Child components are isolated, so the parent's `DOM` source never receives events from those elements and the action never fires. The dev entry checks the real DOM after renders, `renderComponent` checks the mock vtree, and `sygnal-check` finds the class/id, or the control (`DOM.click(Remove)` with `<Remove>` rendered by the child), only in a child component's view.
SYG104.note:
Fix: Handle the event inside the child component and send it up with `PARENT` (read it in the parent with `CHILD.select(Child)`), or broadcast it with `EVENTS`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG104

SYG105.title: SYG105 (info): EVENTS type selected but never emitted, or emitted but never selected
SYG105.summary: An `EVENTS` bus type is emitted with nothing selecting it, or selected with `EVENTS.select(type)` but never emitted. The bus is a broadcast, so an event that nobody has subscribed to when it is emitted is dropped; a mismatched name usually means a typo. At runtime the emitted-not-selected case is reported when the event is emitted, while selected-not-emitted is only reported on demand via `checkEventBus()` (inspect/test helpers); `EVENTS.select()` with no type counts as selecting everything. The static checker compares string-literal types across the scanned files and reports warn, or info when non-literal emits/selects exist.
SYG105.note:
Fix: Make the names match: emit from a model entry, e.g. `{ EVENTS: event('TYPE', data) }`, and subscribe with `EVENTS.select('TYPE')` in the receiving component's intent.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG105

SYG106.title: SYG106 (warn): Parent prop is overwritten by a reserved view argument
SYG106.summary: The view is called with `{ ...props, state, children, slots, context, uid }`, so a prop named `children`, `slots`, `context` or `uid` passed by the parent is overwritten and never reaches the child. A `state` prop is also reported when its value is not a state lens (a field-name string or a `{ get, set }` object), because Sygnal reads `state` as the child's state lens rather than as data. Reported once per component and prop, as a warning, or as an error in strict mode (`--strict` has no static SYG106 rule;
SYG106.note:
Fix: Rename the prop in both parent and child (e.g. `contextValue`, `itemId` instead of `uid`, or `item` instead of `state`); to give the child a slice of parent state use `state="fieldName"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG106

SYG107.title: SYG107 (warn): DOM property name in the wrong case
SYG107.summary: Sygnal sets a JSX name on an HTML element as the DOM property of that name, in that case (React keeps a table of attribute names; Preact falls back to an attribute). A name the element has no property for creates an unused JavaScript property on the element: nothing is rendered, nothing fails, and the server-rendered markup and the mock DOM of `renderComponent` still show it. The usual cause is the case.
SYG107.note: Fix: Write the DOM property's name: ``, ``, ``. For an attribute that has no DOM property, use the attrs module: `attrs-autocomplete="off"` or `attrs={{ autocomplete: 'off' }}`. `sygnal-check --fix` renames the attribute. More: sygnal-check explain SYG107

SYG108.title: SYG108 (error): Intent selector is not valid CSS
SYG108.summary: An intent selector (`DOM.click('.x')`, `DOM.select('.x')`) that the browser can't parse. Sygnal matches selectors with `Element.matches()`, so an invalid one throws a `SyntaxError` on every matching event, and the throw takes the component's other DOM listeners down with it. The usual cause is a utility-class name used as the hook: a Tailwind class like `hover:bg-red-500` (the `:bg-red-500` reads as a pseudo-class), `w-1/2` (`/` needs escaping), `w-[10px]` (`[` starts an attribute selector) or a name starting with a digit.
SYG108.note:
Fix: Give the element a separate plain class as the event hook and select that: `<button className="save hover:bg-red-500">` with `DOM.click('.save')`. Or use a control. If you do need to match such a class, escape it: `DOM.click('.hover\\:bg-red-500')` in a JavaScript string.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG108

SYG109.title: SYG109 (warn): Numeric style value without a unit
SYG109.summary: Sygnal assigns each key of `style` to `elm.style` as written and does not append `px` (React does; Sygnal deliberately doesn't). For a property that needs a unit, a number is invalid CSS, so `style={{ width: 10 }}` sets nothing, silently. Zero is valid, and so are unitless properties such as `opacity`, `zIndex`, `flexGrow`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight` and the SVG `strokeWidth` (the list is React's `isUnitlessNumber`, plus the few CSS number properties React's list misses). Custom properties (`--x`) are never reported, and `delayed`, `remove` and `destroy` sub-objects are checked too.
SYG109.note:
Fix: Write a string with the unit: `style={{ width: '10px' }}` (or `` `${state.w}px` ``). `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites a number literal to `'10px'`, except for time and angle properties such as `transitionDuration` or `rotate`, where the unit is yours to choose.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG109

SYG110.title: SYG110 (warn): Intent selector not present in the component view
SYG110.summary: A class or id selector used in the intent (`DOM.select('.x')`, `DOM.click('.x')`, ...) is never rendered by the component's own view, nor by JSX passed into it as children/slots, so the action never fires. For a control (`DOM.click(Add)`), the view never renders `<Add>`. It is reported as info instead of warn when a dynamic `className`/`id` in the view might produce the name, or when the selector itself is not a static string and could not be checked.
SYG110.note:
Fix: Fix the selector to match the view, or add the class/id to the element, e.g. `className="x"`; use a string literal (or module-level const) selector so it can be checked. For a control, render it in the view (`<Add>Add</Add>`) or listen to a control the view does render. For a CSS Module class, keep a stable hook class beside it (``className={`save ${s.save}`}``), listen to a control, or select the hashed name (``DOM.click(`.${s.save}`)``).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG110

SYG111.title: SYG111 (warn): Controlled input has no input listener
SYG111.summary: An `<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>` has `value` (or a checkbox/radio has `checked`) set, but the component's intent has no input/change/keyup/keydown listener on it or an ancestor. Sygnal writes the bound value back on every render, so any re-render while the user is typing or clicking resets the field; this also applies to literal values such as `value=""` and to `value={null}`/`checked={null}`, which clear or uncheck the field on every render (only an absent prop leaves a field uncontrolled). A key listener that is immediately filtered to one key (e.g. Enter) does not count.
SYG111.note:
Fix: Update state on input, e.g. `DOM.input('.name').value()` (or `DOM.change(...)` for toggles/selects), or drop the `value`/`checked` prop (not set it to `null`) to leave the field uncontrolled and read it on blur or submit.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG111

SYG112.title: SYG112 (error): Reply action has no model entry
SYG112.summary: A request sent to a driver with reply actions (`makeFetchDriver`, `driverFromAsync`, the socket driver) names its reply actions, as in `{ url, ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }`, and the driver delivers the reply to the sending component as that action. When the component's model has no entry with that name, the reply is dropped, usually because of a typo, or because the entry is in another component: a reply goes only to the instance that sent the request (two instances, every Collection item), never to a parent that has an entry of that name. The dev entry checks each request with reply actions as it is sent;
SYG112.note:
Fix: Use the name of an existing model entry (the message names the closest one), or add the entry: `LOADED: (state, body) => ({ ...state, data: body })`. When an ancestor handles the reply, send the request from the ancestor: the child emits `EVENTS: event('RETRY_TEMPLATES')`, the ancestor selects it in its intent and sends the request from that entry, so the reply comes back to it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG112

SYG115.title: SYG115 (warn): Unknown DOM event shorthand
SYG115.summary: `DOM.<name>(selector)` is shorthand for `DOM.select(selector).events('<name>')`, and the DOM source accepts any property name, so a made-up name such as `DOM.key('.search')`, `DOM.enter(...)` or `DOM.keyDown(...)` listens for an event the browser never fires: the action silently never happens. The dev entry reports a shorthand call whose name is not a known DOM event, once per component and name. Key names and the enriched-stream helpers (`.key()`, `.value()`, `.checked()`, `.data()`) are not events.
SYG115.note:
Fix: Use the real event and an enriched-stream helper: `DOM.keydown('.search').key()` (add `.filter(k => k === 'Enter')` for one key), `DOM.input('.name').value()`, `DOM.change('.box').checked()`. For a custom event you dispatch yourself, use the explicit form `DOM.select(sel).events('my-event')`, which is never reported.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG115

SYG116.title: SYG116 (error): EVENTS value has no string type
SYG116.summary: A model sent a value without a string `type` to the `EVENTS` sink, so no `EVENTS.select(type)` can receive it and it is dropped. The usual cause is a function: a model entry that returns `event(...)` (for example `{ EVENTS: () => event('SAVED', data) }`) instead of being `event(...)`, or any other reducer that returns a function. Each emitted value is copied into a new object, so a function arrives on the bus as `{}`. A reducer that returns `undefined` or `null` (see SYG217) causes it too. `sygnal-check` reports a sink entry that is a function returning `event(...)` (or `emit(...)`) from 'sygnal' (ui-sweep R5).
SYG116.note:
Fix: Make `event()` the sink entry itself: `SAVE: { EVENTS: event('SAVED', (state, data) => payload) }`; return `ABORT` from a reducer to send nothing.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG116

SYG117.title: SYG117 (warn): next() names an action with no model entry
SYG117.summary: `next('X')` in a model handler dispatches `X` to the same component, and only there. When that component has no model entry `X`, nothing happens: no error, no state change. The usual cause is a child calling `next()` for an action its parent handles (a card's `next('ENTER')` when only the page has `ENTER`), which looks like a hang; a typo is the other. The dev entry reports the first `next()` of each name a component sends with no entry, and names the nearest ancestor that has one.
SYG117.note:
Fix: To reach the parent, send the action up: give the entry a `PARENT` sink (`PARENT: (state) => ({ … })`) and read it in the parent's intent with `ENTER: CHILD.select(Card)`, or emit `EVENTS: event('ENTER', …)` and select it there. For a typo, use the existing entry's name; otherwise add the entry to this component's model.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG117

SYG118.title: SYG118 (warn): Host intent replaces a behavior trigger
SYG118.summary: An intent action named like a behavior action (`'tabs.SELECT'`, `'profile.OPEN'`) replaces the trigger the behavior builds for it; it doesn't add one. When that trigger comes from an option you passed (`tabs({ tab: '.tab' })` makes `tabs.SELECT` from clicks on `.tab`; `dialog({ trigger: '.edit' })` makes `profile.OPEN` from clicks on `.edit`), the elements the option names stop working: tab clicks no longer select, the trigger no longer opens the dialog.
SYG118.note:
Fix: To add another element, list both in the option (`trigger: '.edit, .avatar'`, `tab: '.tab, .go-billing'`), or give the other element its own action that dispatches the behavior's with `next('profile.OPEN')`, or write the slice in a reducer (`{ ...state, tabs: { ...state.tabs, selected: 'billing' } }`). To replace the trigger on purpose, leave the option out.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG118

SYG124.title: SYG124 (error): Component used as a control or selector
SYG124.summary: A component was passed where `DOM.select()` or a `DOM.<event>()` shorthand expects a control or a CSS selector, as in `DOM.click(TodoItem)`. A component is not an element: it has no single root to listen on, and its elements are isolated from the parent, so there is nothing for the listener to match. Controls look like components in JSX, which makes this an easy mistake.
SYG124.note:
Fix: Handle the event inside the child and send it up with `PARENT`, then read it in the parent with `CHILD.select(TodoItem)`. Or give the parent a control and render it around the child: `const { Item } = controls({ Item: 'div' })`, `<Item><TodoItem /></Item>`, `DOM.click(Item)`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG124

SYG125.title: SYG125 (error): Control given .intent, .model or .initialState
SYG125.summary: A control from `controls({ ... })` was given `.intent`, `.model` or `.initialState`, as if it were a component. Controls are elements, not components: a control renders its element with a `data-control` marker and nothing else, so it has no intent, model or state, and these statics are never used.
SYG125.note:
Fix: Put the intent and model on the component that renders the control, and listen to the control there: `App.intent = ({ DOM }) => ({ ADD: DOM.click(Add) })`. For something with its own state and actions, write a component instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG125

SYG126.title: SYG126 (info): Control rendered but never listened to
SYG126.summary: A component renders a control (for example `<Add>`), but its intent never listens to it. A control exists to link an element to an intent, so an unused one is usually a missing intent entry or a leftover from a refactor. A control the model sends element commands to (`ELEMENT: { showModal: HelpDialog }`) counts as used. It is info because a control may also be used only to find the element in tests (`t.query(Draft)`).
SYG126.note:
Fix: Listen to it in the component's intent (`ADD: DOM.click(Add)`), or render the plain element (`<button>`) if it needs no events.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG126

SYG127.title: SYG127 (error): Behavior collision or unresolvable uses entry
SYG127.summary: A component's `uses` static names behaviors: `TaskList.uses = { pager: pager({ pageSize: 10, next: Newer }) }` runs the behavior on `state.pager`, with its actions named `pager.NEXT`. Three things break that. The host's `initialState` already has the key (`initialState = { pager: ... }`): the behavior's slice replaces it, so the host's value is lost. A `uses` value is not what a `defineBehavior()` factory returns (a plain object, the factory itself without the call, `undefined`): it is skipped, so `state[key]` and its actions never exist.
SYG127.note:
Fix: Remove the key from the host's `initialState` (set the behavior's values through its options: `pager({ pageSize: 10 })`), or rename the `uses` key. For an unresolvable entry, call the factory: `uses = { pager: pager() }`, with `pager = defineBehavior({ ... })`. For an unknown option, use the name the behavior reads (the message lists them and suggests the closest).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG127

SYG128.title: SYG128 (error): Duplicate control key
SYG128.summary: Two `controls()` calls in one file declare the same key, or one call repeats a key. Every control renders `data-control="<Key>"` and is selected by that key, so two controls with one key match each other's elements: a listener on one also fires for the other.
SYG128.note:
Fix: Rename one of the keys, or declare both controls in a single `controls({ ... })` call.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG128

SYG129.title: SYG129 (warn): CHILD.select() of a component this one doesn't render
SYG129.summary: An intent reads `CHILD.select(TaskRow)`, but the component's view doesn't render `TaskRow`: a component it renders does (a grandchild, for example a Collection item inside a child). A component's `PARENT` output reaches only the component that renders it, so the action never fires and nothing says why. sygnal-check follows the views it can read and reports the chain (`App > ProjectSection > TaskRow`).
SYG129.note:
Fix: Relay the value through the component in between: in `ProjectSection.intent` read `RELAY: CHILD.select(TaskRow)`, in `ProjectSection.model` send it on with `RELAY: { PARENT: (state, data) => data }`, and read `CHILD.select(ProjectSection)` in `App`. For a value many components need, broadcast it with `EVENTS` instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG129

SYG130.title: SYG130 (error): href() names no route or leaves out a param
SYG130.summary: `router.href(name, params)` builds a link from the route table passed to `makeRouter({ routes })`. When `name` is not a route (or is the `'*'` not-found route), href() returns the app's root path; when the pattern has a `:param` that `params` leaves out, that segment is empty (`/tasks/`). Either way the link goes somewhere else than intended. The `sygnal/diagnostics` dev entry checks every href() call; production builds don't. A `{ to }` command with the same problem is SYG620.
SYG130.note:
Fix: Use a route name from the table (the message suggests the closest one) and pass every param the pattern names: `href('task', { id: task.id })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG130

SYG131.title: SYG131 (warn): Route params the pattern does not use
SYG131.summary: An href() call or a `{ to, params }` router command passes a param that the route's pattern has no `:name` for. It is ignored, so the value never reaches the URL; usually it was meant for the query string, or the route is the wrong one.
SYG131.note:
Fix: Pass only the pattern's params, and put other values in the query: `href('tasks', {}, { page: 2 })` or `{ to: 'tasks', query: { page: 2 } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG131

SYG132.title: SYG132 (warn): Declaration static that is never sent
SYG132.summary: Declaration statics (`route`, `resources`, `connections`, `head`) are computed from the component's state and sent to their driver whenever they change, with or without a model. A root component (the one passed to `run()`) with a model but no `initialState` has no state, so its state stream never emits: the route never arrives, the resources never load, the connections never open, the head never changes. Sub-components share their parent's state, so this only happens at the root.
SYG132.note:
Fix: Give the root an `initialState`, even an empty object; for the router, seed the route: `App.initialState = { route: router.current() }`. Don't add an `initialState` to a sub-component that shares its parent's state: it would replace that state (SYG405).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG132

SYG133.title: SYG133 (warn): SPA router inside a Vike app
SYG133.summary: `makeRouter()` intercepts link clicks and writes the history itself, and so does Vike's client router. Running the SPA router inside a Vike app makes both handle each click and navigation. In Vike, give the router Vike's `navigate()`: it then leaves links and history to Vike, navigates with `navigate()`, and re-reads the route after each Vike navigation.
SYG133.note:
Fix: `makeRouter({ routes, navigate })` with `import { navigate } from 'vike/client/router'`, using a route table that mirrors the Vike routes; or read the route from Vike's page context and drop the router.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG133

SYG140.title: SYG140 (warn): Widget dispatched an undeclared event
SYG140.summary: A widget made with `defineWidget()` called `dispatch(name, detail)` (the third parameter of `mount`) with a name that is not in its `events` list. The event is still dispatched (a bubbling `CustomEvent` on the host), but `events` is what the docs, sygnal-check and the other widget diagnostics read: a listener for the declared name never hears this one, which is usually a typo (`dispatch('chnage', d)`) or a declaration that was never added. The dev entry reports it once per widget and name when it is dispatched; sygnal-check reports a literal `dispatch('x')` inside `mount()` (whatever the parameter is called) when `events` is a literal list.
SYG140.note:
Fix: Add the name to the widget's `events` (`defineWidget({ events: ['pick', 'clear'], ... })`), or dispatch one of the declared names.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG140

SYG141.title: SYG141 (warn): Listener for an event the widget does not declare
SYG141.summary: The intent listens for an event on a widget's host (`DOM.select('.due').events('pikc')`, or a widget control: `DOM.select(Due).events('pikc')`) that the widget doesn't list in its `events`, that no element fires natively, and that is a near-typo of a declared event, so the action most likely never fires. sygnal-check resolves the selector through the static `className` and `id` of the elements the component's own view renders: it reports only when every element with that class or id is a widget host and the widgets' `events` are literal lists.
SYG141.note:
Fix: Listen for the declared event the name is close to (`DOM.select('.due').events('pick').detail()`), or add the name to the widget's `events` and dispatch it from `mount()`. On a Select or Combobox: `DOM.select('.size').events('value-change').detail()`; on a Menu: `events('select')`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG141

SYG142.title: SYG142 (error): Widget command not declared
SYG142.summary: An element command (`ELEMENT: { open: '.due' }`) reached a widget's host, but the widget declares no command of that name and the host element has no such method, so it can't run (for a non-widget element this is SYG641). The message lists the commands the widget declares. A widget's declared command wins over a native method of the same name (`focus` runs the widget's `focus`; `close` and `togglePopover` too, with the options object). The dev entry reports it when the command reaches the element.
SYG142.note:
Fix: Send one of the widget's commands, or add the command to its definition: `defineWidget({ commands: { open: (instance, options) => instance.open() } })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG142

SYG143.title: SYG143 (warn): Widget tag used as a selector
SYG143.summary: The tag `defineWidget()` returned was used where a selector is expected: `DOM.select(DatePicker)`, `DOM.click(DatePicker)`, `ELEMENT: { open: DatePicker }` or inside a template string. A widget tag is a JSX tag, not a selector (several hosts of the same widget may render), so it matches nothing and the action never fires. The dev entry reports it once per widget; sygnal-check reports it for intent selectors and element command targets.
SYG143.note:
Fix: Give the widget a `className` and select that: `<DatePicker className="due" />` with `DOM.select('.due').events('pick')` and `ELEMENT: { open: '.due' }`. Or make it a control (the alternative form): `const { Due } = controls({ Due: DatePicker })`, then `DOM.select(Due)` and `{ open: Due }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG143

SYG144.title: SYG144 (info): Widget event the host element also fires natively
SYG144.summary: A widget declares an event whose name the browser also uses (`'change'`, `'input'`, `'select'`, `'toggle'`...). Native events of that name fire on the host or bubble up from inside it (flatpickr's own input fires `change` as well), so a listener on the host gets both the widget's `CustomEvent` and the native event, and `.detail()` is `undefined` for the native one. Information only: it may be what you want. The dev entry reports it once per widget when a host mounts (names the host element knows as `on<name>`); sygnal-check reports the literal `events` entries it recognises.
SYG144.note:
Fix: Give the widget's event its own name (`'pick'` for a date picker's selection, `'rate'` for a rating) and emit that, or make the listener handle both (`.filter((e) => e instanceof CustomEvent)`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG144

SYG145.title: SYG145 (warn): Sortable item without its id attribute
SYG145.summary: The `sortable` behavior finds the item a pointer press or a key is on with `event.target.closest(item)` and reads its id from the item element's `attr` attribute (`data-id` by default), then looks that id up in `state[from]` (by `idField`, `id` by default). An item element without the attribute can't be matched to an entry of the list, so the press or key is ignored and the item can't be moved. Usually the item renders its id under another attribute name, or the `item` selector matches an element inside the one that carries the id. Reported once per `item` selector, at the first press or key on such an item.
SYG145.note:
Fix: Render the id on the item element (`<li className="task" data-id={state.id}>`), point `item` at the element that carries it, or name the attribute: `sortable({ from: 'tasks', item: '.task', attr: 'data-key' })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG145

SYG146.title: SYG146 (warn): Sortable item or handle selector matches nothing
SYG146.summary: At the host's first pointer press or key press, the `sortable` behavior checks its selectors against what the host rendered (its children and Collection items included): `item` is reported when elements carry the id attribute (`attr`) but none matches `item`, and `handle` when items exist but none contains an element matching `handle`. Either way no item can be picked up, by pointer or keyboard. An empty list can't tell a typo from no items, so the check waits for a later interaction. Reported once per selector.
SYG146.note:
Fix: Use the selector of the elements the items render: `item: '.task'` for `<li className="task" data-id={id}>`, `handle: '.grip'` for the drag handle inside it, or leave `handle` out to drag the whole item.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG146

SYG147.title: SYG147 (warn): Sortable list key is not an array in the host state
SYG147.summary: `sortable({ from })` reorders `state[from]` (each key of an array `from` for moves between lists). When the host starts, a `from` key whose value is missing or not an array is reported: nothing in it can be found, so no item can be moved. The message suggests a close array key of the state when there is one. Reported once per key; a list that arrives later should start as an empty array.
SYG147.note:
Fix: Name the array in the host's state (`from: 'tasks'` for `initialState: { tasks: [...] }`), and start a list that is loaded later as `[]`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG147

SYG148.title: SYG148 (warn): Collection viewTransitionName is not a CSS identifier
SYG148.summary: A `<Collection>` or `<VirtualCollection>` has a `viewTransitionName` that is not a string starting a CSS identifier (a letter, `_`, `-` followed by a letter or `_`, or `--`; then letters, digits, `-` and `_`). Each item's name is `<prefix>-<id>`, so with a prefix such as `'1card'`, `'my card'` or `'card.x'` every name is invalid CSS: the browser ignores the `view-transition-name` and nothing animates, with no error. The dev entry reports it once per component and prefix when the Collection renders. An empty string, `0` or `false` names no item and is not reported.
SYG148.note:
Fix: Use a CSS identifier as the prefix: `viewTransitionName="card"` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`, not starting with a digit). The ids are escaped for you.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG148

SYG149.title: SYG149 (warn): Two items with the same view-transition name
SYG149.summary: After a render, two rendered elements on the page (not in a `display: none` subtree, such as a hidden tab panel: the browser doesn't capture those) have the same `view-transition-name` from Collections with the same `viewTransitionName` prefix: the same item `id` is in two of them at once (an 'All' list and a 'Favorites' list both named `card`). A name must be unique when a View Transition starts, so the browser skips the whole transition (Chromium logs `Unexpected duplicate view-transition-name`). The same prefix on several Collections is meant for one item moving between them, never shown in two at once.
SYG149.note:
Fix: Give Collections that can show the same item at the same time different prefixes (`viewTransitionName="all"` and `viewTransitionName="fav"`), or set the item's own `style={{ viewTransitionName }}` where it needs one.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG149

SYG150.title: SYG150 (warn): Agent action has no model entry
SYG150.summary: A component's `agent` declaration (sygnal/ai) lists an action under `actions` that the component's `model` has no entry for (and no behavior of its `uses` owns). The agent layer offers it as a tool, and every call dispatches an action nothing handles, so the call fails with "changed nothing" and the model retries or gives up. Usually a typo, or an entry renamed on one side only. sygnal-check reports it when the declaration and the model are object literals it can read (no spreads), and suggests the closest model entry. TypeScript catches it only when every key is wrong.
SYG150.note:
Fix: Rename the key to the model entry it means (`actions: { ADD: { description: 'Add a todo', input } }` for `model.ADD`), or add the model entry: `TodoApp.model = { ..., ADD: (state, text) => ({ ...state, todos: [...state.todos, { id: state.nextId, text }] }) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG150

SYG151.title: SYG151 (warn): Misspelled agent static
SYG151.summary: A component has a static named like the agent declaration but spelled differently: `agents`, `tools`, `Agent`, `tool`. The agent layer (the chat behavior, WebMCP, the command bar, `t.tools()`) reads only `Component.agent`, so the component offers no tools and its `read` projection never reaches the model, without any error. Reported on a component (a function with other Sygnal statics) or on an object with `actions` or `read`.
SYG151.note:
Fix: Rename the static: `TodoApp.agent = { name: 'todos', description: 'The todo list', read: (state) => ({ todos: state.todos }), actions: { ADD: { description: 'Add a todo', input: z.string() } } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG151

SYG152.title: SYG152 (warn): LLM request without an ok action
SYG152.summary: A model sends an LLM request (an object with `messages`, sent to the chat driver of sygnal/ai) that names no `ok` reply action. The driver delivers the finished reply (the assistant `message`, its `text`, `toolCalls`, `finishReason` and `usage`) only as the `ok` action, so the reply is lost: a `delta` action shows the text while it streams, but the final message never reaches the state and the status never leaves streaming. sygnal-check follows requests that local helpers build; a request with a spread (`{ ...base, messages }`) is not reported, since the spread may name `ok`.
SYG152.note:
