Fix: Name the actions the reply arrives as, and handle them: `LLM: (state) => ({ messages: state.messages, delta: 'DELTA', ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' })` with `DONE: (state, { message }) => ({ ...state, messages: [...state.messages, message], draft: '' })`. For a whole conversation with tools, the `chat` behavior does this for you.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG152

SYG153.title: SYG153 (warn): WebMCP form attribute set as a DOM property
SYG153.summary: A `<form>` has `toolname`, `tooldescription` or `toolautosubmit` (or a field has `toolparamdescription`) written as a plain JSX attribute. WebMCP's declarative API reads these as HTML attributes, but Sygnal's JSX pragma turns an attribute it doesn't know into a DOM property (`form.toolname = ...`), which the browser ignores: the form is never offered to the browser's agent, and nothing reports it at run time.
SYG153.note:
Fix: For a form with the `form` behavior, give it a tool and let it write every attribute: `form(schema, { values, submit: 'SIGN_UP', tool: formTool({ name: 'sign_up', description: 'Create an account' }) })` with `formTool` from `sygnal/ai` (experimental; each field's `<label>`, then its `aria-label`, becomes its `toolparamdescription`). Otherwise write them as attributes: `<form attrs-toolname="sign_up" attrs-tooldescription="Create an account">` and `<input name="email" attrs-toolparamdescription="The email to sign up with" />` (or `attrs={{ toolname: 'sign_up' }}`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG153

SYG160.title: SYG160 (warn): Result part rendered outside a card
SYG160.summary: A part declared with `result: true` in `defineCatalog({ parts })` (sygnal/ai) answers a card: the `chat` behavior's `ask_user` tool shows a card built from the catalog, and the result part sends `compose.answer(props, value)` to PARENT, which the chat hears with `CHILD.select` and turns into the tool call's output. The answer names the card by `props.scope`, the tool call id that `askCard(catalog, state, part)` passes to `catalog.render`. Here a result part was rendered with no scope (by a `compose` page, or by `catalog.render` called without `scope`), so its answer has nowhere to go: no tool call waits for it.
SYG160.note:
Fix: Render cards with `askCard(catalog, state, part)` for each `tool-ask_user` part of the chat's messages. On a composed page, use a part without `result: true`, or a separate catalog for the page and for the cards.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG160

SYG161.title: SYG161 (error): Catalog container render is a component with a model
SYG161.summary: A container in `defineCatalog({ containers })` (sygnal/ai) is a view function: `catalog.render()` calls its `render` inline with `{ key, node, slots, children, ui, control }`, so the composed parts stay children of the component that renders the composition. Its `render` here is a component (it has a `model`, `intent`, `initialState` or `uses`). A component would own the parts placed in its slots: the host's `CHILD.select(Part)` would stop hearing them, their lenses would start from the container's state, and a part moved out of it would be re-created. The function is still called as a view, so its model, intent and state never run.
SYG161.note:
Fix: Make `render` a plain function of its argument (`render: ({ children, ui, control }) => <Tabs ...>`), and keep container state in `ui` with `control(name, value)` (a click on the element sets `ui[key][name]`). Put stateful UI inside a part instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG161

SYG162.title: SYG162 (error): Catalog part with neither component nor render
SYG162.summary: Every part in `defineCatalog({ parts })` (sygnal/ai) needs something to render: a `component` (a Sygnal component, rendered as a child of the host with its lens, params and props) or a `render` view function (called inline with the same props). This part has neither, usually a misspelled key or an import that resolved to undefined. It stays in the catalog, so layouts that name it are valid, but it renders nothing. Reported in development, when the catalog is defined; `sygnal-check` reports a literal part declaration (without a spread) that has neither key.
SYG162.note:
Fix: Add `component: MyPart` (check the import) or `render: (props) =>
…
`. More: sygnal-check explain SYG162

SYG170.title: SYG170 (warn): Context field read with no provider
SYG170.summary: A component reads `context.theme` (in its view, or in a reducer through `props.context`), but neither it nor any component above it has `theme` in its `.context`, so the value is `undefined`. Context flows down the render tree: a component sees what it and its ancestors declare. sygnal-check follows every way up from the reader and reports only when each ends at a component that `run()` or `defineElement()` starts, so it knows the whole chain.
SYG170.note:
Fix: Add the field to the `.context` of the reader or a component above it: `App.context = { theme: (state) => state.theme }`. If the name is misspelled (the message suggests the closest one on the chain), fix the read.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG170

SYG171.title: SYG171 (warn): PARENT sink no parent reads
SYG171.summary: A component's model sends to `PARENT`, but none of the components that render it reads `CHILD.select(It)` in its intent. A `PARENT` value reaches only the component that renders it, through `CHILD.select`, so here every value goes nowhere and the click does nothing. sygnal-check reports it when the parents render it by tag, as a Collection item or as a Switchable target, no scanned intent selects it (a select in the wrong component is SYG129), and it can read every parent's intent: one with `uses` (a behavior may read `CHILD`), a sources rest pattern, `CHILD` passed to a helper, or a `CHILD.select()` it can't resolve keeps it silent.
SYG171.note:
Fix: Read it in the parent's intent and handle it in the model: `App.intent = ({ CHILD }) => ({ PICK: CHILD.select(Badge) })` with `App.model = { PICK: (state, data) => ... }`. If nothing needs the value, remove the `PARENT` sink; for components further apart, use `EVENTS`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG171

SYG201.title: SYG201 (warn): STATE reducer dropped keys from the previous state
SYG201.summary: A STATE reducer returned a plain object that is missing keys present (and not `undefined`) in the previous state, which usually means a missing `...state` spread. Those keys are silently lost from state. Calculated fields, `INITIALIZE` and internal `__*` actions are excluded; reported once per component and action.
SYG201.note:
Fix: Spread the previous state: `(state, data) => ({ ...state, field: data })`. If removing the keys is intended, ignore the warning.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG201

SYG202.title: SYG202 (warn): STATE reducer returned undefined
SYG202.summary: A STATE reducer returned `undefined`, typically from a block-bodied arrow function without `return`. In a root component this wipes the state (a warning). Returning `undefined` from a Collection item's reducer is the documented way to remove the item, so it is not reported there; in another sub-component (a child rendered by tag) it is reported as info. `INITIALIZE` and internal `__*` actions are excluded.
SYG202.note:
Fix: Return the new state, e.g. `(state, data) => ({ ...state, ... })`, or return `ABORT` to leave the state unchanged.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG202

SYG204.title: SYG204 (warn): Root component has no state, so its view never renders
SYG204.summary: The core calls a component's view only while its state is defined. A root component gets its first state from `initialState`, from an `INITIALIZE` reducer, or, with no model at all, renders without one. A root that has a model but no `initialState` starts with `undefined` state, so nothing is rendered: no error, an empty page, and a `DOM.click()` intent that can never fire because its element never appears. Generated code that has no data of its own often looks like this.
SYG204.note:
Fix: Give the root an `initialState`, `App.initialState = {}` when it has no data of its own, or return the first state from an `INITIALIZE` reducer. To show a loading state before data arrives, start from one (`{ loading: true }`) rather than from no state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG204

SYG206.title: SYG206 (error): Invalid calculated field definition
SYG206.summary: An entry in `calculated` is neither a function nor a two-element `[deps, fn]` array where `deps` is an array and `fn` is a function. The component constructor throws, so the component is never created.
SYG206.note:
Fix: Define each field as `state => value` or `[['a', 'b'], state => value]`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG206

SYG207.title: SYG207 (warn): Calculated field shadows an initialState key
SYG207.summary: A key in `calculated` also exists in `initialState`. The calculated value overwrites the stored value of the same name, so the `initialState` value is never visible. Checked once when the component is constructed.
SYG207.note:
Fix: Rename either the calculated field or the `initialState` key.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG207

SYG208.title: SYG208 (warn): Calculated field depends on an unknown key
SYG208.summary: A calculated field declared as `[deps, fn]` lists a dependency that is neither another calculated field nor a key of `initialState`. The dependency is likely misspelled, so memoization compares an always-`undefined` value. Only checked when the component has an `initialState`.
SYG208.note:
Fix: Fix the dependency name, or add the key to `initialState`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG208

SYG209.title: SYG209 (error): Circular calculated field dependency
SYG209.summary: Calculated fields declared with `[deps, fn]` depend on each other in a cycle (the message shows the path, e.g. `a -> b -> a`), so no evaluation order exists. The component constructor throws.
SYG209.note:
Fix: Break the cycle so that each calculated field depends only on state keys or on fields that do not depend back on it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG209

SYG210.title: SYG210 (warn): INITIALIZE used with a sink other than STATE
SYG210.summary: The model defines `INITIALIZE` as an object with sinks other than the state sink (e.g. `EVENTS` or `EFFECT`). `INITIALIZE` only supports the state sink, so those other sink entries are deleted and never run.
SYG210.note:
Fix: Keep only `STATE` under `INITIALIZE` and move the other sinks to a different action (for example one triggered by `BOOTSTRAP` or via `next()`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG210

SYG211.title: SYG211 (error): Retired in 6.0: Invalid model shorthand entry
SYG211.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it was thrown for a malformed `'ACTION | SINK'` model key (one that did not split into an action and a sink). Sygnal 6.0 removed those keys (the object form is the only form), so there is nothing to split; a removed key is reported as SYG612 (dev) and SYG504 (`sygnal-check --strict`).
SYG211.note:
Fix: Use the object form: `SAVE: { EFFECT: (state, data, next) => … }`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#pipe-keys.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG211

SYG212.title: SYG212 (error): Model entry is not a function or an object of sinks
SYG212.summary: A model entry's value is neither a function (a STATE reducer) nor a plain object mapping sink names to reducers; for example a string, number, array or `null`. Model setup throws when the component is initialized.
SYG212.note:
Fix: Use a reducer function or a sink map, e.g. `{ STATE: (state) => ..., EVENTS: ... }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG212

SYG213.title: SYG213 (warn): Retired in 6.0: Duplicate model entry for the same action and sink
SYG213.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it warned when an `'ACTION | SINK'` key and an object-form entry defined the same action and sink. With the shorthand keys removed in 6.0, an action/sink pair can be defined only once.
SYG213.note:
Fix: Nothing to change. Use one object-form entry per action: `SAVE: { STATE: …, EFFECT: … }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG213

SYG214.title: SYG214 (error): EFFECT handler threw
SYG214.summary: A model entry on the `EFFECT` sink threw an exception. The error is caught and logged with `console.error` (with the original error attached) rather than thrown, so the app keeps running but the effect did not complete. In diagnostics `error` mode the diagnostic is rethrown asynchronously. If the exception is itself a coded Sygnal error (for example SYG215 from `next()`), it is reported under that code instead.
SYG214.note:
Fix: Fix the exception shown in the attached error, or guard the handler against missing state or data.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG214

SYG215.title: SYG215 (error): next() delay is not a number
SYG215.summary: The third argument of `next(type, data, delay)` was given and is not a number. `next()` throws and the follow-up action is not dispatched. When it is called inside a reducer or EFFECT handler, the handler catches the throw and reports it under this code (not SYG216 or SYG214), so a STATE reducer leaves the state unchanged and a driver-sink reducer sends nothing.
SYG215.note:
Fix: Pass a number of milliseconds, or omit it for the default 10 ms: `next('ACTION', data, 100)`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG215

SYG216.title: SYG216 (error): Reducer threw
SYG216.summary: A model reducer threw an exception. For a STATE reducer the error is logged and the state is left unchanged; for a driver sink (e.g. `EVENTS`, `PARENT`, custom drivers) it is logged and nothing is sent. The error is logged with `console.error` rather than thrown (rethrown asynchronously in diagnostics `error` mode). A coded Sygnal error thrown inside the reducer (for example SYG215 from `next()`) is reported under its own code instead.
SYG216.note:
Fix: Fix the exception shown in the attached error, or guard the reducer against missing state or data.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG216

SYG217.title: SYG217 (warn): Driver-sink reducer returned undefined
SYG217.summary: A reducer for a non-STATE sink (e.g. `EVENTS`, `PARENT` or a custom driver) returned `undefined`, often from a missing `return`. The `undefined` value is still sent to the driver.
SYG217.note:
Fix: Return the value the driver expects, or return `ABORT` to send nothing.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG217

SYG218.title: SYG218 (error): Reducer returned an unsupported type
SYG218.summary: A reducer for a non-STATE sink (e.g. `EVENTS`, `PARENT` or a custom driver) returned a symbol other than `ABORT`. Any other value, including `null`, arrays and bigints, is sent to the driver as-is, like a constant sink value. It is logged with `console.error` (not thrown) and nothing is sent.
SYG218.note:
Fix: Return the value the driver expects, or return `ABORT` to send nothing.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG218

SYG219.title: SYG219 (warn): EFFECT handler returned a value
SYG219.summary: An `EFFECT` handler returned something other than `undefined`. EFFECT entries run only for side effects, so the return value is ignored; this usually means the logic was meant for a STATE or driver sink. Returning `ABORT` from an EFFECT also triggers it.
SYG219.note:
Fix: Do not return a value from EFFECT handlers; move value-producing logic to a `STATE` or driver sink entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG219

SYG220.title: SYG220 (warn): Calculated field threw
SYG220.summary: A calculated field function threw while computing derived state, for example by reading a property of missing data. The error is caught and the field is skipped for that update, so it is not recomputed from the new state.
SYG220.note:
Fix: Guard the calculation against missing data, e.g. `state => state.user?.name ?? ''`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG220

SYG221.title: SYG221 (error): set() called with a string
SYG221.summary: `set()` takes an object to merge (`set({ open: true })`) or a function that returns one (`set((state, data) => ({ ... }))`). Called with a field name, `set('city')` spreads the string into the state, adding the keys `'0'`, `'1'`, ... one per character, and the field itself never changes. The dev entry recognises those keys after the reducer runs and reports the field name; TypeScript also rejects a string argument.
SYG221.note:
Fix: To store the action data in a field, pass a function: `set((state, city) => ({ city }))`. For a fixed value pass an object: `set({ city: 'Paris' })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG221

SYG222.title: SYG222 (warn): STATE reducer returned the same object after it was mutated in place
SYG222.summary: A STATE reducer changed the state object it received (`state.count++`, `state.done = true`, `delete state.x`) and returned that same object. Since 6.0 a reducer that returns the object it got means "no change" (the same as `ABORT`), so the change is ignored: no state is emitted and nothing re-renders. The dev entry takes a shallow snapshot of the state (its keys and top-level values) before each STATE reducer runs and compares it when the reducer returns the same object; the report names the changed keys. Mutations below the top level (`state.items.push(x)`) are not seen. In production the mutation is silently ignored.
SYG222.note:
Fix: Return a new object: `INC: (state) => ({ ...state, count: state.count + 1 })`. To write updates as mutations, wrap the reducer in immer's `produce()`: `INC: produce((draft) => { draft.count++ })`, which returns a new object when something changed and the same object when nothing did.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG222

SYG223.title: SYG223 (warn): persist pick or omit names a key that is not in initialState
SYG223.summary: `App.persist = persist({ key, pick, omit })` saves the top-level state keys listed in `pick` (or every key except those in `omit`). A name in either list that is not a key of the component's `initialState` (or of its `uses`: a behavior's slice, such as `chat`, is a state key too) is usually a typo or a renamed key: with `pick` that key is never saved (and never restored), with `omit` the key you meant to leave out is saved after all. The dev entry reports it when the root component is created; sygnal-check reports it statically when the options and `initialState` are literals, with the closest key as a suggestion.
SYG223.note:
Fix: Use top-level keys of `initialState` or `uses`: `persist({ key: 'todo-app', pick: ['todos', 'filter'] })`, or add the key to `initialState`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG223

SYG224.title: SYG224 (error): persist on a component that is not the root
SYG224.summary: `persist({ ... })` is set up by the root component only (the one passed to `run()` or `renderComponent()`): it saves and restores the app's whole state tree, and a sub-component's state is a slice of it. On any other component the `persist` static is ignored, so nothing is saved or restored. In Vike, a Page, Layout or Wrapper rendered in the Layout/Wrapper shell is a sub-component (the shell is the app's root), so `persist` isn't supported there yet, and the message says so; a Vike page with no Layout or Wrapper is its own root, where `persist` works. The dev entry reports it when the component is created;
SYG224.note:
Fix: Move `persist` to the root component and `pick` the key that holds the sub-component's state: `App.persist = persist({ key: 'app', pick: ['todos'] })` for a child rendered with `state="todos"`. In a Vike Layout/Wrapper shell, remove it and save the state yourself (`STATE.watch` writing to `localStorage`, read back in `BOOTSTRAP`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG224

SYG226.title: SYG226 (warn): Undo track, resetOn or coalesce names an unknown action
SYG226.summary: `undoable(model, { key, track, resetOn, coalesce })` (and the `undo({ ... })` behavior) records changes to `state[key]` made by the actions in `track`, clears the history on the actions in `resetOn`, and groups quick repeats of the actions in `coalesce` into one step. A name in any of these lists that has no model entry never runs, so with `track` its changes are never recorded (undo skips them), with `resetOn` the history is never cleared (after a load, undo would bring back the old document), and with `coalesce` the action meant to be grouped (typing) is recorded one step per change. It is usually a typo or a renamed action.
SYG226.note:
Fix: Use the name of a model entry (`track: ['TYPE']`, `resetOn: ['LOADED']`, `coalesce: ['TYPE']`), or add the entry to the model. Leave `track` out to record every action that changes `state[key]`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG226

SYG230.title: SYG230 (warn): Form field name not in values
SYG230.summary: The `form` behavior hears `input` and `focusout` on its form element and reads the event target's `name` as a path in `values` (`email`, `addresses.7.city` for the row with id 7). A named field inside the form whose name is not a field of `values` is ignored: its value never reaches `state.form` and it is never validated. It is usually a typo, a renamed field, a row name built with the index instead of the row's `id`, or an input that belongs to something else (a search box) placed inside the form element. Reported once per name, on `input`;
SYG230.note:
Fix: Name the input after a path in `values` (`name="email"`, or `name={f.email.name}` from `state.form.fields`), add the field to `values`, or move the unrelated input out of the form element. For a field that appears at run time, name it in the `dynamic` option with its start value: `dynamic: (state) => Object.fromEntries(state.lines.map((key) => [key, { amount: '', currency: 'USD' }]))` makes `${key}.amount` a field while the line is there.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG230

SYG231.title: SYG231 (error): form() schema is not a Standard Schema
SYG231.summary: `form(schema, options)` validates with any Standard Schema (https://standardschema.dev): an object with `~standard.validate`, which zod (3.24+), valibot (1.0+), arktype and others provide. Anything else (a plain object of rules, a validator function, an older library's schema with only `parse`) can't validate, so `form()` throws when it is called, with this code in dev; in production the first validation throws a plain TypeError.
SYG231.note:
Fix: Pass a Standard Schema object: `form(z.object({ email: z.string().email() }), { ... })`, `form(v.object({ ... }), { ... })`, or a hand-written `{ '~standard': { version: 1, vendor: 'app', validate: (values) => ({ value }) | ({ issues: [{ message, path }] }) } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG231

SYG232.title: SYG232 (info): Form submit dropped while one is in progress
SYG232.summary: A `form.SUBMIT` (the form element's submit, or `simulateAction('form.SUBMIT')`) arrived while `state.form.submitting` was true (a valid submit sent its request and neither `form.DONE` nor `form.ERRORS` has answered it), or while a submit was queued waiting for an async `check` or an async schema. The form drops it, so a double click never sends twice. Only a submit whose model entry sends on the HTTP sink (the `http` option) stays `submitting`; any other submit is done at once.
SYG232.note:
Fix: Disable the submit button while `state.form.submitting` is true, and answer the submit action with reply actions: `SIGN_UP: { HTTP: (state, values) => ({ url, json: values, ok: 'form.DONE', error: 'form.ERRORS' }) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG232

SYG233.title: SYG233 (warn): Form value missing from the schema output
SYG233.summary: On a valid submit the form dispatches the `submit` action with the schema's output (trimmed, transformed values), not with `state.form.values`. A top-level key of `values` that the output doesn't have was stripped (or renamed) by the schema, usually because the schema doesn't declare it (`z.object()` and `v.object()` drop unknown keys), so the submit action never gets that field. Reported once per key, and only when every key of the output is a key of `values`: an output with keys of its own comes from a schema that reshapes the values (a `transform` that renames), which is left alone.
SYG233.note:
Fix: Declare the field in the schema, make the schema keep unknown keys (`z.looseObject`, `v.looseObject`), or remove the field from `values` if it isn't part of the form.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG233

SYG234.title: SYG234 (warn): Form submit action has no model entry
SYG234.summary: `form(schema, { submit: 'SIGN_UP' })` dispatches the host action named by `submit` with the schema's output when a submit is valid. (With `request: { url }` the form sends the valid submit itself and `submit` is optional.) When neither option is given, or the host component has no model entry named by `submit`, a valid submit does nothing visible (the form marks it done, `submitted: true`, and nothing else happens).
SYG234.note:
Fix: To save to a URL, give the form a request: `form(schema, { values, request: { url: '/api/signup' } })`. Otherwise name a host action the form doesn't define and add it to the model: `submit: 'SIGN_UP'` with `SIGN_UP: { HTTP: (state, values) => ({ url: '/api/signup', method: 'POST', json: values, ok: 'form.DONE', error: 'form.ERRORS' }) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG234

SYG235.title: SYG235 (warn): Form check names an unknown field or sets reply fields
SYG235.summary: `check: { email: { request, error } }` runs an async check for a field through a driver: the form sends `request(value)` with its own reply action (`ok`/`error` set to `'form.CHECKED_email'`) and `latest: true`, so a newer value's check replaces an older one. A `check` key that isn't a field of `values` never runs (reported when the component is created; not with the `dynamic` option, whose fields may include it), and a request that sets `ok`, `error` or `latest` has them replaced by the form's (reported when the check runs).
SYG235.note:
Fix: Use a field name from `values` as the key, and return only the request from `request`: `check: { email: { request: (email) => ({ url: '/api/email-free', query: { email } }), error: (body) => !body.free && 'Taken' } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG235

SYG236.title: SYG236 (warn): Form array rows without an id
SYG236.summary: Field arrays name their fields by row id (`addresses.7.city`), so errors, touched state, server errors and focus stay with a row when another row is removed. An array of objects in `values` whose rows have no `id` falls back to the index, and after a removal the next row inherits the removed row's errors and touched state. `form.ADD` gives new rows the next id itself; the start values need ids too. Reported when the component is created.
SYG236.note:
Fix: Give each row a unique `id` in `values`: `addresses: [{ id: 1, street: '', city: '' }]`, render rows with a Collection, and name their inputs `addresses.${state.id}.city`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG236

SYG237.title: SYG237 (warn): Two forms in one component listen on the same form selector
SYG237.summary: Each `form` behavior hears `input`, `focusout` and `submit` on its form element, found by the `form` option inside the host component (default `'form'`). Two `form` uses in one component with the same selector (both left at the default, usually) both match every form element of the view, so typing in one form changes the other's values too (when the names overlap) and each submit is handled by both. Reported when the component is created.
SYG237.note:
Fix: Give each form element its own class and pass it as the `form` option: `uses = { login: form(loginSchema, { ..., form: '.login' }), news: form(newsSchema, { ..., form: '.news' }) }` with `<form className="login">` and `<form className="news">`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG237

SYG238.title: SYG238 (warn): Root component with a model but no initial state
SYG238.summary: A root component (the one passed to `run()` or `renderComponent()`) has a `model` but no `initialState`, so its state is `undefined` and its view doesn't run: the page (or the test's `t.html()`) stays empty until an action sets the whole state. A root without a model renders anyway (from `initialState`, or with no state), and a child gets its state from its parent, so neither is reported. The state may also come from `renderComponent(C, { initialState })` or an HMR swap; then nothing is reported either. Reported once per component.
SYG238.note:
Fix: Give the root its start state: `App.initialState = { count: 0 }`. If the state really arrives later (from a request), start from a placeholder such as `{ status: 'loading' }` and render that.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG238

SYG239.title: SYG239 (warn): Form schema function returns a new schema for the same state
SYG239.summary: `form((state) => schema, options)` validates with a schema that depends on the host's state (which fields are required depends on what is on the form). The form calls the function whenever it validates and caches each result per schema object, and it re-validates whenever the function returns another schema.
SYG239.note:
Fix: Return the same schema object while the rules don't change: memoize it on the part of the state it reads, not on the whole state. For a schema built from a list or a layout in state, cache it per that object: `const schemas = new WeakMap(); const schemaOf = (state) => { if (!schemas.has(state.lines)) schemas.set(state.lines, build(state.lines)); return schemas.get(state.lines) }`, then `form(schemaOf, { ... })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG239

SYG240.title: SYG240 (error): Agent action or query input has no JSON Schema form
SYG240.summary: An `agent.actions` or `agent.queries` entry's `input` must be a Standard Schema that also implements Standard JSON Schema (Zod 4.2+, ArkType 2.1.28+, Valibot wrapped with `toStandardJsonSchema()` from `@valibot/to-json-schema`), or a plain JSON Schema wrapped with `jsonSchema()` from `sygnal/ai`. The agent layer sends the model the input-side JSON Schema and validates every call with the schema before the action or query runs.
SYG240.note:
Fix: Use a supported schema: `input: z.string().min(1)`, `input: toStandardJsonSchema(v.picklist(['all', 'done']))`, or `input: jsonSchema({ type: 'integer' })`. For Zod Mini keep its validation with `jsonSchema(z.toJSONSchema(s), { validate: s })`. A `Date` can't come from JSON, and Zod's JSON Schema conversion throws for `z.date()` and `z.coerce.date()` alike (the field reaches the model with no schema, SYG243): take an ISO string, `z.iso.datetime()` (convert it in the reducer) or `z.iso.datetime().transform((s) => new Date(s))` (the model sees the string, the action gets a `Date`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG240

SYG241.title: SYG241 (error): Agent read, query, when, until or label threw
SYG241.summary: The agent layer calls a component's `agent.read(state)` (the projection an agent sees), each action's and query's `when(state)` (whether the tool is offered) and `agent.label(state)` (a Collection item's label) with the instance's current state, once per state change, a query's `run(state, input)` when an agent calls it, and an action's `until(state)` while its call waits. One of them threw.
SYG241.note:
Fix: Make the function total over every state the component can have: guard optional fields (`state.todos?.length ?? 0`), and keep it a pure function of the state it gets.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG241

SYG242.title: SYG242 (warn): WebMCP tool over a size budget
SYG242.summary: `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` keeps every tool inside Chrome's WebMCP budgets, which neither Chrome 153 nor the polyfill enforce: a tool name of at most 30 characters, a description of at most 500, a parameter description of at most 150, and a result of at most 1,500 characters of JSON. Something went over, and it was cut so the agent still gets a usable tool: a long name keeps its first 25 characters plus `_` and a 4-character hash of the whole (so names stay unique), a description or parameter description ends in `…`, and a long result keeps `ok` and `error`, gets `truncated: true`, and carries its `state` as a cut JSON string.
SYG242.note:
Fix: Shorten the `agent` declaration's `name`, the action names or the `description` texts, or make `read` return a smaller projection (counts and the fields an agent needs, not the whole state). A Collection item tool's key description lists every item's label: a shorter `label` keeps more of them.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG242

SYG243.title: SYG243 (warn): Agent action or query input schema converted with losses
SYG243.summary: Part of an `agent.actions` or `agent.queries` entry's `input` has no JSON Schema form, for example a refinement (Valibot `check`, ArkType `narrow`) or a `Date`, so the library's lossy conversion left it out of the schema the model gets. The model doesn't see that rule, so it may send values that break it; the layer still validates every call with the full schema and returns the issues to the model. Zod drops refinements without saying so, so no warning is possible there. Reported once per action or query.
SYG243.note:
Fix: Put the rule in the description the model reads (`.describe('at least 2 characters, must contain @')`), or express it with a JSON Schema keyword (`minLength`, `pattern`, `enum`) instead of a refinement. For a date, take an ISO string and convert it in the reducer: `z.iso.datetime()` (Zod), `v.pipe(v.string(), v.isoDateTime())` (Valibot), `'string.date.iso'` (ArkType).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG243

SYG244.title: SYG244 (warn): Agent read returns strings, untrusted not declared
SYG244.summary: WebMCP marks a tool whose results may carry text from users (or other untrusted sources) with `untrustedContentHint`, so the agent treats that text as data, not instructions. `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` takes the hint from the declaration's `untrusted` field.
SYG244.note:
Fix: Declare it: `untrusted: true` when `read` returns user-entered text (todo texts, names, messages), `untrusted: false` when its strings are only the app's own (enum values, labels the app wrote).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG244

SYG245.title: SYG245 (error): form tool option is not made by formTool()
SYG245.summary: `form(schema, { tool })` (experimental, ) offers the form to the browser's agent as a declarative WebMCP tool, but only when `tool` is made by `formTool({ name, description, autosubmit })` from `sygnal/ai`. The tool code lives in `formTool` so that apps using `form` without a tool don't carry it; the form behavior only calls the hook on the object it is given. A plain `{ name, description }` object has no such hook: the form works as before but writes no `toolname` attributes and answers no agent. Reported once, in development.
SYG245.note:
Fix: Wrap the object: `import { formTool } from 'sygnal/ai'`, then `form(schema, { values, submit: 'SIGN_UP', tool: formTool({ name: 'sign_up', description: 'Create an account' }) })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG245

SYG246.title: SYG246 (error): Agent query is not a synchronous function
SYG246.summary: An `agent.queries` entry is a read-only tool: its `run(state, input)` gets the component's current state and the validated input and returns the result the model sees, as `{ ok: true, result }`. It runs outside the action queue, so it must be a pure, synchronous function of what it gets: it can't wait for a request, and nothing it does reaches the app's state. This one is not: `run` is missing or not a function (the query is not offered), or it returned a promise (an `async` function, or one that calls `fetch`), so the call fails with `{ ok: false, error }`. Reported once per query while an agent layer runs.
SYG246.note:
Fix: Compute the result from `state` and `input` and return it: `run: (state, { customer }) => state.invoices.filter((i) => i.customer === customer)`. For data that has to be fetched, use an action instead: its model entry sets what to load (a `resources` entry or a driver request), and `until: 'resourceName'` on the action makes the call answer with the component's `read` once the data has arrived.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG246

SYG247.title: SYG247 (warn): Agent query has the tool name of an action
SYG247.summary: Actions and queries of one `agent` declaration share its tool-name space: each becomes the tool `<name>_<key>`, with the key in snake case (`FIND` and `find` both give `orders_find`). This query's tool name is already taken by one of the declaration's actions, so the action keeps it and the query is not offered. Reported once per query while an agent layer runs; sygnal-check reports it before the app runs.
SYG247.note:
Fix: Rename the query so its key names what it returns (`queries: { search: … }` next to an action `FIND`), or remove the duplicate.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG247

SYG248.title: SYG248 (warn): Agent action until names no resource
SYG248.summary: An `agent.actions` entry's `until` makes the call wait for the action's result: a string names one of the component's `resources`, and the call answers once that resource is neither loading nor refreshing. This string names no resource of the component (a typo, a resource declared on another component, or a component with no `resources`), so there is nothing to wait for: the call answers at once, with the state right after the action, as without `until`. Reported once per action while an agent layer runs; sygnal-check reports it before the app runs when the component's `resources` is an object literal.
SYG248.note:
Fix: Name a key of the component's own `resources` (`until: 'search'` for `resources = { search: (state) => … }`), or pass a function for a result that arrives through a reply action: `until: (state) => state.status !== 'loading'`, with the action's own reducer setting `status: 'loading'`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG248

SYG250.title: SYG250 (warn): Layout names an unknown part or slot
SYG250.summary: A composition's layout (sygnal/ai `compose`, `catalog.finish()`, `catalog.render()`) names a part or container the catalog doesn't have, a slot its container doesn't declare, or a node key that isn't one of its nodes. It usually comes from `SET_LAYOUT` with a hand-made layout, a layout restored by `persist` after the catalog changed, or a model's typo. The node is dropped (the children of an unknown container or slot take its place, so the parts it held survive) and the rest of the layout is used. The same code reports a part's `companions` entry that names no part (ignored). Reported in development;
SYG250.note:
Fix: Use the catalog's part and container ids and the slot names the container declares. For a persisted layout, bump the `persist` version (or `migrate` the old layout) when you rename or remove parts.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG250

SYG251.title: SYG251 (warn): Invalid param value in a layout
SYG251.summary: A node's `params` don't fit the part's declaration: a value that isn't one of the param's `options`, a number that isn't a number (or is outside `min` … `max`: clamped), text or a list of the wrong type, a list shorter than its `min`, or a param the part doesn't declare. The default is used instead. A node whose record param names no current record (`from(state)` doesn't list it), or whose required `type: 'text'` / `'list'` param (with no default) is missing, can't be shown and is dropped. Over-long text and list items are cut to `maxLength` silently. Reported in development, by the finishing step (`SET_LAYOUT`, `REMOVE`, and both backends).
SYG251.note:
Fix: Send values the declaration allows (`params: { range: 'quarter' }` for `options: { week, month, quarter }`), and record ids `from(state)` returns. When records can disappear, expect their nodes to go.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG251

SYG252.title: SYG252 (warn): Record param from() does not return an array of { value }
SYG252.summary: A record param (`params: { id: { from: (state) => records } }`) turns app state into one option per record: a decision backend offers each record as a choice, an LLM backend lists them as an enum, and the record's `value` becomes the node key (`project:7`). `from` must return an array of `{ value, name?, aliases?, description? }` with a string or number `value`. It returned something else (or threw), so the part has no records (entries without a valid `value` are skipped). Reported in development, once per part and catalog.
SYG252.note:
Fix: Return `state.projects.map((p) => ({ value: p.id, name: p.name, description: `${p.name}: ${p.status}` }))`, and guard against missing state (`(state.projects || []).map(…)`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG252

SYG253.title: SYG253 (warn): Misspelled catalog declaration key
SYG253.summary: A key of a `defineCatalog({...})` declaration (sygnal/ai), of a part, a container or a param is one letter or a swap away from a key `defineCatalog` reads (`descrption`, `compnent`, `deafult`, `maxuses`). `defineCatalog` ignores keys it doesn't know, so the setting has no effect: a misspelled `description` leaves the model with only the part's id, a misspelled `default` makes the first option the default, a misspelled `component` renders nothing (SYG162). Other unknown keys are not reported: an app may keep its own data on a declaration. Static only (`sygnal-check`, for literal declarations); the editor offers the rename as a quick fix.
SYG253.note:
Fix: Rename the key to the one suggested. The keys: a catalog `parts`, `containers`, `description`, `categories`, `rows`, `guidance`, `limits`, `examples`; a part `component`, `render`, `props`, `description`, `state`, `local`, `params`, `in`, `group`, `maxUses`, `required`, `pin`, `companions`, `category`, `result`; a container `slots`, `minSlots`, `min`, `max`, `maxUses`, `accepts`, `arranged`, `direction`, `description`, `in`, `params`, `render`; a param `options`, `default`, `label`, `ask`, `type`, `min`, `max`, `bins`, `maxLength`, `required`, `items`, `from`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG253

SYG254.title: SYG254 (info): Catalog descriptions or options overlap
SYG254.summary: A model composing from a catalog (sygnal/ai `compose.decisions()` or `compose.llm()`) sees a part only as its `description`, and a param only as its options' descriptions. In the evals most selection errors came from three wordings, which this lint flags: two part descriptions that share a phrase (two adjacent content words: "monthly revenue" on both the revenue KPI and the revenue chart pulled in the wrong part); a part description that names one of its own param values ("revenue over the last 12 months" on a part with a `range` param: the description is read for every value);
SYG254.note:
Fix: Write each description as "Noun (what it shows)", leading with the word a user says for that part and not repeating another part's content ("Revenue (KPI card: this month's total)", "Revenue chart (line chart of the revenue trend)"); put alternatives in a `group`; leave param values out of the description (the param supplies them); word each param's options so they name only what that param changes.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG254

SYG256.title: SYG256 (warn): Output guard rejects the updated state
SYG256.summary: Since Sygnal 7, STATE runs first in a model entry and every other sink gets the committed state. On an installed Sygnal 7 or later, this check reports a STATE write of a literal field value that makes a same-action output guard return the imported ABORT value. For example, STATE sets status to 'working', then HTTP checks state.status !== 'working' and suppresses the request that just started. This conservative check covers simple field comparisons and boolean guards, retaining STATE branch conditions so a guard already known to reject before STATE is not reported.
SYG256.note:
Fix: Keep the admission guard, but read props.previousState (the state from before the action) for the value that admitted it, for example HTTP: (state, data, next, { previousState }) => previousState.status !== 'working' ? { url: '/work', requestId: state.requestId, ok: 'DONE' } : ABORT. Use the updated state for payload fields written by STATE. Do not remove the guard: STATE returning ABORT does not cancel other sinks, so an unconditional output can send duplicate requests. No automatic fix is offered.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG256

SYG257.title: SYG257 (info): Output reads a field its action changed (7.0 timing audit)
SYG257.summary: An opt-in migration audit for the 7.0 reducer timing: an output sink (EFFECT, HTTP, EVENTS, PARENT, ELEMENT, another driver or a behavior output) read a top-level state field that the same action's STATE changed. Since 7.0 the output gets the new, committed value; in 6.x it got the old one. Reported once per component, action, sink and field.
SYG257.note:
Fix: If the output meant the value from before the action (an admission guard, a 'was' value), read it from the fourth argument: (state, data, next, { previousState }) => previousState.status ... Otherwise nothing needs to change: the output now sees what STATE wrote.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG257

SYG258.title: SYG258 (warn): Clock or randomness read from a global in a STATE reducer
SYG258.summary: A STATE reducer calls `Date.now()`, `new Date()` with no arguments, `Math.random()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` (also through `globalThis.`, `window.` or `self.`) directly in its body. The reducer then gives a different state each time the same action runs, so replaying recorded actions (record/replay, a test with `renderComponent`) does not reproduce the state. Model handlers receive `now()`, `random()` and `uuid()` on their 4th argument (props); record/replay and `renderComponent` (fixed clock, seeded random, deterministic ids) supply them, so the reducer stays deterministic. Calls in nested functions, views and intents are not reported.
SYG258.note:
Fix: Take the value from the reducer's 4th argument: `ADD_TASK: (state, title, next, { now, uuid }) => ({ ...state, tasks: [...state.tasks, { id: uuid(), title, created: now() }] })` instead of `crypto.randomUUID()` and `Date.now()`; `new Date()` becomes `new Date(now())`. A component prop with the same name shadows them.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG258

SYG259.title: SYG259 (warn): An output reads a field its action's STATE cleared
SYG259.summary: An action's STATE reducer sets a top-level state field to an empty literal (`''`, `null`, `undefined`, `false`, `[]` or `{}`), and another handler of the same model entry (EFFECT, PARENT, HTTP, EVENTS, ELEMENT or another sink) reads that field from its state argument. Since Sygnal 7.0 the STATE reducer runs first and the other outputs get the committed state, so the handler always reads the cleared value: an Enter that clears a text box and sends its text up with PARENT sends `''`.
SYG259.note:
Fix: Read the value from before the action, on the handler's 4th argument: `PARENT: (state, data, next, { previousState }) => previousState.text`. Or pass the value in the action's data from the intent (`KEY: DOM.keydown('.box').filter(e => e.key === 'Enter').map(e => e.target.value)`) and read `data`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG259

SYG260.title: SYG260 (warn): undo() or undoable() on a key shared() syncs
SYG260.summary: `shared()` from `sygnal/yjs` keeps `state[key]` in a Yjs document that other clients edit too. Sygnal's `undo({ key })` behavior and `undoable(model, { key })` record snapshots of the whole slice and restore one on UNDO: the restored snapshot is then written to the document like any local edit, so it reverts every change other users made since that snapshot, not only this user's. The Yjs driver has a per-user undo instead: a `Y.UndoManager` per shared key that tracks only this client's own transactions, so a remote change made after this user's edit survives the undo.
SYG260.note:
Fix: Remove the snapshot undo for that key and send the commands to the driver: `UNDO: { SHARED: { undo: 'board' } }`, `REDO: { SHARED: { redo: 'board' } }`; `shared({ history: 'history' })` puts `{ canUndo, canRedo }` in `state.history` for the buttons. `undo()` on keys that aren't shared keeps working next to it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG260

SYG261.title: SYG261 (warn): shared() inferred the kind of an empty array
SYG261.summary: Without a `shape`, `shared()` infers how each field of the slice is stored in the Yjs document from its value: an array of objects that all have an `id` becomes an id-keyed collection (concurrent adds, edits, moves and removes of different items merge), any other array a `Y.Array` of plain values. An empty array fits both, so the driver guesses a collection; if the field later holds plain values (strings, numbers), it is switched to a list then, and a concurrent edit by another client can be lost in the switch. Reported once per field path, in dev, when the slice is first written to the document.
SYG261.note:
Fix: Declare the field's kind: `shared({ shape: { tags: 'list' } })` for plain values, `shared({ shape: { items: collection() } })` (from `sygnal/yjs`) for items with an `id`. Fields the shape leaves out are still inferred.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG261

SYG262.title: SYG262 (warn): Canvas data layer rebuilt with equal nodes
SYG262.summary: A `<shapes items={…}>` data layer of `sygnal/canvas` got a new array in which at least half of its nodes (64 or more) are new objects with exactly the fields of the nodes they replace: a reducer rebuilt every shape (`shapes.map(s => ({ ...s }))`, a JSON round trip, a fresh copy from a store) while changing few or none. The canvas keys its static layer, its translation blits and its camera cache on node identity (as `sygnal/yjs` keys its diff on it), so a layer whose nodes all change identity repaints everything on every frame, silently: the app still works, at a full repaint's cost.
SYG262.note:
Fix: Replace only the nodes that change and keep the others: `shapes.map(s => s.id === id ? { ...s, x } : s)`, or patch by index. For a selection, look the ids up in a `Set` and return the untouched objects as they are.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG262

SYG301.title: SYG301 (error): RxJS operator used on an xstream stream
SYG301.summary: An RxJS operator such as `pipe`, `switchMap`, `debounceTime` or `tap` was called on a Sygnal stream, which is an xstream stream and does not have it. With `sygnal/diagnostics` loaded, these names are defined on xstream's `Stream.prototype` to throw a `TypeError` that names the xstream equivalent, instead of the bare `x.switchMap is not a function`. A side effect of the dev entry is that `typeof stream.pipe === 'function'` is true while it is loaded.
SYG301.note:
Fix: Use the xstream equivalent from the message, e.g. `.map(x => inner$).flatten()` for `switchMap`, or `.compose(debounce(ms))` for `debounceTime`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG301

SYG302.title: SYG302 (info): Default import from 'xstream' or 'xstream/extra/*'
SYG302.summary: xstream is published as CommonJS with an `exports.default`, and so is each of its extras (`xstream/extra/dropRepeats`, `debounce`, ...). Bundlers that apply interop give `import xs from 'xstream'` the stream factory, but Node's ESM loader and Vite 8 (in a package with `"type": "module"`) give the module object, so `xs.create`, `xs.merge` and `xs.of` are undefined there, `dropRepeats()` is "not a function", and a driver, intent or test fails when it runs, after `tsc` and the checker passed.
SYG302.note:
Fix: Import it from Sygnal: `import { xs } from 'sygnal'` (`import { xs as stream } from 'sygnal'` for another name), `import { dropRepeats, debounce } from 'sygnal'`. `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites an import whose only specifier is the default one. For an extra Sygnal doesn't export, resolve the default yourself: `import pairwiseModule from 'xstream/extra/pairwise'` then `const pairwise = pairwiseModule.default ?? pairwiseModule`. To react to a state change, `STATE.watch(fn)` needs no extra at all (SYG303). Types stay importable from xstream: `import type { Stream } from 'xstream'`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG302

SYG303.title: SYG303 (info): STATE.stream with dropRepeats() in an intent
SYG303.summary: An intent builds an action from `STATE.stream` composed with `dropRepeats()`, as in `CHANGED: STATE.stream.map(s => s.tab).compose(dropRepeats())`: the hand-written way to act when part of the state changes. `STATE.watch(fn)` is the canonical form: it emits the selected value each time it changes, compares values structurally (a new array with the same items is no change), works the same in a Collection item (its own state), and needs no xstream extra (a default import of one fails at run time under Node ESM and Vite 8, SYG302).
SYG303.note:
Fix: Use `STATE.watch(fn)`: `CHANGED: STATE.watch(state => state.tab)`, followed by the same operators (`STATE.watch(s => s.text).compose(debounce(1000))`). Add `{ immediate: true }` (`STATE.watch(fn, { immediate: true })`) when the action must also fire for the current value, as `STATE.stream` did.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG303

SYG401.title: SYG401 (warn): Collection 'from' field is missing or not an array
SYG401.summary: A `<Collection>` needs an array to render. The runtime reports this when `from="field"` names a key that is not in the parent state (or its calculated fields), when that field is not an array, or when a `from={{ get, set }}` getter returns a non-array; the dev entry also reports a `<Collection>` with no `from` whose parent state is not an array. In every case the Collection renders no items: a missing `from` key until the key appears in the state (it then renders, since 6.0), a non-array value until it becomes an array.
SYG401.note:
Fix: Point `from` at an array field and initialize it in `initialState`, e.g. `initialState = { items: [] }` with `<Collection of={Item} from="items" />`, or make a custom `get()` return an array.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG401

SYG402.title: SYG402 (error): Context is not an object
SYG402.summary: The component's `.context` is set to something other than a plain object (for example a function or an array). It is logged and ignored: the component contributes no context values, and descendants only receive the context inherited from further up. It is logged, not thrown, so rendering continues.
SYG402.note:
Fix: Define context as an object of named entries: `Comp.context = { theme: state => state.theme }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG402

SYG403.title: SYG403 (error): Invalid context entry
SYG403.summary: A `.context` entry value is not a function. Context entries are functions of state only: the state-key string (`{ user: 'currentUser' }`) and `true` entries Sygnal accepted before 6.0 were removed. That entry is skipped each time context is computed, so descendants read `undefined` for it; the other entries still work. It is logged, not thrown.
SYG403.note:
Fix: Write each entry as a function of state: `{ user: state => state.currentUser }`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#leftovers.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG403

SYG404.title: SYG404 (error): Context stream errored
SYG404.summary: The stream that computes a component's context emitted an error, most often because a context function threw. An errored xstream stream stops, so this component's context stops updating for its descendants from that point on. The original error is attached to the log.
SYG404.note:
Fix: Check the attached error and make each context function safe for every state it can receive (e.g. guard against missing fields with `state.user?.name`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG404

SYG405.title: SYG405 (error): Sub-component has initialState without isolatedState
SYG405.summary: A sub-component defines `initialState` but not `isolatedState = true`, so its `initialState` would overwrite the state slice its parent passes in. For a component rendered by tag in a parent's view this is an error: it is thrown when the child is instantiated, and the parent catches it, logs it under this code and renders its error fallback instead of the child. For Collection items and Switchable children it is only a warning and the initial state still replaces what the parent passed. It doesn't matter whether the tag has a `state` prop: `<Stopwatch state="stopwatch" />` and `<Stopwatch />` both throw.
SYG405.note:
Fix: Remove `initialState` from the sub-component and let the parent own the state: put the child's start values in the parent's `initialState`, under the field the `state` prop names (`App.initialState = { stopwatch: { ms: 0 } }` for `<Stopwatch state="stopwatch" />`). Or set `Child.isolatedState = true` if the child should keep its own local state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG405

SYG406.title: SYG406 (error): View threw
SYG406.summary: The component's view function threw while rendering. The error is logged and the component renders its `onError` fallback if it has one, or an empty `<div data-sygnal-error>` otherwise. The app keeps running, but that component shows no real content until a later render succeeds.
SYG406.note:
Fix: Fix the error in the view (often a missing field on `state` or `props`), and add `Comp.onError = (error, { componentName }) =>
…
` if you want a custom fallback. More: sygnal-check explain SYG406

SYG407.title: SYG407 (error): onError handler threw
SYG407.summary: A component's `onError` handler threw while handling a view error (SYG406) or a sub-component instantiation error (SYG408). Sygnal logs the second error and renders an empty `<div data-sygnal-error>` instead of your fallback.
SYG407.note:
Fix: Keep `onError` simple and make it always return a vnode, e.g. `Comp.onError = () =>
Something went wrong
`. More: sygnal-check explain SYG407

SYG408.title: SYG408 (error): Sub-component failed to instantiate
SYG408.summary: Creating a sub-component (a custom component, Collection, or Switchable found in the parent's view) threw an uncoded exception, for example from the child's intent. The parent catches it, logs it with the original error attached, and renders its own `onError` fallback, or an empty `<div data-sygnal-error>`, in that child's place. The rest of the parent keeps rendering. A coded Sygnal error thrown while instantiating (SYG405, SYG413, SYG414, SYG903, ...) is reported under its own code instead, with the same fallback.
SYG408.note:
Fix: Read the attached error and fix its cause.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG408

SYG409.title: SYG409 (warn): Child tried to update a calculated field
SYG409.summary: A sub-component, Switchable, or Collection is bound to a parent state field (via its `state` or `from` prop) that is one of the parent's `calculated` fields, and the child wrote a new value back to it. Calculated fields are derived from other state, so the write is ignored and the parent state is left unchanged.
SYG409.note:
Fix: Bind the child to a plain (non-calculated) state field, and change the fields the calculated value is derived from instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG409

SYG410.title: SYG410 (error): Invalid sub-component 'state' prop
SYG410.summary: The `state` prop on a sub-component or Switchable is neither a state key string nor an object with a `get()` function (for example a number, or a `{ set }` object without `get`). It is logged and the child falls back to receiving the parent's whole state, which is usually not what was intended. Also reported (by the dev checks at run time, and by sygnal-check for a literal) when a child's `state` is an empty string, `state=""`, or a path with an empty segment (`"user."`, `".user"`, `"a..b"`): that names an empty key, so the child reads `state[""]`, gets no state and is left out of the view without any other error.
SYG410.note:
Fix: Pass a state key string (`state="user"`) or a lens object `state={{ get: s => s.user, set: (s, user) => ({ ...s, user }) }}`. For an empty `state`, leave the prop out to share the parent's state (`<Child />`; `sygnal-check --fix` removes `state=""`), or name a key in every segment of the path.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG410

SYG411.title: SYG411 (error): Collection 'of' is missing or not a component
SYG411.summary: A `<Collection>` has no `of` prop, or `of` is not a component function (a component name as a string, `<Collection of="Row">`, is a form Sygnal 6.0 removed; it is also reported as SYG612). This is thrown while the parent's view is processed, so the Collection cannot render.
SYG411.note:
Fix: Pass the item component function itself: `<Collection of={TaskCard} from="tasks" />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG411

SYG412.title: SYG412 (error): Invalid Collection 'from' prop
SYG412.summary: The `from` prop on a `<Collection>` is neither a state key string nor an object with a `get()` function. It is logged (not thrown) and the Collection renders nothing.
SYG412.note:
Fix: Use a state key string (`from="items"`) or a lens object with `get` and `set`: `from={{ get: s => s.items, set: (s, items) => ({ ...s, items }) }}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG412

SYG413.title: SYG413 (error): Retired in 6.0: Unnamed component factory not found
SYG413.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it was logged when a view rendered an element carrying neither a component factory nor its options (`sygnal-factory`). Since 6.0 a component vnode carries the component function itself (`data.c`); there are no factories or options objects to lose.
SYG413.note:
Fix: Nothing to change. Render components as JSX tags of their functions.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG413

SYG414.title: SYG414 (error): Retired in 6.0: Component not found
SYG414.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it was logged when a view rendered a component by a string name that no `.components` registry entry matched. Sygnal 6.0 removed string tags and `.components`: a component is always referenced by its function. A leftover string tag renders as a plain element and is reported as SYG612 in development.
SYG414.note:
Fix: Import the component and use it as a JSX tag. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#string-tags.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG414

SYG415.title: SYG415 (error): Switchable 'of' is missing or invalid
SYG415.summary: A `<Switchable>` has no `of` prop, `of` is not a plain object, or one of its values is not a component function. This is thrown while the parent's view is processed, so the Switchable cannot render.
SYG415.note:
Fix: Pass an object mapping names to components: `<Switchable of={{ list: ListView, grid: GridView }} current={state.mode} />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG415

SYG416.title: SYG416 (error): Switchable 'current' is missing or invalid
SYG416.summary: A `<Switchable>` has no `current` prop, `current` is not a string or function, or `current` is not one of the keys of `of`. This is thrown while the parent's view is processed, so no component can be shown.
SYG416.note:
Fix: Set `current` to one of the keys of `of`, e.g. `current="list"` when `of={{ list: ListView, grid: GridView }}`, and make sure the state value it comes from is initialized.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG416

SYG417.title: SYG417 (warn): Portal target not found
SYG417.summary: A `<Portal target="…">` selector matched no element in the document. Sygnal retries for a short time (about 10 attempts, 5 ms apart) in case the target is rendered by a sub-component that has not settled yet, then warns and leaves the portal content unrendered.
SYG417.note:
Fix: Make sure an element matching the `target` selector exists in the page (for example `<div id="modal-root">` in your HTML) before the Portal mounts.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG417

SYG418.title: SYG418 (error): Invalid Collection sort prop
SYG418.summary: The `sort` prop on a `<Collection>` has an unsupported shape: an object with more than one key, a direction that is not `'asc'`, `'desc'`, `1` or `-1`, or a value that is not a string, array, object or function. The invalid sort (or array element) is logged and ignored, so the items are not sorted as intended.
SYG418.note:
Fix: Use a field name (`sort="title"`), a single-key object (`sort={{ title: 'desc' }}`), a comparator function, or an array of these.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG418

SYG419.title: SYG419 (error): Retired in 6.0: Invalid switchable() 'name$' parameter
SYG419.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown by the low-level `switchable()` helper, which Sygnal 6.0 removed together with the `component()` factory. `<Switchable of={...} current={...} />` is the one form.
SYG419.note:
Fix: Render `<Switchable of={{ a: A, b: B }} current={state.tab} />` in a view.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG419

SYG420.title: SYG420 (error): JSX tag is undefined
SYG420.summary: A JSX element's tag evaluated to `undefined`, usually because a component was not imported, was misspelled, or was imported as default instead of named (or vice versa). Sygnal renders an `<UNDEFINED>` element in its place and logs the message with `console.error`; it is collected like other runtime diagnostics (the JSX runtime reports it through the diagnostics core, or only prints it when no Sygnal core is loaded).
SYG420.note:
Fix: Import or define the component in the file that uses it, and check that the import style (default vs named) matches the export.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG420

SYG421.title: SYG421 (error): Invalid data (dataset) key
SYG421.summary: A view renders a `data` key the DOM can't store. `data={{ ... }}` is written with `element.dataset[key] = value`, and the browser throws a SyntaxError DOMException for a key with a hyphen followed by a lower-case letter (`'task-id'`), or an attribute-name error for characters such as spaces, quotes or `=`. The patch fails, so rendering can stop, and the console shows only a bare `DOMException {}`. The dev entry checks every rendered dataset key before the patch and names the key; renderComponent's mock DOM never throws, so it is also the only signal there.
SYG421.note:
Fix: Use a camelCase key in the `data` prop: `data={{ taskId: 7 }}` renders `data-task-id="7"` (a `data-task-id="7"` JSX attribute works too); read it with `.data('taskId')`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG421

SYG422.title: SYG422 (error): Invalid timer spec
SYG422.summary: A component's `timers` static declares a timer that `makeTimerDriver()` can't run, so it is not started (the other timers are). A spec is `{ every: ms, action }` (a positive interval), `{ after: ms, action }` (0 or more) or `{ frame: 'ACTION' }`, each with an optional `background: true`. Reported for a non-positive or non-numeric `every`, a negative `after`, both `every` and `after`, a missing or non-string `action`, or a `frame` that isn't an action name. A falsy entry (`state.running && { ... }`) is not an error: it means the timer is stopped. sygnal-check reports it too, for specs written as literals (`{ every: 0, action: 'TICK' }`);
SYG422.note:
Fix: Use `tick: state.running && { every: 100, action: 'TICK' }`, `done: state.armed && { after: 5000, action: 'EXPIRE' }` or `frame: state.animating && { frame: 'FRAME' }`. To stop a timer, return a falsy value for it instead of an invalid spec.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG422

SYG423.title: SYG423 (warn): Context change skipped a view whose output it changes
SYG423.summary: A component reads context, the context changed, and Sygnal did not re-render the component, because its view read none of the changed keys during its last call. Sygnal 6.0 re-renders a component on a context change only when its view read a key that changed. With `sygnal/diagnostics` loaded, a sample of the skipped views is called again with the new context; when the result differs, the page shows a stale render and this is reported.
SYG423.note:
Fix: Read the entries in the view itself, `context.theme` or `function C({ context: { theme } })`, on every call. Pass a value you need later as a prop or keep it in state instead of a saved context object.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG423

SYG424.title: SYG424 (warn): Duplicate Collection item id
SYG424.summary: Two or more items in a `<Collection>`'s array have the same `id`. A Collection keys its items by `id` (an item without one by its index in the array), so only the first item with that id renders, and the item component's writes go to that first item. The others are not shown.
SYG424.note:
Fix: Give every item a unique `id` when it is created, for example from a counter in state or `uuid()` from the reducer's 4th argument (`(state, data, next, { uuid }) => …`). Items with no `id` at all are keyed by their index.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG424

SYG425.title: SYG425 (warn): isolatedState slice lacks initialState keys
SYG425.summary: An `isolatedState` component is bound to a slice of its parent's state (`state="key"` or a lens) that already exists, so it keeps that slice and its `initialState` is not applied (since 6.0 the parent's data wins). The slice lacks keys that `initialState` defines, so the component's view and reducers see them as undefined.
SYG425.note:
Fix: Add `resetState` to the tag (`<Panel state="panel" resetState />`) to start the component from its `initialState`, replacing the slice. To keep the parent's data, initialize the missing keys in the parent's state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG425

SYG426.title: SYG426 (warn): Deprecated lowercase marker tag
SYG426.summary: A view writes a Sygnal marker as a lowercase string tag: `<collection>` or `<switchable>` (which work without an import), or `<clientonly>`, `<portal>`, `<transition>` or `<suspense>`. The lowercase tags are deprecated since 6.3.0 and will be removed in the next major: the tag will then render an unknown HTML element (`<collection>`) instead of the component, and the Collection and Switchable handlers will load only when their imported components are used. Since 6.3.0 `<portal>`, `<transition>` and `<suspense>` already work only when the capitalized component is used somewhere else in the app.
SYG426.note:
Fix: Import the component and write it capitalized: `import { Collection } from 'sygnal'` and `<Collection of={Item} from="items" />` (`Switchable`, `Portal`, `Transition` and `Suspense` from 'sygnal', `ClientOnly` from 'sygnal/vike'). `sygnal-check --fix` renames the tags and adds the import.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG426

SYG427.title: SYG427 (error): CHILD.select() of something that is not a component
SYG427.summary: A component is imported from a module that doesn't export it, so the binding is `undefined`. The browser refuses to load the module ("does not provide an export named …"), but Vitest runs on with `undefined`: `CHILD.select(Child)` never emits, and `<Child />` renders nothing (SYG420, only when that branch renders). A test that never shows the branch passes, with no diagnostic. With `sygnal/diagnostics` loaded, `CHILD.select()` of anything but a function is reported when the component is created, so every test of the parent catches it.
SYG427.note:
Fix: Export the component from its module (`export function Child() { … }`), or fix the imported name. Pass `CHILD.select()` the component function itself.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG427

SYG428.title: SYG428 (warn): A state path that names a key containing a dot
SYG428.summary: Since 6.5.0, a child's `state="a.b"`, a Switchable's `state` and a Collection's `from="a.b"` are paths: `state.a.b` (`a[0].b` for an array position). Before, the string was one key, so a state with a key that itself contains a dot (`{ 'a.b': [...] }`) was read directly. Such a key is now missed: the designator reads `state.a.b`, which is undefined, so the child or the Collection renders nothing, and the first write creates `{ a: { b: ... } }` beside the old key. The dev diagnostics report it when the owner's state has a key equal to the designator.
SYG428.note:
Fix: Rename the key so it has no dot (`{ ab: [...] }` with `state="ab"`), or keep it and pass a lens: `state={{ get: (s) => s['a.b'], set: (s, v) => ({ ...s, 'a.b': v }) }}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG428

SYG429.title: SYG429 (warn): Switchable state map names no page
SYG429.summary: A Switchable's `state` can be a map from page names to bindings, `state={{ projects: 'pages.projects', settings: 'pages.settings' }}`: each listed page binds its own slice (a key, a path, a lens or a `byId` selection) with a tag child's lifetime rules, and the pages not listed share the owner's state. A key that is not one of the `of` pages binds nothing, so the page it was meant for (usually a typo of its name) shares the owner's whole state instead of its slice. The dev checks report it once per component and key when the Switchable renders; `sygnal-check` reports it when `of` is an object literal.
SYG429.note:
Fix: Use the page's name from `of={{ … }}` as the key (the message names the closest one), or remove the entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG429

SYG430.title: SYG430 (warn): VirtualCollection has no bounded height
SYG430.summary: A `<VirtualCollection>` is its own scroll container (`overflow-y: auto`) and renders the rows that fit in its height. Its element is either 0 px tall, so no row is in view, or as tall as all of its rows (its height comes from its content, e.g. no `height` in its class, or a `max-height: 100%`, `calc()` of a percentage or `fit-content` that resolves against a parent without a height; Sygnal measures whether the height follows the rows), so it never scrolls and would render every row. In the second case Sygnal renders only the rows within the viewport's height, and rows further down the page stay empty.
SYG430.note:
Fix: Give its `className` a bounded height: `.rows { height: 400px }` or `max-height`, or in a flex column `flex: 1; min-height: 0`. Check that a parent with `display: none` isn't the cause of a 0 height.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG430

SYG431.title: SYG431 (warn): VirtualCollection items without ids
SYG431.summary: Items of a `<VirtualCollection>`'s array have no `id`, so they are keyed by their index (as in a Collection, D169). A VirtualCollection keeps a measured height and an instance per key: when items are added, removed or reordered, both follow the position, not the item, so rows get each other's heights and a row's instance shows another item. Reported once per VirtualCollection.
SYG431.note:
Fix: Give every item a unique `id`, e.g. `rows: data.map((r) => ({ id: r.key, ...r }))`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG431

SYG432.title: SYG432 (warn): VirtualCollection item does not render one element
SYG432.summary: The item component of a `<VirtualCollection>` rendered a fragment (an array of elements) or text. A VirtualCollection measures each row's root element and sets `data-index`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` on it; a fragment has no root element, so its rows can't be measured (later rows overlap or leave gaps) or announced in position. Reported once per VirtualCollection.
SYG432.note:
Fix: Return one element from the item's view: wrap its content in a `<div>` (or an `<li>`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG432

SYG433.title: SYG433 (warn): VirtualCollection scroll target not in the list
SYG433.summary: An element command `{ scrollToIndex: target, index }` or `{ scrollToId: target, id }` reached a `<VirtualCollection>` with an index outside its rows (an index counts the rows after `filter` and `sort`, from 0) or an id that no shown item has (not in the array, or filtered out). It didn't scroll.
SYG433.note:
Fix: Send an integer index from 0 to the number of shown rows minus 1, or the id of an item the filter keeps: `{ scrollToId: '.rows', id: row.id }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG433

SYG434.title: SYG434 (warn): Invalid VirtualCollection estimateSize or overscan
SYG434.summary: `estimateSize` must be a positive number (a row's height in px before it is measured) or a function `(item, index) => px`, and `overscan` a number ≥ 0 (rows rendered beyond each edge). Another value is ignored: 32 px and 5 rows are used instead.
SYG434.note:
Fix: Pass `estimateSize={32}` (about your row height) or `(item) => (item.expanded ? 120 : 32)`, and `overscan={5}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG434

SYG435.title: SYG435 (warn): Sortable list shown filtered or in another order
SYG435.summary: `sortable` moves entries of `state[from]`: the arrow keys swap the item with its neighbour in the array, Home / End move it to the array's ends, the announced positions count the array, and a pointer drop lands next to the entry it is dropped on. When the list is rendered from a `<Collection>` with `sort` (or `filter` that hides entries between shown ones), the shown order isn't the array's: under a sort a move changes nothing visible (the Collection sorts it back), and under a filter a keyboard step can pass hidden entries and the positions count entries nobody sees.
SYG435.note:
Fix: Reorder only a list that is shown as it is stored: drop the Collection's `sort` for a reorderable list (sort the array itself, once, if it needs an initial order), and while a filter hides entries hide the drag handles (or render the full list) so a move can't pass hidden ones.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG435

SYG436.title: SYG436 (warn): VirtualCollection estimateSize far from the measured row heights
SYG436.summary: `<VirtualCollection estimateSize={n}>` counts every row that hasn't been rendered yet as `n` px tall; a rendered row is measured. When the real rows are taller than the estimate, the list's total height is too short until the rows near the end have been rendered and measured, so a fast scroll to the end shows blank space where the last rows belong and the scrollbar jumps as the total grows; when they are much shorter, the scrollbar shrinks and jumps instead. The dev entry compares a numeric `estimateSize` with the median of the first 10 measured rows and reports it once per list when they differ by more than 1.3×.
SYG436.note:
Fix: Pass the rows' real height, `estimateSize={71}` (the message gives the measured median); when unsure, err high. When rows differ predictably, pass a function: `estimateSize={(item) => (item.image ? 240 : 56)}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG436

SYG440.title: SYG440 (warn): Two agent declarations with the same name
SYG440.summary: Agent tools are named after the declaration (`agent.name`, else the component name): `todos_read`, `todos_add`. Two shown instances with different declarations, or the same non-item component rendered twice, produce the same tool names, so only the first one's tools are offered and the other can't be reached. (Collection items of one component are one keyed tool and are not reported.) Reported once per name while an agent layer runs. sygnal-check reports two declarations with the same literal name (or none, so the component names collide) when one component renders both, directly or through its children.
SYG440.note:
Fix: Give each declaration its own `agent.name` (for a component rendered twice, derive it from a prop: `Panel.agent = { name: 'left_panel', ... }` on a wrapper per place), or narrow the layer with `agentTools(app, { from })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG440

SYG441.title: SYG441 (warn): Agent Collection items without unique ids
SYG441.summary: A Collection item component's `agent` actions become one tool with an `id` parameter whose values are the items' ids. Items without an `id` are keyed by their index, which shifts when an item is added or removed, so a model's call can reach the wrong item. Items whose ids repeat across Collections of the same item component (the same card id in two board lanes) are ambiguous: the call reaches the first. Reported once per declaration while an agent layer runs.
SYG441.note:
Fix: Give every item an `id` that is unique across all the Collections of that item component (`{ id: 'todo-1', ... }`), or add an owner-level action that takes the qualified key (`MOVE_CARD: { input: z.object({ lane, card }) }`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG441

SYG442.title: SYG442 (error): Chat or command bar behavior not connected to its app
SYG442.summary: The `chat` and `commandBar` behaviors (sygnal/ai) run agent actions through the app's runtime, which they reach through a hook layer every app picks up when it starts.
