The first `chat()` or `commandBar()` call installs that layer, and also adds it to the app already running that `run()` registered (the page's first live app), so a component using one of them loaded lazily into that app works. Another app started before the first call (a second `run()` on the page, a `sygnal/element` custom element) can't be found and has none: its assistant still streams replies, but sends no tools, no `read` context, and runs no tool calls;
SYG442.note:
Fix: Make the first `chat()` / `commandBar()` call happen before `run()`: define the host component (or call the factory once) in a module the entry imports, not only in a component loaded later.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG442

SYG450.title: SYG450 (warn): Catalog in names an unknown container or slot
SYG450.summary: A part's (or container's) `in` lists the places it may go, as `'container'` (any of its slots) or `'container:slot'`; the root is `'page'`. An entry names a container the catalog doesn't declare, a slot that container doesn't have, or the built-in `row` (rows are transparent: a part in a row is where the row is). That entry is ignored; with none left the part goes on the page. The same code reports a container's `min` / `max` that isn't a non-negative integer, `min` above `max`, a `maxUses` that isn't a positive integer, or `accepts` other than `'leaves'` (ignored). Reported in development, when the catalog is defined;
SYG450.note:
Fix: Name declared containers and slots (`in: ['page', 'tabs:billing']`), and declare the container in `containers` before using it in `in`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG450

SYG451.title: SYG451 (warn): Composed has no catalog or from is not a composition
SYG451.summary: `<Composed catalog={catalog} from="page" />` (sygnal/ai) renders the composition kept at `from` in the host component's state, with the catalog's parts. Here it can't: the `catalog` prop is missing (or isn't made by `defineCatalog()`), the value at `from` (a key, default `'page'`, or a path such as `['boards', 0, 'page']`) is not a composition (an object with a `layout`, as the `compose` behavior keeps under its key in `uses`), or `card` is not an `ask_user` tool part. The marker renders nothing and the rest of the view goes on.
SYG451.note:
Fix: Pass the catalog and the key of the compose behavior in `uses`: `App.uses = { page: compose(catalog, { backend }) }` with `<Composed catalog={catalog} from="page" />`. For a composition the view computes, call `catalog.render(slice, state)` in the view instead. For a chat card, pass the tool part: `<Composed catalog={catalog} card={part} />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG451

SYG452.title: SYG452 (warn): Layout lists a node key twice
SYG452.summary: A layout's node keys are identities: each node appears in exactly one slot, once. This layout lists a key in two places (or inside itself, a cycle). A key is the identity of a part's instance, so two places can't share it. The first place (in depth-first order) is kept and the others are dropped. It comes from a hand-made layout passed to `SET_LAYOUT` or from editing `nodes` directly. Reported in development, by the finishing step.
SYG452.note:
Fix: Give each node its own key (a repeat of a part is `part~2`), and move a node by removing its key from the old slot. `fromTree(catalog, tree, previous)` builds keys for you.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG452

SYG453.title: SYG453 (warn): Two children with the same identity share one instance
SYG453.summary: A component instance's identity among its parent view's children is its component plus its `key`, else its `id` prop, else its position in the view. Two tags of the same component with the same `key` (or `id`) in one view, anywhere in it, are the same identity, so they are one instance: it has one state, both places show its output, and the second tag's props replace the first's. Reported once per parent, component and key.
SYG453.note:
Fix: Give each tag a key that is unique among its parent view's children, usually from the data it shows (`<Card key={card.id} />`). Use the same key for the same thing on every render: a new key makes a new instance.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG453

SYG454.title: SYG454 (warn): State binding changed without a new component identity
SYG454.summary: In Sygnal 6 a retained component's state path or byId binding is fixed at mount. A changing byId selector without a corresponding key can keep reading and writing the old record. Sygnal 7 disposes and remounts components when a known state path or byId target changes, even with the same explicit key; equivalent fresh byId objects preserve the component. Opaque custom lenses remain mount-bound. The static checker reports direct dynamic unkeyed byId selections only when the installed Sygnal is known to be 6; it is silent for 7 and when the installed version cannot be determined (no node_modules, Yarn PnP, git-tree --base checks).
SYG454.note:
Fix: On Sygnal 6 write <Workspace key={selected.id} state={byId('projects', selected.id)} />. The key creates a new component lifetime, disposing the old requests, timers and subscriptions. On Sygnal 7 known paths and byId targets remount automatically. For an opaque custom lens whose target changes, use an explicit key; memoization or forcing a render cannot identify its semantic target.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG454

SYG455.title: SYG455 (error): Outlet from names no wizard behavior
SYG455.summary: `<Outlet from="wizard">` renders the current step of the `wizard()` behavior the component declares under that key in its `uses`. The key names none (a typo, or `uses` declares the wizard under another key, or on another component), so the outlet has no steps to show and renders nothing. The runtime reports it once per component, in production too; the static checker reports it for a string `from` when the component's `uses` can be read, and also when the key names a behavior that isn't `wizard()`.
SYG455.note:
Fix: Declare the behavior on the component that renders the outlet, under the key `from` names: `NewFilter.uses = { wizard: wizard({ steps }) }` with `<Outlet of={STEPS} from="wizard" />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG455

SYG456.title: SYG456 (error): Outlet has no component for the current name
SYG456.summary: `<Outlet of={…}>` renders `of[name]` for the current name: the wizard's current step (`from`), the route's name (`route`), or `current`. The map has no component under that name, so nothing is rendered in its place. Typical causes: a step added to `wizard({ steps })` but not to `of`, or a route (the not-found route too) with no page. The runtime reports it once per component and name, in production too, when it happens; the static checker reports each step of the wizard's `steps` with no key in an `of` object literal.
SYG456.note:
Fix: Add the component under that name: `of={{ source: Source, review: Review }}` with one key per step name, or one per route name in route mode (`notFound: NotFound` included).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG456

SYG457.title: SYG457 (warn): Outlet of names no step of its wizard
SYG457.summary: An `<Outlet of={{ … }} from="wizard">` maps step names to components, and one of its keys is not a step of the `wizard()` it names (its `steps` option). That entry never renders: a misspelled step name (its step then has no component, SYG456), or a step that was removed from the flow. Reported when `of` and `steps` are object literals of named keys.
SYG457.note:
Fix: Rename the key to the step it is for (the checker suggests the closest name), or remove the entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG457

SYG458.title: SYG458 (warn): Declaration reads a context field off its bag
SYG458.summary: Since Sygnal 7.2 the second argument of the declaration statics `resources`, `timers`, `connections`, `head`, `browser` and `route` is the bag the view gets, `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`, not the context. For compatibility the context's own fields are still readable on the bag until 8.0, so `Page.resources = { item: (state, { route }) => ... }` keeps working, but 8.0 removes them; and when the component also takes a prop of that name the bag's own key wins, so the declaration reads the prop, not the context field. The dev entry reports the read at run time.
SYG458.note:
Fix: Read it from the bag's context: `Page.resources = { item: (state, { context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + route.params.id }` instead of `(state, { route }) => ...`, and `bag.context.route` instead of `bag.route`. `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites the destructuring form, keeping props at the top level: `(state, { id, route })` becomes `(state, { id, context: { route } })`, merged into an existing `context: { ... }` entry. A TypeScript annotation moves with them: `(state, { route }: Ctx)` becomes `(state, { context: { route } }: { context: Ctx })`, and a type literal's members move the same way;
More: sygnal-check explain SYG458

SYG459.title: SYG459 (warn): Behavior option reads a state field off its bag
SYG459.summary: Since Sygnal 7.2 the functions of a behavior's options (the wizard's `when`, `valid`, `label`, `visit`, `dirty`, `discard`, `dialog`, `draft`, `key`, `resetTo`, `url.from`; the form's `values`, `dynamic`, `request`) get the bag the view gets, `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`, after their own arguments. Before 7.2 the wizard's second argument was the host's state, so `when: (step, h) => h.route` still runs but reads `undefined`: the bag has no `route` prop. TypeScript types a behavior bag's props as `unknown`, which catches the reads whose value is used, but not every one.
SYG459.note:
Fix: Read the host's state from the bag: `when: (step, { state }) => state.route.name === 'review'`, or `h.state.route` instead of `h.route`. `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites `h.route` to `h.state.route`, and `(step, { route })` to `(step, { state: { route } })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG459

SYG501.title: SYG501 (error): Removed in 6.0: view with positional arguments
SYG501.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). The view declares more than one parameter, as in `function Lane(props, state, context)`. Sygnal 6.0 removed positional view arguments: a view is called with one argument, so `state` and `context` are undefined in the second and third parameters. At run time the dev checks report the same form as SYG612 (`positional-views`).
SYG501.note:
Fix: Destructure the one argument: `function Lane({ state, context, ...props })`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#positional-views.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG501

SYG502.title: SYG502 (warn): Retired in 6.0: STATE reducer signals no change without ABORT
SYG502.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0, strict mode flagged a STATE reducer that returned the state object it received (`return state`, `cond ? next : state`) instead of `ABORT`, because that still produced a new state. Since 6.0 returning the identical object is "no change", the same as `ABORT`: no state is emitted and nothing re-renders. A reducer that mutates the state in place and then returns it is reported by SYG222 instead.
SYG502.note:
Fix: Nothing to change: `return state` and `return ABORT` are equivalent in a STATE reducer. To change the state, return a new object.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG502

SYG503.title: SYG503 (warn): Side effect in a STATE reducer that returns ABORT
SYG503.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A STATE reducer runs a call whose result is unused (such as `cmd.send('play')`, `next('X')` or `localStorage.setItem(…)`) and then returns `ABORT`. This is the old pattern for side effects; the canonical form puts side effects in an `EFFECT` sink so STATE reducers stay pure. The check is a heuristic.
SYG503.note:
Fix: Move the side effect to an EFFECT sink: `PLAY: { EFFECT: (state, data, next) => { cmd.send('play') } }`, keeping any state change in `STATE`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG503

SYG504.title: SYG504 (error): Removed in 6.0: 'ACTION | SINK' model key
SYG504.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A model key uses the `'ACTION | SINK'` shorthand, such as `'SEND | EFFECT': …`. Sygnal 6.0 removed these keys: the object form is the only form. `sygnal-check --strict --fix` rewrites the key when no other entry handles the same action. At run time the dev checks report it as SYG612 (`pipe-keys`).
SYG504.note:
Fix: Use the object form: `SEND: { EFFECT: (state, data, next) => … }`, merging into an existing `SEND` entry if there is one. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#pipe-keys.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG504

SYG505.title: SYG505 (warn): Non-canonical EVENTS emit
SYG505.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A model entry emits a global event with `emit('TYPE', fn)` (as the whole entry or spread into the object form), or its EVENTS sink builds the `{ type: 'TYPE', data }` object by hand. The canonical form is an `EVENTS` sink using `event()` inside the object form. `--fix` rewrites the common cases and adds the `event` import.
SYG505.note:
Fix: Use `ACTION: { EVENTS: event('TYPE', (state, data) => payload) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG505

SYG506.title: SYG506 (error): Removed in 6.0: CHILD.select() with a component name
SYG506.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). An intent calls `CHILD.select('TaskCard')` with the child's name as a string. Sygnal 6.0 removed name lookups: children are matched by their component function. `--fix` replaces the string with the identifier when that name is in scope. At run time the dev checks report it as SYG612 (`child-select-name`).
SYG506.note:
Fix: Pass the component function: `CHILD.select(TaskCard)` (import it first if needed). See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#child-select-name.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG506

SYG507.title: SYG507 (info): Prop drilled through more than 2 component levels
SYG507.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A component receives a prop from its parent and passes it on unchanged, under the same name, to its own child component, so the value crosses three component levels. Data that flows that far down belongs in `.context`, which reaches every descendant without each level forwarding it. This is informational only.
SYG507.note:
Fix: Provide the value as context on the top component, e.g. `Parent.context = { theme: state => state.theme }`, and read `context.theme` where it is needed.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG507

SYG508.title: SYG508 (warn): select()/errors() round trip where reply actions would do
SYG508.summary: Strict mode only. A component sends a request with `category: 'quote'` to a driver with reply actions (`makeFetchDriver`, `driverFromAsync`, or a sink named `HTTP`) and reads the reply back in its own intent with `HTTP.select('quote')` or `HTTP.errors('quote')`. The canonical form is a request with reply actions: it names them in the request, so the intent line, the category string and the select/errors split all go away, and the reply reaches exactly the component instance that sent it. `select()`/`errors()` remain for requests without reply actions and for stream-level composition (see Alternative forms).
SYG508.note:
Fix: Name the reply actions in the request and remove the intent line: `LOAD: { HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/quote', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }) }`, with `LOADED: (state, body) => …` (the parsed body) and `FAILED: (state, { status }) => …` in the model.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG508

SYG509.title: SYG509 (warn): Clock or randomness read from a global in a handler
SYG509.summary: Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A model handler (a STATE reducer, an EFFECT handler, another sink's handler or the payload function of `event()`) calls `Date.now()`, `new Date()` with no arguments, `Math.random()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` (also through `globalThis.`, `window.` or `self.`) directly in its body. The canonical form takes `now()`, `random()` and `uuid()` from the handler's 4th argument (props), which record/replay and `renderComponent` (fixed clock, seeded random, deterministic ids) supply, so replaying the actions gives the same result. Calls in nested functions, views and intents are not reported.
SYG509.note:
Fix: Use the handler's 4th argument: `SAVE: { EFFECT: (state, data, next, { now }) => { localStorage.setItem('savedAt', String(now())) } }`, or `(state, data, next, props) => … props.uuid() …`; `new Date()` becomes `new Date(now())`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG509

SYG510.title: SYG510 (warn): waitForState matched only a state the test had already seen
SYG510.summary: Strict mode only (`renderComponent(C, { strict: true })` or `configureStrict(true)`). `t.waitForState(pred)` searches the recorded history first, so it resolves at once when any earlier state matches. Reported when the only match is a state from before the test's last awaited input (`await t.simulateEvent(...)`, `await t.simulateAction(...)`) and the current state doesn't match: the wait was true in the past and proves nothing about now. A match the current state also satisfies (`count === 0` again after a reset) isn't reported.
SYG510.note:
Fix: Assert the current state, `expect(t.state).toMatchObject({ ... })`, or wait for a new state, `await t.next(pred)`. To wait for a state an input will cause, call `t.next(pred)` before the input, or await the input and read `t.state`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG510

SYG601.title: SYG601 (error): Retired in 6.0: Missing or invalid sources
SYG601.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown when a component made by the `component({ ... })` factory was called by hand without a sources object. Sygnal 6.0 removed the factory and its `sources` option; components are always started by `run()` or `renderComponent()`.
SYG601.note:
Fix: Start the app with `run(App)` (or test it with `renderComponent(App)`). See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#component-factory.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG601

SYG602.title: SYG602 (error): Intent is not a function
SYG602.summary: The component's `.intent` is set but is not a function (for example an object of streams). It is thrown when the component is constructed.
SYG602.note:
Fix: Make intent a function of sources: `Comp.intent = ({ DOM }) => ({ CLICK: DOM.select('.btn').events('click') })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG602

SYG603.title: SYG603 (error): Intent returned an invalid value
SYG603.summary: The intent function returned something other than an object of streams: often `undefined` because an arrow function used a block body without `return`, or a single stream of `{ type, data }` objects (a form Sygnal 6.0 removed; the message names it). It is also thrown when an entry of the object is not a stream. It is thrown when the component is constructed.
SYG603.note:
Fix: Return an object of action streams, e.g. `intent = ({ DOM }) => ({ CLICK: DOM.select('.btn').events('click') })` (note the parentheses around the object).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG603

SYG604.title: SYG604 (error): Retired in 6.0: Invalid hmrActions
SYG604.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown for an `hmrActions` static that was not an action name or an array of them. Sygnal 6.0 removed `hmrActions`: `sygnal/vite` keeps the state across a hot update; a leftover `hmrActions` is reported as SYG612.
SYG604.note:
Fix: Remove `hmrActions`; put an action to run after the swap in the model's `BOOTSTRAP`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#hmractions.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG604

SYG605.title: SYG605 (error): Retired in 6.0: Intent action name contains '|'
SYG605.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. `|` was reserved in action names for the `'ACTION | SINK'` model keys, which Sygnal 6.0 removed.
SYG605.note:
Fix: Nothing to change (a name without `|` stays the clearer choice).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG605

SYG606.title: SYG606 (error): calculated is not an object
SYG606.summary: The component's `.calculated` is set but is not a plain object (for example a function or an array). It is thrown the first time calculated fields are added to an object state.
SYG606.note:
Fix: Define calculated fields as an object: `Comp.calculated = { total: state => state.items.length }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG606

SYG607.title: SYG607 (error): Retired in 6.0: State source not found
SYG607.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown by the low-level `switchable()` helper when the sources had no state source under its `stateSourceName`. Sygnal 6.0 removed the helper and the custom source names: the state source is always `STATE`.
SYG607.note:
Fix: Render `<Switchable>` in a view; remove `stateSourceName`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#source-names.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG607

SYG608.title: SYG608 (warn): Strict mode requested without the diagnostics entry
SYG608.summary: `run(App, drivers, { diagnostics: { strict: true } })` was called but the `sygnal/diagnostics` dev entry is not loaded. The strict (canonical-form) checks live in that entry, so no strict findings are reported; the option still turns diagnostics on. Printed once per page load.
SYG608.note:
Fix: Import the dev entry before `run()` in development (`import 'sygnal/diagnostics'`), or use the Sygnal Vite plugin, which injects it in dev. Do not ship it in production builds.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG608

SYG609.title: SYG609 (warn): Sink or source has no driver
SYG609.summary: A component's model sends to a sink (for example `HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/x' })`), or its intent reads a source (`HTTP.select('x')`), but `run()` got no driver with that name. Values sent to a sink without a driver are dropped silently, and a source without a driver is `undefined`, so the intent then fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined". `renderComponent()` does not report this: in tests it records such sinks (`t.requests(name)`) and fakes such sources (`t.respond` / `t.fail`), so a test suite can pass while the app drops every request.
SYG609.note:
Fix: Pass the driver to `run()` under exactly that name: `run(App, { HTTP: makeFetchDriver() })` for HTTP requests, `run(App, { LLM: makeChatDriver({ transport: openResponses({ baseURL, model }) }) })` (from `sygnal/ai`) for an LLM chat sink, `driverFromAsync(fn)` for any promise-returning function, or your own driver. Check the spelling against the drivers you pass.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG609

SYG610.title: SYG610 (error): Request has a 'then' or 'catch' key
SYG610.summary: A request sent to a driver with reply actions (`makeFetchDriver`, `driverFromAsync`) has a `then` or `catch` key, for example `HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/x', then: 'LOADED' })`. An object with a `then` key is a thenable, so it breaks anything that `await`s it, and these keys look like a promise chain but do nothing. The driver does not send the request.
SYG610.note:
Fix: Name the reply actions with the `ok` / `error` keys: `{ url: '/api/x', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }`. The `ok` action gets the parsed body, the `error` action `{ error, status, body, request }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG610

SYG611.title: SYG611 (error): Socket message not sent or connection not opened
SYG611.summary: A value sent to a `makeSocketDriver()` sink could not be acted on. Either a send (`{ to: 'room', json }`) names a connection that this component instance has not declared, that has closed for good (`reconnect: false`, or a URL the browser rejected), or that is a server-sent events connection, which is read-only. Or a declared connection has neither a `socket` nor an `sse` URL. Or the value is neither `{ connections }` nor `{ to, … }`. Connection names are per component instance: a parent cannot send on a child's connection. The message is dropped; a connection that is only (re)connecting is not an error, its sends are queued.
SYG611.note:
Fix: Declare the connection first, `{ connections: { room: { socket: '/ws/rooms/general', message: 'RECEIVED' } } }`, then send on it from the same component: `{ to: 'room', json: { text } }`. Use a WebSocket (`socket:`) for two-way traffic.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG611

SYG612.title: SYG612 (error): Removed in 6.0
SYG612.summary: A component uses a form that Sygnal 6.0 removed, so it is ignored or fails at run time: a component named by a string tag or registered in `.components`, `<Collection of="Name">`, the Collection's wrapper element (`className`, `style`, `class`, `attrs`, `data` / `data-*`, `on`, `hook` or `ref` on `<Collection>`: the items now render directly into the parent element, so these went to a `<div>` that no longer exists and are ignored), `CHILD.select('Name')`, an `'ACTION | SINK'` model key, `.peers`, `hmrActions`, a view with positional parameters (`function C(props, state)`), `DOMSourceName` / `stateSourceName`, `storeCalculatedInState`, or the…
SYG612.note:
Fix: Follow the linked section of the migration guide (https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6): import components and use them as JSX tags, pass the component function to `of` and `CHILD.select`, put a Collection's class or style on your own wrapping element (`
`), use object-form model entries, destructure the view's one argument, and write function components with statics (or use `defineComponent`). More: sygnal-check explain SYG612

SYG620.title: SYG620 (error): Router command not performed
SYG620.summary: A value sent to the router's sink (`makeRouter().driver`) could not be acted on, so nothing was navigated. Either `{ to }` names no route (or the `'*'` not-found route), or the route's pattern needs a param that `params` leaves out, or the value uses the `route` key, which is reserved for the component's `route` declaration (`App.route = 'ROUTE'`), or it is none of the router's commands. The router reports this in production too.
SYG620.note:
Fix: Navigate with `{ to: 'task', params: { id } }` (plus `query`, `hash`, `replace` as needed), `{ url: router.href(...) }`, `{ back: true }`, `{ forward: true }`, `{ block: 'CONFIRM_LEAVE' }` or `{ prefetch: 'task', params }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG620

SYG630.title: SYG630 (warn): Cached request is not idempotent
SYG630.summary: A request to `makeFetchDriver()` sets `cache: true` or `staleTime` but is not a GET or HEAD (a request with `json` or `body` defaults to POST), for example `{ url: '/api/quotes', method: 'POST', json, cache: true }`. The driver's `queryCache()` keeps its reply by method, URL and body, so a second identical write within `staleTime` is answered from the cache and never reaches the server, and identical writes in flight share one fetch. Writes should always be sent.
SYG630.note:
Fix: Remove `cache` / `staleTime` from the write. To refresh cached reads after it succeeds, tag the reads (`tags: ['quotes']`) and add `invalidates: ['quotes']` to the write.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG630

SYG631.title: SYG631 (error): validate is not a Standard Schema
SYG631.summary: A request or resource to `makeFetchDriver()` has a `validate` value that is not a Standard Schema, an object with a `~standard.validate` function (zod, valibot and arktype schemas are). A plain function or another validator's object does not qualify. The driver cannot validate the reply, so the request fails with a TypeError on its `error` action (or as the resource's error).
SYG631.note:
Fix: Pass the schema object itself: `validate: QuoteSchema` (for zod, `z.object({ ... })`). To check a body with your own function, use `parse: (res) => res.json().then(check)` instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG631

SYG632.title: SYG632 (info): invalidate matched nothing
SYG632.summary: A `{ invalidate }` value sent to `makeFetchDriver()` matched no cache entry and no mounted resource, so nothing was refetched or marked stale. Tags are explicit: `{ invalidate: 'quotes' }` matches only requests with `tags: ['quotes']`; a string starting with '/' is a prefix of the request's `url` as written (without the driver's `baseUrl`); a function is called with each request. This is info: invalidating data that no component shows at the moment is often fine.
SYG632.note:
Fix: Add `tags: ['quotes']` to the resources (or cached requests) the write should refresh, or invalidate by URL prefix: `{ invalidate: '/quotes' }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG632

SYG633.title: SYG633 (warn): abort names a lane the requests do not use
SYG633.summary: `{ abort: 'X' }` cancels this component instance's requests whose key is 'X'; a request's key is its `key`, else its `ok` action, else its `error` action. The instance sends its `ok: 'X'` requests with another `key`, so the abort matches none of them and they still deliver. (G-175.)
SYG633.note:
Fix: Abort by that key: `{ abort: true, key: 'search' }`, or drop `key` from the requests so their lane is the `ok` action.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG633

SYG634.title: SYG634 (info): latest: true with a computed key
SYG634.summary: A request has `latest: true` and a `key` that is not a string literal, for example `key: 'search-' + state.q`. `latest` cancels this instance's earlier requests with the same key, so a key that changes with state gives every value its own lane, and a new request never cancels the previous one: out-of-order replies can still arrive. That is right for independent lanes, such as one save per row, so this is info.
SYG634.note:
Fix: Use a fixed key (`key: 'search'`) or none (the lane is the `ok` action) so the newest request cancels the others. Keep a computed key only for lanes that should run side by side (`// sygnal-ignore SYG634`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG634

SYG635.title: SYG635 (warn): Caching asked for without a queryCache
SYG635.summary: A request or resource sets `cache: true` or `staleTime`, or the component sends `{ prefetch: request }`, but the sink's `makeFetchDriver()` has no query cache. The cache is a separate export, so a driver without `cache: queryCache()` caches nothing: the request is sent as an ordinary one, and a prefetch does nothing. In tests the HTTP fake has no cache unless `renderComponent(C, { http: { cache: queryCache() } })` gives it one.
SYG635.note:
Fix: Give the driver a cache: `makeFetchDriver({ cache: queryCache({ staleTime: 30000 }) })` with `import { queryCache } from 'sygnal'` (in tests, `renderComponent(C, { http: { cache: queryCache() } })`). Or remove `cache` / `staleTime` / the prefetch.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG635

SYG636.title: SYG636 (warn): progress that can't be reported as asked
SYG636.summary: A request sets `progress` (a reply action such as `progress: 'UPLOADING'`, or `true` for `HTTP.progress()`), but the driver can't report it as written. A request with `progress` goes over XMLHttpRequest, the only transport that reports upload progress in every browser, and XMLHttpRequest has no equivalent for some fetch options: `init.keepalive`, `priority`, `cache`, `redirect`, `integrity`, `mode`, `referrer`, `referrerPolicy`, `window` and `duplex` are ignored for that request. `progress` on a resource or on a `batch` request is ignored altogether: those report no progress.
SYG636.note:
Fix: Remove the fetch-only `init` options from the progress request, or drop `progress` if the request needs them. For a resource, send the download as a request with `progress` and reply actions (`{ url, progress: 'DOWNLOADING', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }`); for a batch, send the parts as separate requests.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG636

SYG637.title: SYG637 (warn): refresh on a read another component also declares
SYG637.summary: An action sends `{ refresh: name }` for a resource whose read another component also declares. `refresh` refetches only the sending component's own resources, so the other component keeps showing the old answer until something else refetches it: a header badge stays stale after the page below it refreshes. Nothing fails: the request is sent, the sender updates, and a test of the sender passes. Two reads count as the same when they ask for one literal URL by GET; with a `query`, only when they come from one helper called without arguments.
SYG637.note:
Fix: Send `{ invalidate: value }` on the HTTP sink instead, with a tag both reads carry or their URL: it refetches every mounted copy. A URL is a prefix, so `'/alerts'` also matches `'/alerts/1'`. If only this component's copy should update, add `// sygnal-ignore SYG637`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG637

SYG640.title: SYG640 (warn): Element command target not found
SYG640.summary: A model entry sent an element command on the built-in `ELEMENT` sink, such as `{ focus: Email }` or `{ showModal: HelpDialog }`, and nothing matched its target. The target, a control or a selector, is looked up only in the view of the component instance that sent the command: an element inside a child component is isolated from its parent, and a Collection item reaches only its own elements. The dev entry's message says when a matching element is on the page but outside the sender's view (rendered by an ancestor, a child component or another part of the page).
SYG640.note:
Fix: Render the element in the sending component's view, or send the command from the component that renders it: in a Collection, each item sends its own (for example on BOOTSTRAP for a new row). For an element an ancestor renders (a wizard's footer button focusing the page's name field), hand it off: the child emits `EVENTS: event('NAME_FIRST')` (or sends `PARENT`), the ancestor selects it in its intent (`NAME_FIRST: EVENTS.select('NAME_FIRST')`) and its entry sends `ELEMENT: { focus: '#project-name' }`. For an element inside a child, the parent can send `{ focus: focusWithin('.title') }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG640

SYG641.title: SYG641 (error): Unknown element command
SYG641.summary: An element command (`ELEMENT` sink) names a method that can't run. The first key of a command object is the method and the other keys are its options (`{ scrollIntoView: Row, block: 'nearest' }`). A control whose spec object declares `commands` is asked first; then the element's own method runs (focus, blur, select, click, scrollIntoView, showModal, show, close, showPopover, hidePopover, togglePopover, and others such as play or reset). Reported when neither exists, for example a typo (`fokus`) or `showModal` on an element that isn't a `<dialog>`; the message names the control's declared commands.
SYG641.note:
Fix: Use one of the element's methods or the control's commands, with the method as the first key: `{ focus: Email, preventScroll: true }`, `{ close: HelpDialog, returnValue: 'ok' }`. Render dialogs as `<dialog>` and popovers with `attrs: { popover: 'auto' }`. To change what the page shows, change the state instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG641

SYG642.title: SYG642 (warn): Persisted state could not be restored or saved
SYG642.summary: `persist({ ... })` failed to read, migrate or write the stored state: the stored entry is not JSON (edited by hand, written by something else), `migrate(old, fromVersion)` threw, or the storage refused the write (the quota is full, storage is blocked in a private window or by the browser's settings). The app keeps running: after a failed restore it starts from `initialState`, and after a failed write the change is simply not saved (the next change tries again). It is a warning printed in production too, since a full or blocked storage only shows up on users' machines.
SYG642.note:
Fix: For a restore failure, check the stored entry under the persist key (DevTools > Application > Local Storage) and `migrate()` for that stored version; a corrupt entry is replaced on the next save. For a write failure, save less (`pick` only what must survive a reload) or catch quota errors in a custom `storage` adapter.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG642

SYG643.title: SYG643 (warn): Declaration static with no driver to take it
SYG643.summary: A component declares `timers`, `connections`, `resources` or `browser`, but no registered driver takes that static, so nothing happens and nothing else says so: the timers never fire, the connections never open, the resources stay idle, the browser sources never start. The core sends each of these statics to the source of the driver that asks for it (`makeTimerDriver()`, `makeSocketDriver()`, `makeFetchDriver()`, `makeBrowserDriver()`), and the driver is opt-in: `run()` doesn't register it for you.
SYG643.note:
Fix: Register the driver when you start the app: `run(App, { TIMER: makeTimerDriver() })` for `timers`, `run(App, { WS: makeSocketDriver() })` for `connections`, `run(App, { HTTP: makeFetchDriver() })` for `resources`, `run(App, { BROWSER: makeBrowserDriver() })` for `browser` (the key is yours to choose; the core finds the driver by the static it takes).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG643

SYG644.title: SYG644 (warn): Custom element prop hides an HTMLElement member
SYG644.summary: A `defineElement(tag, Component, { props })` declaration names a prop that is also a member of `HTMLElement`, such as `title`, `hidden`, `lang`, `dir` or `translate`. The element defines its own property for each prop, so the native member of that name stops working on this element: setting `el.hidden = true` updates the prop instead of hiding the element, and the matching attribute no longer has its native effect. `sygnal/element` reports it once per tag when the element first connects, through the diagnostics core when diagnostics are on (a console warning in dev otherwise).
SYG644.note:
Fix: Rename the prop (`heading` instead of `title`, `collapsed` instead of `hidden`) and update the attribute and the component's state key that it feeds. Keep the name only when replacing the native behaviour is what you want.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG644

SYG645.title: SYG645 (warn): viewTransitions that can't run
SYG645.summary: A component declares `viewTransitions` (for example `Board.viewTransitions = ['MOVE']`), but the app's DOM driver can't run View Transitions, so those actions patch the page at once, without the animation, and nothing else says so. The static only asks: the transition is run by the DOM driver from `makeViewTransitionDOMDriver()`, which is opt-in so that apps without View Transitions don't ship it, and `run()`'s default DOM driver is the plain one. Reported once per component when it starts. Not reported under `renderComponent` (the mock DOM and the `dom: 'real'` container don't animate).
SYG645.note:
Fix: Give `run()` the View Transition DOM driver: `run(App, { DOM: makeViewTransitionDOMDriver('#root') })` with `import { makeViewTransitionDOMDriver } from 'sygnal'` (use the same mount point as before). Or remove the `viewTransitions` static. For a value that isn't an array, list the action names in one: `Board.viewTransitions = ['MOVE']`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG645

SYG660.title: SYG660 (error): Widget mount threw
SYG660.summary: A widget's `mount(el, props, dispatch)` threw when its host entered the page (or on the first client patch after server rendering). The widget is not mounted. The error goes to the app's `onError` hook with phase `'widget'`, and the component that renders the widget shows its `onError` fallback in the widget's place on its next render (an empty error `<div>` without one); the rest of its view keeps working. Without the dev entry it is logged as `[Sygnal SYG660]` followed by the error.
SYG660.note:
Fix: Fix `mount()` (a missing library import, an option the library rejects, a prop that is `undefined` on the first render). Give the component that renders the widget an `.onError` to show a custom fallback.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG660

SYG661.title: SYG661 (error): Widget update threw or reported an error
SYG661.summary: A widget failed after it mounted: either its `update(instance, props, el)` threw when the props it was rendered with changed (a widget without `update` is remounted instead, so its `mount()` threw), or the widget reported an error itself through `error(e)`, `mount`'s fourth parameter (a failure in its own timer, callback or redraw, such as a `fromZag` render on a machine-driven update). The dev message says which: `update() threw` or `reported an error through error(e)`. Either way, as for SYG660, the error goes to the app's `onError` hook with phase `'widget'` and the owner's `onError` fallback replaces the widget on its next render.
SYG661.note:
Fix: For a throwing `update`: fix `update()` for every value the view can pass (`null`, an empty list, a value of another type). `update` gets the newest props each time they change (a shallow compare), so it should not keep the props it was first given. For `error(e)`: fix what the widget reports (the error's stack points to its timer or callback), or give the owner an `.onError` for a custom fallback.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG661

SYG662.title: SYG662 (error): Widget unmount threw
SYG662.summary: A widget's `unmount(instance, el)` threw when its host left the page. The host is removed anyway, but what `unmount` didn't finish (listeners on `document`, timers, observers) may keep running. The error goes to the app's `onError` hook with phase `'widget'`; there is no fallback to show, since the widget is gone. Without the dev entry it is logged as `[Sygnal SYG662]` followed by the error.
SYG662.note:
Fix: Fix `unmount()`, for example by guarding a library's `destroy()` that throws when called twice or after its element was removed.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG662

SYG663.title: SYG663 (error): Invalid browser-source spec or command
SYG663.summary: An entry of a component's `browser` static can't be started, or a command sent to the browser driver's sink can't be run, so it is skipped and nothing would happen. A `browser` entry is an object with one key that names its source (`intersection`, `resize`, `media`, `storage`, `visibility`, `online`, `geolocation`) and that names the action its events are delivered as (`action: 'SEEN'`, a string); `intersection` and `resize` take a selector in the component's own view, or `true` for its root element; a `resize` entry's `box`, when given, is `'content-box'`, `'border-box'` or `'device-pixel-content-box'`.
SYG663.note:
Fix: Write the entry as `seen: { intersection: '.cover', action: 'SEEN' }`, `dark: { media: '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', action: 'DARK' }` (a falsy value stops it: `seen: !state.seen && { ... }`), and a command as `COPY: { BROWSER: (state) => ({ copy: state.link, ok: 'COPIED' }) }`. Clipboard reads and writes are commands, not `browser` entries.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG663

SYG664.title: SYG664 (error): Browser source not in the driver
SYG664.summary: A `browser` entry (or a BROWSER command) uses a source that the app's browser driver wasn't made with: `makeBrowserDriverWith(intersectionSource, mediaSource)` takes only the sources it is given, so that the others add no bytes, and an entry of any other kind is not started. `makeBrowserDriver()` has every source.
SYG664.note:
Fix: Add the source to the driver, e.g. `makeBrowserDriverWith(intersectionSource, mediaSource, storageSource)`, or use `makeBrowserDriver()`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG664

SYG665.title: SYG665 (warn): Browser source failed with no error action
SYG665.summary: A browser source or command failed: the user denied the geolocation or clipboard permission, the API isn't available (no `navigator.clipboard` outside a secure context, no `navigator.geolocation`), the position timed out, or storage is blocked or full. Its spec names no `error` action, so the component never hears about it and keeps waiting. Reported once per component, entry and kind of failure.
SYG665.note:
Fix: Name an `error` action and handle it: `here: { geolocation: true, action: 'POS', error: 'GEO_FAILED' }` with `GEO_FAILED: (state, { code, message }) => ...`, or `COPY: { BROWSER: (state) => ({ copy: state.link, ok: 'COPIED', error: 'COPY_FAILED' }) }` with `COPY_FAILED: (state, { name, message }) => ...`. Ask for permission-gated sources from a user action, and say why.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG665

SYG666.title: SYG666 (error): Adapter peer dependency missing
SYG666.summary: A module imports one of Sygnal's adapter entries, but a package that entry needs isn't installed. The adapters keep their libraries as optional peer dependencies, so an app that doesn't use them never installs them: `sygnal/react` needs `react` and `react-dom` (or a `preact/compat` alias), `sygnal/zag` needs `@zag-js/vanilla`, and `sygnal/ui/menu`, `sygnal/ui/select` and `sygnal/ui/combobox` each need `@zag-js/vanilla` and their own machine (`@zag-js/menu`, `@zag-js/select`, `@zag-js/combobox`).
SYG666.note:
Fix: Install what the message lists: `npm install react react-dom` for `sygnal/react`; `npm install @zag-js/vanilla@1.45 @zag-js/menu@1.45` for `sygnal/ui/menu` (likewise `@zag-js/select` for `sygnal/ui/select`, `@zag-js/combobox` for `sygnal/ui/combobox`) (the Zag packages must share one version). For Preact, alias `react`, `react-dom` and `react-dom/client` to `preact/compat` (and `preact/compat/client`) in the bundler config.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG666

SYG667.title: SYG667 (error): Invalid adapter argument
SYG667.summary: `fromZag(zag, render, options)` got a first argument that isn't a Zag machine package (an object with `machine` and `connect`, as `import * as menu from '@zag-js/menu'` gives), or a `render` that isn't a function; or `fromReact(Component, options)` got something that isn't a React component (a function, or an object such as `memo()` or `forwardRef()` returns). It is thrown when the widget is defined, at module load, so the app doesn't start with a widget that can't mount.
SYG667.note:
Fix: Pass the whole machine package and a render function: `fromZag(menu, (api, props) =>
...
, { events: { select: ['onSelect', (d) => d.value] } })` with `import * as menu from '@zag-js/menu'` (not the default import or `menu.machine`). For React, pass the component itself: `fromReact(StarRating, { events: { rate: 'onChange' } })`, not an element (``) or a tag name. More: sygnal-check explain SYG667

SYG668.title: SYG668 (warn): Browser source has no element to observe
SYG668.summary: An `intersection` or `resize` entry of a component's `browser` declaration has nothing to observe, so its action never comes. Either no DOM source reached the browser driver for the instance (the app runs without a DOM driver, or the declaration was sent from outside a component's `browser` static), or, under `renderComponent(C, { dom: 'real' })`, the entry's selector matches no element the component renders (a typo, or an element rendered only later). The `t.browser` fake still sends its initial report, so the test can pass while the real app observes nothing. Reported once per component, entry and reason.
SYG668.note: Fix: Run the app with a DOM driver (`run(App, drivers, { mountPoint })`) and declare the entry in the component's own `browser` static. Use a selector the component's own view renders, or `true` for its root element: `cover: { intersection: '.cover', action: 'SEEN' }` with `` in the view. Declare the entry only while its element exists: `chart: state.open && { resize: '.chart', action: 'SIZE' }`. More: sygnal-check explain SYG668

SYG669.title: SYG669 (warn): Sygnal component inside a fromZag render
SYG669.summary: A `fromZag(zag, render)` widget's `render` returned a Sygnal component (`<Badge />`), a widget tag (`<Icon />`, `<Menu />`), or special JSX (`<Transition>`, `<Portal>`, `<Collection>`, `<Switchable>`, `<Suspense>`, `<ClientOnly>`, `<VirtualCollection>`, `<Slot>`, with or without props). The adapter patches its render into the widget host with a snabbdom patch of its own, outside the component tree, so none of these run there: a component isn't instantiated, a widget doesn't mount, and a marker renders as an unknown element. Only plain elements (with Zag's prop getters spread on them) work inside the render. Reported once per widget.
SYG669.note: Fix: Render plain elements in the `render` function (`{props.text}` instead of ``). Pass data in through the widget's props, and put components, widgets and special JSX around the widget tag in the component's view instead of inside it. More: sygnal-check explain SYG669

SYG670.title: SYG670 (error): Auth header sent from the browser to a hosted endpoint
SYG670.summary: A `sygnal/ai` HTTP transport (`openResponses`, `chatCompletions`, `anthropicMessages`, `uiMessageStream`, `agui`) running in a browser was about to send an auth header (`Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`) to a host that is neither local (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `*.localhost`) nor the page's own origin. A key in browser code ships to everyone who opens the page, who can then spend it. The request is refused before anything is sent: the chat request fails (its `error` action gets the error, or SYG678 logs it) and this message is logged, in production too.
SYG670.note:
Fix: Call the provider from your server and point the transport at that route: an AI SDK route with `uiMessageStream('/api/chat')`, or your own proxy with `openResponses({ baseURL: '/api/llm' })`, so the key stays there. Only for a key the user typed in themselves (a bring-your-own-key tool), pass `dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true` to the transport.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG670

SYG672.title: SYG672 (error): Strict mode without the strict layer
SYG672.summary: A transport (`openResponses`, `chatCompletions`, `anthropicMessages`) was given `strict: true`. Strict mode rewrites every tool schema (and the `output` schema) into the provider's strict subset, and that code is imported separately, as `strictSchemas` from `sygnal/ai`, so apps that don't use strict mode don't carry it (about 1.1 KB gzipped). `strict` takes that import, not a boolean. The transport sends its requests non-strict: the model may produce arguments outside the schemas, and the agent layer and the chat driver still validate every call. Reported in development, once per transport.
SYG672.note:
Fix: Import the strict layer and pass it: `import { openResponses, strictSchemas } from 'sygnal/ai'` and `openResponses({ baseURL, model, strict: strictSchemas })`. Or drop `strict` to send portable schemas.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG672

SYG673.title: SYG673 (warn): Malformed chat stream event
SYG673.summary: A chat transport (the `transport` of `makeChatDriver()`, from `sygnal/ai` or your own) yielded an event the driver can't use: not an object with a string `type`, a `text` or `reasoning` event whose `delta` isn't a string, a `tool-call` with no tool `name`, or a `tool-result` / `tool-error` whose `id` matches no tool call of the reply. The event is skipped and the stream goes on, so the reply may miss text or a tool call. Events of an unknown type are ignored silently, as the Open Responses spec requires; this is only for known types with the wrong shape. Reported for the first five such events per driver, in development.
SYG673.note:
Fix: Fix the transport so it yields `ChatEvent`s (see `sygnal/ai`): `{ type: 'text', delta: 'Hi' }`, `{ type: 'reasoning', delta }`, `{ type: 'tool-call', id, name, input }`, `{ type: 'tool-result', id, output }`, `{ type: 'data', name, data }`, `{ type: 'finish', reason, usage }`. A transport that parses a wire format should map each provider event to one of these and drop the ones it doesn't know.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG673

SYG674.title: SYG674 (info): WebMCP not available
SYG674.summary: `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` found no WebMCP context: no `modelContext` option, and neither `document.modelContext` nor the older `navigator.modelContext` exists. That is the normal case in browsers without WebMCP (Chrome before the origin trial, Firefox, Safari) and on insecure pages, so it is only information: the call does nothing and returns a `stop()` whose `available` is `false`. Chrome 153 exposes WebMCP behind `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing` (`--enable-features=WebMCP`) or an origin trial token.
SYG674.note:
Fix: Nothing to fix. To try it elsewhere, install `@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill` (`installWebMCP()`) before the call, or pass `modelContext`. Use `stop.available` to show or hide UI that depends on an agent.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG674

SYG675.title: SYG675 (info): Tool sent non-strict under strict mode
SYG675.summary: A transport with `strict: strictSchemas` (`openResponses`, `chatCompletions`, `anthropicMessages`) rewrites each tool's input schema (and the `output` schema) into the provider's strict subset, so the model can only produce arguments that match. A schema with no strict form, such as a record (`z.record()`, `additionalProperties` with a schema) or a non-object root, and for Anthropic also a recursive schema, a value of any type, or a schema past Anthropic's per-request limits (20 strict tools, 24 optional and 16 union-typed parameters across the strict schemas), is sent non-strict on its own while the other tools stay strict.
SYG675.note:
Fix: Give the schema a strict form: an object root with named properties instead of a record (for example an array of `{ key, value }` objects). Or accept the non-strict tool: validation still protects the state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG675

SYG676.title: SYG676 (warn): WebMCP registerTool rejected
SYG676.summary: `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` registers each agent tool with `document.modelContext.registerTool()`, which returns a Promise. The browser refused one: most often `InvalidStateError: Duplicate tool name` (another script, a second `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` call on the same page, or a declarative form registered the same name first), or an invalid name or empty description. The rejection is reported, never thrown, and that tool stays unavailable to the agent until its name, description or schema changes. Reported once per tool and registration, in development.
SYG676.note:
Fix: Give each exposure its own `prefix` (`experimentalExposeWebMcp(app, { prefix: 'shop_' })`), rename the clashing `agent` declaration or form `toolname`, and call `stop()` before exposing the same app again.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG676

SYG677.title: SYG677 (warn): Chat request sent from outside a component
SYG677.summary: A request reached `makeChatDriver()` without the sender stamp the core puts on every value a component's model sends. The chat driver answers only with reply actions (`delta`, `tool`, `ok`, `error`) on the component that sent the request, and it has no `select()` stream, so a request from anywhere else (a stream written into the driver's sink by hand, a driver wrapper that rebuilds the request object, a test that calls the driver directly) could never be answered. It is dropped, and nothing is streamed.
SYG677.note:
Fix: Send chat requests from a component's model: `SEND: { LLM: (state) => ({ messages: state.messages, delta: 'DELTA', ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' }) }`. A wrapper around the driver must pass the request object through unchanged (or copy its non-enumerable sender stamp). In tests, use `renderComponent`'s LLM fake (`t.stream('LLM', chunks)`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG677

SYG678.title: SYG678 (error): Chat request failed with no error action
SYG678.summary: A `makeChatDriver()` request failed (the network or the provider returned an error, the transport threw, or the structured `output` was not valid JSON or failed its schema), and the request names no `error` action. The chat driver has no `errors()` stream, so without an `error` action the component never hears of the failure and stays in its streaming state. The driver logs the failure with this code, in production too. A stream that was aborted (`abort`, `latest`, a removed component, the app disposed) is not a failure and is never reported.
SYG678.note:
Fix: Name an `error` action on the request and handle it: `{ messages, delta: 'DELTA', ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' }` with `FAILED: (state, { error, issues }) => ({ ...state, status: 'error', error: error.message })`. In tests, `t.fail('LLM', error)` drives that action.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG678

SYG679.title: SYG679 (error): Invalid chat request
SYG679.summary: A value sent to a `makeChatDriver()` sink is not a request the driver can send: it isn't an object, it has no `messages` array, its `coalesce` is not `'frame'`, `'none'` or a number of milliseconds, or its `output` is not a Standard Schema (an object with `~standard.validate`). The request is not sent, so no reply action follows. Stopping a stream is `{ abort: key }` or `{ abort: true }`, not a request.
SYG679.note:
Fix: Send `{ messages: [...], ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' }` (add `delta: 'DELTA'` to stream, `key` to name the request, `output: schema` for structured output with a Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema), or `{ abort: 'reply' }` to stop one. Return `ABORT` (or nothing) from the model entry when there is nothing to send.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG679

SYG680.title: SYG680 (info): Part is LLM-only under a decision backend
SYG680.summary: A catalog part has a free-text param (`type: 'text'` or `type: 'list'`) that is `required` and has no `default`. A decision model (`compose.decisions()`: TypeSafe Jev, Ollama `nimble`) only chooses among options the app declared; it never writes text, so it can't fill that param. `compose.decisions()` leaves the part out of its questions and never places it: the part is LLM-only. `compose.llm()` still uses it. Free-text params that have a `default` are fine: a decision model keeps the default. Collected once per part (info).
SYG680.note:
Fix: Nothing to fix if the part is meant for LLM backends only. To let a decision model place it, give the param a `default` (`{ type: 'text', default: 'Notes' }`), or turn it into choices: `options: { value: description }` (an enum) or a number with `bins`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG680

SYG681.title: SYG681 (error): Compose backend option problem
SYG681.summary: The `compose` behavior (sygnal/ai) needs a backend, `compose.decisions({ model, … })` or `compose.llm({ model, … })`, and a catalog made by `defineCatalog()`: without them `compose()` throws with this code. `compose.decisions()` made without a `model` is reported in development: its `decide()` requests name no model, which a decision service rejects unless your server route fills it in. `compose.llm()` without a `model` is not reported: the chat transport sends its own default (`openResponses({ model })`, …).
SYG681.note:
Fix: Pass both: `compose(catalog, { backend: compose.decisions({ model: 'jev-latest' }) })`. For `compose.decisions()`, pass the model even when your server picks one, so the request documents it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG681

SYG682.title: SYG682 (warn): Decision model answered outside the criteria
SYG682.summary: A reply to a `compose.decisions()` step answered a choice question with a value that is not one of the question's options (its `criteria`), for example a part id the request never offered or a mistyped option in a proxy or fixture. `compose.decisions()` rebuilds each step's questions from the pending state and checks every answer against them; the bad answer is ignored, as if the question had no answer (a part isn't used, a param keeps its default, a place falls back to the part's first allowed place), and the composition continues.
SYG682.note:
Fix: Check what answers the decision endpoint: a server route that rewrites replies, a model that ignores the criteria, or a test reply written by hand. In tests, build replies with `answers(questions, picks)` (it rejects unknown options) or `composeWith`. If a model keeps answering outside the criteria, report it with the request's questions.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG682

SYG683.title: SYG683 (error): LLM layout invalid after repair
SYG683.summary: `compose.llm()` asks the model for a layout tree with structured output: a JSON Schema built from the catalog (one closed object per part, enum params, record values from state, rows holding parts only, `maxDepth`). Most providers enforce the schema while decoding, but some don't (no strict mode, an unconstrained local model), and a schema can't say everything, so every reply is read leniently (`type` or `name` for `part`, flat params, the list under another key) and repaired: unknown parts dropped, a part used more than its `maxUses`, a bad param value replaced by its default, text cut to its `maxLength`, a row of one unwrapped.
SYG683.note:
Fix: Send the request through a transport that enforces structured output (`openResponses` or `chatCompletions` with `strict: strictSchemas`, Ollama's `format`), lower the temperature, or use a model that follows JSON Schemas. Check that the part ids in the catalog's `examples` exist. The diagnostic's `data` holds the reply and the issues found.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG683

SYG684.title: SYG684 (warn): Client tool shadows an agent tool
SYG684.summary: `chat({ clientTools })` (sygnal/ai) declares tools the app answers itself: their calls stay open (`input-available`) until `'assistant.TOOL_OUTPUT'` answers them, or, for the `ask_user` tool of `chat({ ask })`, until a card's result part answers. Here a client tool has the same name as a tool the agent layer made from an `agent` declaration (`<name>_<action>`), so a request can't send both. The client tool is sent and its calls are the app's to answer; the agent action is not offered to the model. Reported once per name, in development.
SYG684.note:
Fix: Rename the client tool (`clientTools: { pick_date: … }`), or the agent declaration's `name` or the action, so each tool name is unique. `ask_user` is taken when `chat({ ask })` is used.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG684

SYG685.title: SYG685 (warn): Answer for a tool call that is not open
SYG685.summary: `'assistant.TOOL_OUTPUT'` (`{ toolCallId, output }` or `{ toolCallId, errorText }`) or a card's answer (`ANSWER`, from a result part's `compose.answer(props, value)`) arrived for a call that is not waiting for one. Only a client tool call that is still `input-available` in the last assistant message can be answered (an `ask_user` card only while it is open). The call may have been answered already, closed by STOP or by a new message ("not answered: …"), dropped with its message by REGENERATE, or it may be an agent tool call, which the agent layer runs.
SYG685.note:
Fix: Answer only the calls in `openToolCalls(state.assistant)`, with the part's `toolCallId`. Disable the answer controls when the call is no longer open (an answered card renders frozen with `askCard`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG685

SYG686.title: SYG686 (warn): Ask catalog without a result part
SYG686.summary: `chat({ ask: { catalog } })` (sygnal/ai) gives the model the `ask_user` tool: a card is composed from the catalog's parts, and the call waits until a result part (`result: true`) answers it with `compose.answer(props, value)`. This catalog has no part with `result: true`, so no card it can build is answerable: every `ask_user` call stays open until the user presses Stop or sends a new message. Reported once per `chat()` call, also in production.
SYG686.note:
Fix: Mark the parts the user answers with `result: true` (a choice, a picker, a form, a yes/no) and send `compose.answer(props, value)` to PARENT from their model, for example `PICK: { PARENT: (_s, value, _n, props) => compose.answer(props, value) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG686

SYG687.title: SYG687 (warn): LLM reply stopped in a loop or cut short
SYG687.summary: `compose.llm()` stopped reading the model's reply before it ended, and used what came before the stop. A small model asked for a change it can't express (before edits had `wrap`, qwen3:8b met "put the dates and amount in a Trip section" with `add dates top, add amount top, …`) can repeat the same operations without end; every list in the reply's JSON Schema has a `maxItems`, but not every provider enforces it.
SYG687.note:
Fix: Check what the change asked for and what the reply did (`decisions.ops`); rephrasing the change, or sending it as a fresh composition (`{ prompt, fresh: true }`), often helps a small model. Use a transport and model that enforce the schema (Ollama's structured output does, `strict: strictSchemas` on OpenAI), or raise `maxTokens` if a long page was cut. The diagnostic's `data` holds the reply.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG687

SYG690.title: SYG690 (warn): API contract skew
SYG690.summary: `contractFetch()` (sygnal/api) wraps the `fetch` of `makeFetchDriver` and `makeSocketDriver` and watches for the answer `contractSkew()` gives on the server: a 409 `CONTRACT_SKEW` with an `x-contract-skew` header. It means the app sends a contract hash (`contractHash(contract)` in a header, through the client's `headers` option) that differs from the server's: the tab was loaded before a deploy changed the API, so its requests may no longer match the server's inputs or outputs. Each such request fails with `isContractSkew(failure)` true in its `error` action (a resource has `status: 'error'`).
SYG690.note:
Fix: Offer a reload from `onSkew` (`contractFetch({ onSkew: () => showReloadBanner() })`) or from the `error` action (`isContractSkew(failure)`). Deploy the client and the server together, and send the hash of the contract the client was built with.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG690

SYG691.title: SYG691 (warn): Unknown API endpoint
SYG691.summary: A member chain on a client made by `orpcClient(contract)` (sygnal/api) names a procedure or router that the contract doesn't have, such as `api.quotes.lst()` for a contract with `quotes.list`. The client mirrors the contract router: each procedure is an endpoint function, each router an object, so the misspelled name is `undefined`, and calling it throws `TypeError: api.quotes.lst is not a function` when the model entry or resource runs. TypeScript reports this in a typed project; sygnal-check follows the client to its `orpcClient(...)` call and the contract to its object literal, through imports, so plain JavaScript gets it too.
SYG691.note:
Fix: Use the procedure's name as the contract declares it (the message suggests the closest one), or add the procedure to the contract and implement it on the server. For a `*.server` import, import the server function's name, and move a constant or helper the client needs into a shared module that both sides import.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG691

SYG692.title: SYG692 (warn): Sandbox event dropped
SYG692.summary: A sandboxed component (`createSandbox` or `<Sandboxed>` from sygnal/sandbox) sent an `EVENTS` value the page did not accept, so it never reached `onEmit` or the tag's `emit` event. The page accepts only the types declared in `emits`, and only data that passes that type's Standard Schema (zod, valibot, arktype, ...): the guest is untrusted code, so its events are untrusted input, and the host's intent should only ever see validated data. The message says which: a type not declared in `emits` (an inherited name such as `constructor` never counts), invalid data (with the schema's issues), a schema that threw, or no `emits` at all.
SYG692.note:
Fix: Declare the type with a schema for its data, `emits={{ ANSWER: AnswerSchema }}`, or fix the guest so it sends what the schema expects. If the guest should not send that event, nothing needs fixing: dropping it is the protection.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG692

SYG701.title: SYG701 (warn): Click listener on a non-interactive element
SYG701.summary:
The intent listens for clicks (`DOM.click('.card')`, `DOM.select('.card').events('click')`, or a control such as `controls({ Card: 'div' })`) on an element that is not interactive, such as a `
`, ``, `
  • `, `

    ` or ``, and that has no `role` and `tabIndex`. Mouse users can click it, but keyboard users can't focus it and screen readers don't announce it as something to activate, so the action is out of their reach. sygnal-check matches the intent selector against the component's own view;
SYG701.note:
Fix: Render a `<button type="button">` (or declare the control as `'button'`) and style it as needed. If the element must stay a `<div>`, add `role="button" tabIndex={0}` and also handle `DOM.keydown(x)` for Enter and Space. To keep one on purpose, add `// sygnal-ignore SYG701` above the intent line.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG701

SYG702.title: SYG702 (warn): Form field without an accessible label
SYG702.summary: An `<input>` (other than hidden, submit, reset, button or image), `<select>` or `<textarea>` has no accessible name: no `<label>` wraps it, no `<label for>` matches its id, and it has no `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title` or `placeholder`. Screen readers then announce only "edit text" or "combo box". A `placeholder` counts as a last-resort name (as axe does), though a visible label is better. sygnal-check follows the field to the component or helper that renders it and accepts a label around every place it is used; a `uid('x')` id matches a label with the same `uid('x')` call.
SYG702.note:
Fix: Wrap the field: `<label>Email <input type="email" /></label>`, or link them by id: `<label for={uid('email')}>Email</label><input id={uid('email')} />` (`uid` is a view prop). For a field with no visible label, add `aria-label="Search"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG702

SYG703.title: SYG703 (warn): Image without alt text
SYG703.summary: An `` has no `alt` attribute. Screen readers then read out the file name, or skip the image without saying what it shows. `alt=""` is allowed: it marks the image as decorative. Images named another way (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title`) or hidden (`role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden`) are not reported. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
SYG703.note:
Fix: Add `alt="what the image shows"` (for a dynamic image, `alt={item.name}`); for a purely decorative image use `alt=""`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG703

SYG704.title: SYG704 (warn): Link without href used as a button
SYG704.summary: The intent listens for clicks on an `<a>` that has no `href`. Without `href` an `<a>` is not focusable and is announced as plain text, so keyboard and screen-reader users can't trigger the action. sygnal-check matches the intent's click selectors against the component's own view, like SYG701. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
SYG704.note:
Fix: For an action, render `<button type="button">` (styled as a link if needed). For navigation, give the `<a>` a real `href` (with the router, `href={router.href('task', { id })}`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG704

SYG705.title: SYG705 (warn): Button without an accessible name
SYG705.summary: A `
SYG705.note:
Fix: Put text in the button, or for an icon-only button add `aria-label="Close"` and mark the icon `aria-hidden="true"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG705

SYG706.title: SYG706 (warn): Positive tabIndex
SYG706.summary: An element has `tabIndex` greater than 0. Positive values move it ahead of every element with `tabIndex={0}` or none, so the Tab order no longer follows the page, and every other positive value has to be kept in step by hand. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
SYG706.note:
Fix: Use `tabIndex={0}` to make an element focusable in document order, or `tabIndex={-1}` to focus it only from code. Change the order of the markup if the Tab order should change.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG706

SYG707.title: SYG707 (warn): Unknown ARIA attribute or invalid role
SYG707.summary: An element has an `aria-*` attribute that is not in WAI-ARIA (usually a typo such as `aria-lable` or `aria-labeledby`), or a `role` that is not a WAI-ARIA role: a typo, or an abstract role such as `widget` or `section` that authors may not use. Assistive technology ignores both, so the intended label, state or role never reaches users. The lists are WAI-ARIA 1.2 plus the 1.3 additions, and the `doc-*` and `graphics-*` role modules; dynamic role values are not checked. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
SYG707.note:
Fix: Fix the spelling (the message suggests the closest name), or use a concrete role such as `button`, `checkbox`, `tab` or `region`. For your own data, use a `data-*` attribute.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG707

SYG708.title: SYG708 (warn): Label or ARIA reference to an id that is not rendered
SYG708.summary: A `<label for>`, `aria-describedby` or `aria-labelledby` names an id that no element renders, so the label or description is attached to nothing (often a typo, or an id that was renamed on one side only). A literal id may be rendered anywhere in the checked files; a `uid('x')` reference needs an element in the same component with `id={uid('x')}`. When some id in the project is dynamic (`id={props.id}`), literal references are not checked, and dynamic references never are. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
SYG708.note:
Fix: Render the target with the same id, or fix the reference. Inside a component, use `uid('x')` on both sides: `` and `

`. More: sygnal-check explain SYG708

SYG722.title: SYG722 (warn): Menu, Select or Combobox without an accessible name
SYG722.summary: A `<Menu>`, `<Select>` or `<Combobox>` from `sygnal/ui/menu`, `sygnal/ui/select` or `sygnal/ui/combobox` has no `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The part names its control from them (Menu's trigger text is its `label`; Select's trigger and Combobox's input are labelled by the visible `label`, or take `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` directly), so without any of them a screen reader announces an unnamed menu button or combobox. A dynamic value or a spread counts as a name; an empty string doesn't. It is a warning, also under `--strict`;
SYG722.note:
Fix: Give it a visible label: `<Select className="size" label="Size" items={SIZES} />`. When the label is elsewhere on the page, point at it with `aria-labelledby="<its id>"`; for an icon-only Menu trigger, use `aria-label="More actions"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG722

SYG724.title: SYG724 (warn): Sortable handle not keyboard-accessible, or no live region
SYG724.summary: A `sortable` use whose keyboard path or announcements can't work. Keyboard moves start on the handle (the item when there is no `handle` option): sygnal-check finds the elements that match it in the host's view and the views it renders (Collection items, children) and reports one that can't take focus (not a button, field, link with `href` or `summary`, no `tabIndex` or `tabIndex={-1}`, not contenteditable), or a focusable one other than a `<button>` (SYG705 covers those) with no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` / `title` and no content.
SYG724.note: Fix: Render the handle as `

SYG730.title: SYG730 (warn): Action reachable only by hovering
SYG730.summary: An intent action's stream comes only from `mouseenter` / `mouseover` (or `pointerenter` / `pointerover`) listeners, nothing else triggers it (no other DOM event in that stream, no `next()`, reply action, connection, timer or behavior), and its model entry changes the state. Keyboard users never hover and touch screens hover only on a tap, so what it shows (a tooltip, a preview, a menu) or does can't be reached by them. An `agent` declaration doesn't count as a path: it serves agents, not people. Only streams the checker can see in full are judged (DOM listeners with literal event names, xstream operators, callbacks);
SYG730.note:
Fix: Trigger the action from focus too, and close it on blur and Escape as on mouse leave: `SHOW: xs.merge(DOM.mouseenter('.card'), DOM.focusin('.card'))`, `HIDE: xs.merge(DOM.mouseleave('.card'), DOM.focusout('.card'))`; give the element a way to take focus (a `<button>`). For a tooltip, `tooltip()` from `sygnal/ui` handles hover, focus and Escape (`tooltips()` for many triggers on one component, such as glossary terms).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG730

SYG731.title: SYG731 (warn): Toggled state shown only by a class
SYG731.summary: An element that a click listener targets shows an on/off or selected state only through a class that follows the state (`className={{ done: state.done }}`, `className={state.filter === 'done' ? 'selected' : ''}`), while the click's own STATE reducer flips that field (`done: !state.done`) or, for an equality, writes it (`filter: 'done'`). Sighted users see the change; a screen reader announces a plain button.
SYG731.note:
Fix: For an on/off toggle (the reducer flips `!field`), expose the state with the same condition as the class: `<button className={{ done: state.done }} aria-pressed={state.done}>`; `aria-selected` for a tab or listbox option, `aria-expanded` for a disclosure, `aria-checked` with `role="switch"`, `aria-current="page"` for the current link. Or use a native `<input type="checkbox">` with a label. For a change that isn't a toggle, announce it: let the text or `aria-label` follow the same condition, or add `aria-live="polite"` / `role="status"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG731

SYG900.title: SYG900 (warn): A diagnostics check threw
SYG900.summary: A diagnostics check itself crashed: one of the `sygnal/diagnostics` runtime checks threw inside a hook, or a `sygnal-check` rule threw (or a file could not be parsed). The failure is isolated, so the app and the other checks keep running, but that check produced no results for the code involved. This points to a bug in the checker, or (for parse errors) a syntax error in your file.
SYG900.note:
Fix: For a parse error, fix the syntax error in the named file; for a config-file finding, fix or remove the named key (or the JSON syntax); otherwise please report it to Sygnal with the file or component that triggers it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG900

SYG901.title: SYG901 (error): Retired in 6.0: Sub-component sink stream errored
SYG901.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was logged when the stream merging a component's sub-component sinks errored, an internal of the core Sygnal 6.0 replaced. The 6.0 core has no such stream: an error in a child's reducer, view or driver value is reported under that phase's own code (SYG216, SYG406, ...) and the app's `onError` hook.
SYG901.note:
Fix: Nothing to change: errors are reported under their phase's own code (SYG216, SYG406, ...) and the app's `onError` hook.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG901

SYG902.title: SYG902 (error): Retired in 6.0: EFFECT stream errored
SYG902.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was logged when the stream running a component's EFFECT entries errored, an internal of the core Sygnal 6.0 replaced. In 6.0 an EFFECT runs synchronously with its action; a throwing EFFECT is reported as SYG216 (with the `onError` hook) and later actions keep running.
SYG902.note:
Fix: Nothing to change: a throwing EFFECT is reported as SYG216 and the app's `onError` hook, and later actions keep running.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG902

SYG903.title: SYG903 (error): Retired in 6.0: Component factory returned invalid sinks
SYG903.summary: Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown when a component factory (the removed `component()` / `collection()` / `switchable()` helpers, or a hand-written one) returned something other than a sinks object. Sygnal 6.0 instantiates every component from its function; there are no factories.
SYG903.note:
Fix: Nothing to change. Pass component functions to JSX, `of` and `CHILD.select`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG903
