SygnalPluginOptions.api.title: SygnalPluginOptions.api?: { handler?: string; prefix?: string; contracts?: string[]; functions?: boolean | { dir?: string; header?: string;}; }
SygnalPluginOptions.api.summary: sygnal/api (experimental): wire the app's API into the dev server and the client build. - `handler`: a module whose default export is a Fetch handler (Request → Response), served in dev at `prefix` (default '/api'); a production server mounts the same module. - `contracts`: contract modules (oRPC) that client code gets as routes and a build-time contractHash only, without their schemas (not under Vitest; leave a module out to validate replies on the client). - `functions`: function-first `*.server.ts` files under `dir` (default 'src'): replaced in client code by stubs that build the requests; `header` (default 'x-api-functions') carries each file's contract hash.

SygnalPluginOptions.check.title: SygnalPluginOptions.check?: boolean | CheckPluginOptions
SygnalPluginOptions.check.summary: Run sygnal-check (an optional dependency) in dev on startup and after every source change. Findings go to the terminal and the browser console; error-severity findings also to Vite's error overlay. Skipped silently when sygnal-check isn't installed.
SygnalPluginOptions.check.example: sygnal({ diagnostics: { mode: 'error', strict: true }, check: { strict: true } })

SygnalPluginOptions.compile.title: SygnalPluginOptions.compile?: boolean | { views?: boolean; ssr?: boolean; blocks?: boolean; test?: boolean; }
SygnalPluginOptions.compile.summary: Experimental: compile JSX views at build time. Vite 8 only (a no-op with a warning below); files under node_modules are never compiled. `true`: every part that has shipped; an object turns parts off (each defaults to true): - `views`: an HTML element (not a form field, custom element or SVG tag) becomes a direct vnode call, its data made once at module load when its attributes are static. The vnodes are the ones the JSX runtime makes. - `ssr`: in server builds, compiled elements render to HTML strings inside renderToString (the same HTML, no vnode per element). Never under Vitest.

SygnalPluginOptions.devtools.title: SygnalPluginOptions.devtools?: boolean | { redux?: boolean; }
SygnalPluginOptions.devtools.summary: In dev (`vite`, never `vite build` or Vitest), import 'sygnal/devtools' in the same files as the diagnostics snippet. It installs the DevTools bridge (`window.__SYGNAL_DEVTOOLS__`) for the browser extension. Production builds never contain it. false: not injected. `{ redux: true }` also sends the actions and the root's state to the Redux DevTools extension (connectReduxDevtools() from 'sygnal/devtools').

SygnalPluginOptions.diagnostics.title: SygnalPluginOptions.diagnostics?: DiagnosticsPluginOptions | DiagnosticsMode
SygnalPluginOptions.diagnostics.summary: Runtime diagnostics in dev (`vite`, never `vite build`). In every file that imports `run` from 'sygnal' the plugin sets the dev flag and imports 'sygnal/diagnostics' (the runtime checks); the Vike and Astro client entries get the same. 'off' injects none of it (DevTools: see `devtools`). Any other mode than 'warn', or an ignore list, is passed as run()'s `diagnostics` option, unless the run() call sets that option itself.

SygnalPluginOptions.graph.title: SygnalPluginOptions.graph?: boolean
SygnalPluginOptions.graph.summary: Serve the live app graph page at `/__sygnal/graph` on the dev server (requests from this machine with a local Host / Origin only, as `/__sygnal/mcp`), built by sygnal-check and updated on every save; its URL is printed under Vite's. Skipped silently when sygnal-check isn't installed. In dev the component functions also get their static key (non-enumerable, read by inspect() as `key`), and with DevTools on the open app tabs answer the page's "Live data" (mounted components, instance counts, action flashes, state). Dev server only: production builds contain none of it.

SygnalPluginOptions.mcp.title: SygnalPluginOptions.mcp?: boolean | McpPluginOptions
SygnalPluginOptions.mcp.summary: Serve an MCP endpoint at `/__sygnal/mcp` on the dev server (streamable HTTP; requests from this machine with a local Host / Origin only), so a coding agent can read and drive the running apps in the open page: get_state, dispatch, component_tree, recent_actions, get_diagnostics, copy_as_test, agent_tools, apps, tabs, and sygnal-check's check / graph / explain when it is installed. Every run() app of the page is served (`app` picks one). MCP revisions 2026-07-28 (stateless) and 2024-11-05 … 2025-11-25 (initialize); answers are application/json (no SSE stream, no sessions). Dev server only; it also loads 'sygnal/devtools' in the page.

SygnalPluginOptions.nativeGlobalThis.title: SygnalPluginOptions.nativeGlobalThis?: boolean
SygnalPluginOptions.nativeGlobalThis.summary: Resolve xstream's `globalthis` dependency to a tiny stub that returns the native `globalThis`, instead of the npm polyfill and its dependency chain (~4 KB gzip), in dev, build and Vitest (a `resolve.alias`; every dependency's `globalthis` import gets the stub). Not added when your own `resolve.alias` already maps `globalthis`. false: keep the original package.

SygnalPluginOptions.productionMessages.title: SygnalPluginOptions.productionMessages?: "full" | "short"
SygnalPluginOptions.productionMessages.summary: In `vite build` client code, Sygnal's own messages are reduced to the code, the component name and the docs URL, and per-component debug logging (`Component.debug`, `SYGNAL_DEBUG`) is removed. 'full': keep the complete messages and the logging.

SygnalPluginOptions.vitestSetup.title: SygnalPluginOptions.vitestSetup?: boolean
SygnalPluginOptions.vitestSetup.summary: Under Vitest, add the 'sygnal/diagnostics' entry to `test.setupFiles` so tests (e.g. renderComponent) get the runtime checks.

The tag's JSX children are rendered by the app's DOM driver into a container in the host (`[data-widget-children]`), as ordinary elements: components, `<Collection>`, isolation and intents work inside. `sync` gets them; the widget paints them its own way and dispatches DOM events on them. `true`: the container is visually hidden but in the accessibility tree (Enter / Space on a focused child is its `click`; `focus` is told); `'hidden'`: hidden from everything.

WidgetDefinition.commands.title: WidgetDefinition.commands?: Record<string, (instance: I, options: Record<string, any>, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>) => unknown>
WidgetDefinition.commands.summary: Element commands (`ELEMENT: { open: '.due' }` or `{ open: Due }`), called with the instance. A command wins over a native method of the same name (`focus`, `close`, `togglePopover`: it gets the options object). Register the names in `ElementCommandRegistry` to type the commands.

WidgetDefinition.events.title: WidgetDefinition.events?: readonly EV[]
WidgetDefinition.events.summary: The events `dispatch` sends (bubbling CustomEvents on the host; read them with `.detail()`)

WidgetDefinition.fallback.title: WidgetDefinition.fallback?: string | VNode | ((props: P, h: ControlH) => VNode | string)
WidgetDefinition.fallback.summary: What SSR renders inside the host until the client mounts (not for void hosts like `input`)

WidgetDefinition.field.title: WidgetDefinition.field?: true | { event?: NoInfer<EV>; read?(instance: I, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>): any; }
WidgetDefinition.field.summary: The widget is a form field named by its `name` prop (the widget field contract): when it dispatches `event` (default: `value.event`, else `'change'`), its host also fires a bubbling `input` event, which the `form` behavior reads as the field's new value (the event's detail); the focus leaving the host marks the field touched; processForm entries get `read()` (default: the last value dispatched, else the `value` prop). Its own nameless controls' `input` events don't count. `true`: the defaults.

WidgetDefinition.focus.title: WidgetDefinition.focus?: (instance: I, child: Element | null, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>) => void
WidgetDefinition.focus.summary: With `children`: a child got keyboard focus (`null`: none has it); draw a focus ring where it is
WidgetDefinition.focus.example: defineWidget({ children: true, mount, sync(instance, childrenVnode, el), focus(instance, child) })

WidgetDefinition.hostProps.title: WidgetDefinition.hostProps?: readonly string[]
WidgetDefinition.hostProps.summary: More prop names to put on the host element as well

WidgetDefinition.mount.title: WidgetDefinition.mount: (el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>, props: P, dispatch: WidgetDispatch<EV>, error: (e: unknown) => void) => I
WidgetDefinition.mount.summary: Called once the host is in the document (or on the first client patch after SSR) with the props the view passed. Returns the instance that `update`, `unmount` and `commands` get. `error(e)` reports a later failure the widget catches itself (a library's own re-render): it is handled like a throwing `update` (SYG661, the owner's `onError` fallback in its place).
WidgetDefinition.mount.example: defineWidget({ tag, mount(el, props, dispatch), update(instance, props), unmount(instance), events: ['pick'] })

WidgetDefinition.name.summary: A name for diagnostics and inspect() (`'DatePicker'`); the host tag stands in without one

WidgetDefinition.ownProps.title: WidgetDefinition.ownProps?: readonly string[]

WidgetDefinition.sync.title: WidgetDefinition.sync?: (instance: I, children: VNode, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>) => void

WidgetDefinition.sync.example: defineWidget({ children: true, mount, sync(instance, childrenVnode, el), focus(instance, child) })

WidgetDefinition.tag.title: WidgetDefinition.tag?: TAG

WidgetDefinition.tags.title: WidgetDefinition.tags?: readonly string[]
WidgetDefinition.tags.summary: Tags of the widget's children vocabulary that are SVG tags to the JSX pragma (`marker`, `line`, `text`): they become plain elements app-wide (props stay props). Children of a literal `<svg>` in the same template are still SVG.

WidgetDefinition.unmount.title: WidgetDefinition.unmount?: (instance: I, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>) => void
WidgetDefinition.unmount.summary: Called when the host leaves the DOM.
WidgetDefinition.unmount.example: defineWidget({ tag, mount(el, props, dispatch), update(instance, props), unmount(instance), events: ['pick'] })

WidgetDefinition.update.title: WidgetDefinition.update?: (instance: I, props: P, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>) => void
WidgetDefinition.update.summary: Called with the newest props when they change (shallow compare; `style`/`attrs` objects by their entries). Without it, a change remounts.
WidgetDefinition.update.example: defineWidget({ tag, mount(el, props, dispatch), update(instance, props), unmount(instance), events: ['pick'] })

WidgetDefinition.value.title: WidgetDefinition.value?: { write(instance: I, value: any, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>): void; read?(instance: I, el: WidgetElementOf<TAG>): any; equals?(a: any, b: any): boolean; event?: NoInfer<EV>; strict?: boolean; }
WidgetDefinition.value.summary: Experimental (7.2): the widget carries a value both the app and the user change (an editor's text, a camera, a map's viewport). The `value` prop is controlled: `write` is called only when the app changed it to something the widget didn't report itself (no echo loops, no stale writes); the widget reports its own changes with `dispatch(event, value)` (`event` default `'change'`). With `strict` (here, or the `strict` prop), an edit the model didn't take (the prop never moved) is written back after the app's turn. `read` makes the host's `value` the widget's (`.value()` in intents). `update` is not called for `value` alone.

Each entry derives a request from state and (7.2, as every declaration static) the bag, the view's `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`: `(state, { id, context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + (id ?? route.params.id)`; re-run when the state, the context or a prop changes; falsy means idle: `Quote.resources = { quote: (state) => state.id && '/api/quotes/' + state.id }`. `state.quote` is a `Resource`: `{ status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error', data, error, refreshing }`, written by the built-in RESOURCE action (idle until the first request).

WizardStepComp.route.summary: The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.

WizardStepComp.timers.summary: timers derived from state, run by `makeTimerDriver()` (registered: `run(App, { TIMER: makeTimerDriver() })`; renderComponent provides it) and delivered as this instance's own actions: `Stopwatch.timers = (state) => ({ tick: state.running && { every: 100, action: 'TICK' } })`. Diffed by name whenever the result changes structurally: a new name starts, a falsy or removed one stops, a changed spec restarts. `every` is drift-free (data `{ n, t }`), `after` fires once (`{ t }`), `frame` runs every animation frame (`{ t, dt }`). A hidden Switchable page's timers stop unless `background: true`; dispose stops them; nothing runs during SSR.

WizardStepComp.viewTransitions.summary: actions whose state change animates as a View Transition: `Board.viewTransitions = ['MOVE']`, `App.viewTransitions = ['ROUTE']` (the router's reply action) for route changes. The DOM patch that the action's STATE reducer causes runs inside `document.startViewTransition()`, which needs the app's DOM driver from `makeViewTransitionDOMDriver()` (SYG645 in dev otherwise). Patched at once, without a transition, under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and where the browser has no API.
